docs.title: Fleet
docs.text:
Fleet is a lazy expression accumulator with an immutable builder API that specializes in creating CDISC SDTM/ADaM datasets using the well-known Polars library.

  • Performance blazing fast polars API
  • Designed as an AI-first toolkit
  • Seven, the exact number of dependencies
  • Extensible API to match your own standards

docs.title: What is Fleet?
docs.text:
Fleet adds chainable verb pipelines directly onto every Polars DataFrame so you can build standards-compliant CDISC datasets with minimal boilerplate:

import fleet
import polars as pl
from codelists import SEX  # generated by: fleet init ct

# SDTM DM domain from raw data
dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN",  value="DM")
    .hardcode_no_ct("STUDYID", value="MYSTUDY01")
    .assign_no_ct("USUBJID",   source="patient_id")
    .assign_ct("SEX", source="sex_raw",
               ct_codelist=SEX, ct_mapping={"M": "M", "F": "F"})
    .to_frame()
)

# ADaM BDS dataset (ADVS) from SDTM
advs = (
    vs_sdtm.adam
    .source("USUBJID")
    .study_day("ADY", analysis_date="ADT", reference_date="TRTSDT")
    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL")
    .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .to_frame()
)

Nothing runs until you call .to_frame(). All intermediate verbs accumulate into a single Polars with_columns pass — no intermediate allocations.

docs.title: Namespace Extensions
docs.text:
Importing fleet registers two chainable namespaces on every Polars DataFrame:

Namespace Target dataset Description df.sdtm SDTM domains 14 derivation verbs: domain mapping, CT lookup, datetime normalisation df.adam ADaM BDS 22 derivation verbs: study day, baseline, change, flags, BSA, MAP, QTc, LOCF, summary records

ADaM sub-structures and therapeutic-area extensions are nested under df.adam:

Property Target dataset Description df.adam.adsl ADSL 8 patient-level verbs: treatment dates, duration, population flags, age conversion, periods df.adam.occds OCCDS (ADAE, ADCM…) 5 occurrence verbs: first/last date, worst severity df.adam.onco Oncology RECIST response, BOR, filter_pd df.adam.ophtha Ophthalmology ETDRS/LogMAR, study eye df.adam.peds Pediatrics Age derivations, prematurity df.adam.vaccine Vaccine Fever, seroconversion, ADIS AVAL df.adam.metabolic Metabolic Waist ratios, body fat % df.adam.neuro Neuroscience Centiloid, MMSE, CDR-SoB

These mirror the admiral TA packages.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to Fleet are documented here.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• CDISC Library API integration — native client (CDISCClient) for downloading Controlled Terminology directly from the authoritative CDISC Library REST API
  • CDISCClient.get_packages() — list available CT versions (SDTM, ADaM)
  • CDISCClient.get_codelist() — download a single codelist by NCI concept ID with version pinning
  • Credentials via .env file or CDISC_API_KEY environment variable
  • CT Code Generator — CodelistGenerator converts CDISC Library JSON into typed Python constants with IDE auto-completion
  • CodelistGenerator.from_sdtm_ig() — derive codelists from the SDTM IG (source of truth), scoped to requested domains
  • CodelistGenerator.from_concept_ids() — download codelists from an explicit set of NCI concept IDs
  • Generated classes include _concept_id attribute, submission value constants, human-readable aliases (e.g. SEX = C66731), and __all__ for clean imports
  • Optional include_docs flag to inject CDISC definitions into code comments
  • fleet CLI bootstrapping pipeline and standalone commands:
  • fleet init cfg — create study_config.yaml with study metadata, IG versions, domains, and directory structure
  • fleet init define — generate define.yaml pre-populated with standard variables from the CDISC Library IG (SDTM + ADaM)
  • fleet init ct — generate codelists.py from codelist references in the define.yaml files
  • fleet init-ct — standalone bootstrap of codelists.py from the SDTM IG for given domains
  • fleet add-ct — incrementally add domains to an existing codelists.py (preserves existing codelists)
  • fleet define-xml — generate Define-XML 2.1 from a define.yaml specification (with optional HTML preview)
  • Custom Validation Rules — sponsor-specific CDISC rule authoring and validation workflow:
  • fleet add-rule — scaffold a schema-valid rule YAML skeleton (auto-increments ID, uniqueness check across directory)
  • fleet check-rule — validate a rule file (YAML syntax + structure + JSON Schema); exits 1 on error for CI gates
  • custom_rules= parameter on .validate(), ValidationService.validate_sdtm(), and .validate_adam() — load a directory of rules via the engine's -lr flag
  • validation.custom_rules in study_config.yaml — team-wide default rules directory
  • fleet init cfg scaffolds the custom_rules/ directory and field automatically

  • Header comments in generated rule files include CDISC operator reference link and rule type guide

  • assign_ct now accepts codelist classes — pass a generated class (e.g. SEX) instead of a raw NCI string; ct_mapping is optional when raw data already matches CDISC submission values

  • Admiral-parity expansion — new core computations and record-generating verbs:

  • utils.py: bsa() (Body Surface Area, 4 methods), mean_arterial_pressure(), qtc() (Fridericia/Bazett), age_in_years() (unit-aware), extreme_flag() (min/max per group)
  • df.adam: .bsa(), .map(), .qtc() — namespace wrappers for the new computations
  • df.adam: .derive_summary_records() — aggregate by group and append summary rows (mean, sum, min, max, median, count)
  • df.adam: .derive_locf_records() — forward-fill (LOCF) within patient groups
  • df.adam: .derive_param() — pivot source parameters, compute a new AVAL, and append as new records (e.g. BMI from HEIGHT+WEIGHT)
  • df.adam.adsl: .age_years() — unit-aware age conversion (YEARS, MONTHS, WEEKS, DAYS)
  • df.adam.adsl: .derive_period() — create standard Subperiod/Phase variables (APxxSDT, APxxEDT, TRTxxP)
  • Spec-driven support: bsa, map, qtc are available as algorithm values in define.yaml
  • StudyContext.init() — scaffolds a new study workspace (folder tree, study_config.yaml) with full IG/CT/domain configuration; raises StudyConfigError if already initialised
  • DefineScaffolder — queries CDISC Library IG to generate define.yaml pre-populated with standard variables, types, labels, mandatory flags, and codelist references
  • Evolved StudyConfig model with SDTMConfig, ADAMConfig, CTConfig sub-models for IG versions, domains, and CT package
  • MkDocs documentation site with Material theme
  • mike versioned deployment to GitHub Pages
  • Pre-executed example notebook: ADSL pipeline (CDISCPILOT01)
  • llms.txt for LLM-friendly documentation

docs.title: Fleet Validation Strategy
docs.text: Package: fleet-cdisc (import name: fleet)  |  Specification version: 1.0  |  Date: 2026-03-30

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text: Fleet is a Python library that generates CDISC SDTM and ADaM datasets for clinical statistical programming. It is built entirely on Polars through a namespace extension API, and is designed to run inside a sponsor's existing validated Python infrastructure. This document defines Fleet's validation strategy using the risk-based framework established by the R Validation Hub and the software-agnostic regulatory context articulated by the FDA. The strategy is structured around four complementary pillars: standards traceability through the CDISC Library API, cross-language benchmark parity against {admiral}, regulatory-grade validation via the official CDISC Rules Engine (CORE), and automated unit testing with static analysis.

docs.title: 2.1 FDA Position on Statistical Software
docs.text:
The FDA's 2015 Statistical Software Clarifying Statement[^1] explicitly states that the agency does not require nor endorse any specific software for analyzing data from clinical investigations. Sponsors are responsible for ensuring that any software used produces accurate results and for maintaining adequate documentation of that accuracy. This places the validation obligation on the sponsor's qualified infrastructure — of which Fleet is one component — rather than on the software vendor alone.

Implication for Fleet

Fleet does not need to be independently validated by a regulatory body. Sponsors qualify Fleet by demonstrating it produces accurate, traceable, and reproducible CDISC-compliant outputs within their own validated environment.

docs.title: 2.2 R Validation Hub Framework
docs.text:
The R Validation Hub white paper[^2] — co-authored by representatives from AstraZeneca, GSK, Roche/Genentech, Amgen, and other sponsors — establishes a risk-based approach for assessing package accuracy within validated infrastructure. Although written for R, the framework is language-agnostic and is increasingly applied to Python packages used in regulatory submissions. The framework classifies packages into three risk tiers based on:

Risk Factor Description Intended use How directly the package generates submission-ready outputs Consequence of inaccuracy Patient safety risk and regulatory impact if results are wrong Testability Availability of unit tests, cross-validation tools, and independent benchmarks

Fleet addresses all three dimensions, as documented in the qualification summary in §5.

docs.title: Pillar 1 — CDISC Library Traceability
docs.text:
Fleet's fleet init define and fleet init ct CLI commands query the CDISC Library REST API[^3] directly to bootstrap study specifications and controlled terminology. Variable metadata (labels, types, core designations, permitted terms) is sourced from the authoritative CDISC machine-readable IG model — not hard-coded. The resulting define.yaml and codelists.py are committed artefacts that provide full lineage from source variable to CDISC standard.

# Step 1: Pull domain variable metadata from the CDISC Library IG for SDTM 3.4
uv run fleet init define

# Step 2: Generate codelists.py from NCI concept IDs in define.yaml
uv run fleet init ct

This produces codelist classes — for example SEX (C66731), RACE (C74457) — that are used in pipeline code by class name, never raw string ID:

from examples.cdiscpilot01.sdtm.codelists import SEX, RACE

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .assign_ct("SEX",  source="sex",  ct_codelist=SEX)
    .assign_ct("RACE", source="race", ct_codelist=RACE)
    .to_frame()
)

Traceability chain: CDISC Library API → define.yaml → codelists.py → pipeline code → output dataset

Each link is a versioned, reviewable artefact stored alongside the study specification.

docs.title: Pillar 2 — Cross-Language Benchmark: {admiral} Parity
docs.text:
{admiral}[^4] is the Roche/Atorus R package for ADaM derivations; it is the de-facto gold standard in R-based clinical programming and is documented in multiple regulatory submissions. Fleet's test suite contains tests/unit/test_admiral_parity.py — 400+ lines of tests that benchmark Fleet's Python outputs against documented {admiral} algorithm specifications.

Coverage as of v0.1.0:

Test class Algorithms verified TestBSA Dubois-DuBois, Mosteller, Haycock, Gehan-George (4 methods) TestMeanArterialPressure Standard MAP formula TestQTc Bazett, Fridericia (2 methods) TestAgeInYears Day-accurate age in years, months, weeks TestDeriveSummaryRecords Mean aggregation by parameter group (BDS record generation) TestDeriveLOCFRecords Last-observation-carried-forward imputation TestDeriveParam BMI derivation from height/weight TestADSLAgeYears Age derivations on ADSL frame TestADSLDerivePeriod Exposure period flags TestANL01FLAdmiralParity restrict_derivation + derive_var_extreme_flag (last-valid-row ANL01FL pattern)

No R runtime is required. The parity tests work in two ways:

  • Formula transcription — mathematical formulas (BSA, QTc, MAP, age conversion) are transcribed directly from {admiral}'s published R source code. The tests then assert that Fleet's Polars implementation produces numerically identical results for the same inputs, using analytically-derived expected values computed in pure Python from the same formula.
  • Behavioural specification — for higher-level patterns such as ANL01FL flagging, the expected output rows and flag values are transcribed verbatim from {admiral}'s documented examples (the test comments quote the equivalent R code). Fleet's Python implementation is then verified to reproduce that exact output.

This approach means the validation does not depend on an R installation, a specific R version, or rpy2. The published {admiral} specification is the invariant; Fleet's implementation is validated against it.

# Example: ANL01FL last-valid-row parity test
# tests/unit/test_admiral_parity.py — TestANL01FLAdmiralParity
#
# Equivalent admiral R pattern (quoted in test docstring):
#   restrict_derivation(advs, derivation = derive_var_extreme_flag,
#     args = params(by_vars = exprs(USUBJID, PARAMCD),
#                   order = exprs(ADT), new_var = ANL01FL, mode = "last"),
#     filter = !is.na(AVAL))

result = (
    bds_frame.adam
    .flag("ANL01FL", criteria="last", order_by="ADT",
          groups=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"],
          where='~pl.col("AVAL").is_null()')
    .to_frame()
)
# Only the last non-null-AVAL record per group receives "Y"; all others are null
assert result["ANL01FL"].to_list() == [None, "Y", None, "Y", None, "Y"]

docs.title: Pillar 3 — Official CDISC Rules Engine (CORE)
docs.text: Fleet integrates the official CDISC Rules Engine (CORE)[^5] — the open-source validation binary published by CDISC and used by FDA as the reference conformance checker for SDTM and ADaM submissions. Fleet manages the engine lifecycle through its own CLI and wraps it via a Python API.

docs.title: Installation and health check
docs.text:
# Download the managed engine binary for the current platform
uv run fleet install-engine

# Verify engine and supporting dependencies
uv run fleet doctor

fleet doctor outputs a structured status report covering: engine binary presence, engine version, pyreadstat availability for XPT serialisation, and environment variable overrides.

docs.title: Python validation API
docs.text:
from fleet import ValidationService

svc = ValidationService()

# Validate an SDTM domain against SDTMIG 3.4
dm_result = svc.validate_sdtm(dm, domain="DM", version="3.4")
dm_result.print_report()          # console: pass/warn/fail by rule
dm_result.save_html_report("outputs/dm_validation.html")  # archivable HTML

# Validate an ADaM dataset against ADaMIG 1.3
adsl_result = svc.validate_adam(adsl, dataset="ADSL", version="1.3")
assert adsl_result.is_valid

The ValidationResult object exposes .is_valid (bool), .print_report(report_type="summary") (or "full" for expanded details including INFO-level engine noise), and .save_html_report(path) — a styled HTML artefact with rule-level error and warning cards, suitable for archiving as a validation deliverable.

docs.title: Engine discovery order
docs.text:
Fleet resolves the engine path at runtime via a four-tier chain (first match wins):

  1. FLEET_RULES_ENGINE environment variable (.env at project root)
  2. validation.engine_path in study_config.yaml (committable to VCS for team reuse)
  3. Managed install under ~/.fleet/cdisc-rules-engine/core/
  4. Legacy ../cdisc-rules-engine/core.py (development fallback)

docs.title: Pillar 4 — Automated Test Suite and Static Analysis
docs.text:
Fleet maintains a comprehensive automated test suite executed on every change:

uv run pytest                  # unit + integration tests
uv run ruff check              # style and lint (PEP 8, import ordering, type hints)
uv run ruff format --check     # formatting consistency

In addition, all five example scripts in examples/ are treated as integration smoke tests and must execute without error after every feature change:

uv run python examples/full_pipeline_example.py
uv run python examples/cdiscpilot01_inline.py
uv run python examples/cdiscpilot01_spec_driven.py
uv run python examples/adnca_example.py
uv run python examples/tdd_example.py

These scripts exercise the complete derivation pipeline end-to-end — from raw CSV ingestion through SDTM and ADaM derivation to final export — against the CDISCPILOT01 reference study.

docs.title: Pillar 5 — Local Rule Snapshot (fleet init rules)
docs.text:
Fleet's fleet init rules command caches the exact CDISC conformance rules for the IG versions declared in the study's define.yaml files. Rules are fetched from the CDISC Library API, grouped by domain, and written as human-readable YAML into metadata/sdtm/rules/ and metadata/adam/rules/.

# After fleet init define has created define.yaml files:
uv run fleet init rules

Each YAML file records the rule's CORE ID, description, check logic, scope, severity, and regulatory citations. When committed to VCS, these files provide:

  • Version lock: The exact rule definitions in effect when the study was validated, immune to upstream CDISC updates.
  • Audit trail: Reviewers (including regulators) can inspect which rules were applied without re-querying the CDISC Library.
  • Diff visibility: Any change in the rule set between study milestones is visible in version control history.

docs.title: Custom rules
docs.text:
When the standard CDISC CORE rule set does not cover a study-specific requirement, sponsors can author custom rules in the same YAML schema used by the engine.

Fleet provides first-class support for custom rules through:

  • validation.custom_rules in study_config.yaml — sets a team-wide default directory
  • fleet add-rule — scaffolds a schema-valid YAML skeleton with a # TODO Check: block
  • fleet check-rule — validates a rule file (YAML syntax, structure, full JSON Schema)
  • custom_rules= parameter on .validate() — loads rules per-pipeline
# Scaffold a new rule (auto-increments ID)
uv run fleet add-rule --domain AE --description "AESEV required when AESER = Y"

# Validate the rule file before running against datasets
uv run fleet check-rule metadata/custom_rules/FLEET-AE-001.yaml

# Use in pipeline
# .validate("AE", custom_rules="metadata/custom_rules")

Use a company prefix (e.g. ROCHE-AE-001) to avoid collisions with CORE-XXXXXX.

docs.title: 4. Risk Assessment
docs.text:
Applying the R Validation Hub risk-based framework to Fleet:

Dimension Fleet's profile Risk Intended use Generates submission-ready SDTM/ADaM datasets included in regulatory packages High intended-use criticality Consequence of inaccuracy Incorrect derivations could affect safety/efficacy conclusions; however, CORE validation provides an independent runtime check before submission Mitigated by Pillar 3 Testability 400+ admiral parity tests; CDISC Library traceability; CORE conformance checking; smoke test examples; ruff static analysis High testability → lowers residual risk Open source provenance Public GitHub repository; MIT license; full source inspectable by sponsor QA Transparent Dependency surface Polars ≥ 1.0, Pydantic ≥ 2.0, PyYAML, httpx, lxml; all actively maintained, no high-CVE dependencies (check at installation) Low-medium

Overall risk classification: Medium (high criticality, but substantially mitigated by the four pillars above). This places Fleet in the same tier as {admiral}, tern, and other commonly qualified open-source clinical packages.

docs.title: Why Fleet?
docs.text:
Fleet is designed to bridge the gap between modern, high-performance data engineering and the specialized business logic of clinical statistical programming (SDTM and ADaM).

While traditional tools (like SAS or SQL) or general-purpose Python libraries (like Pandas or plain Polars) are capable of building clinical datasets, they often require writing hundreds of lines of boilerplate code to handle common CDISC requirements: merging controlled terminology, calculating study days, deriving baselines, and maintaining traceability.

Fleet solves this by extending Polars with chainable, domain-specific verbs.

docs.title: 1. Simplicity: Intent-Driven Syntax
docs.text:
With Fleet, your code reads like a specification. Instead of writing complex join logic and conditional expressions, you use verbs that exactly match CDISC concepts.

Without Fleet (Manual Polars):

import polars as pl

# Deriving a baseline value requires multiple steps and intermediate variables
# 1. Filter to baseline records
baseline_df = adbd.filter(pl.col("ABLFL") == "Y").select(["USUBJID", "PARAMCD", "AVAL"])
baseline_df = baseline_df.rename({"AVAL": "BASE"})

# 2. Join back to the main dataset
adbd = adbd.join(baseline_df, on=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"], how="left")

# 3. Calculate change from baseline
adbd = adbd.with_columns((pl.col("AVAL") - pl.col("BASE")).alias("CHG"))

With Fleet:

import fleet

# Intent is immediately clear in a single chain
adbd = (
    adbd.adam
    .baseline(flag_col="ABLFL", target_col="AVAL", new_name="BASE")
    .chg(new_name="CHG", from_col="AVAL", base_col="BASE")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: 2. Power: High Performance Lazy Evaluation
docs.text:
Fleet doesn't just wrap Polars; it deeply integrates with its lazy evaluation engine. When you chain Fleet verbs (e.g., .assign_ct(), .study_day()), no computation happens immediately.

Instead, Fleet accumulates your business logic into a single, optimized set of Polars expressions. When you call .to_frame(), Polars executes the entire pipeline in one pass, leveraging multithreading and query optimization.

  • No intermediate DataFrames: Saves memory.
  • Blazing fast: Processes millions of records in milliseconds.
  • Zero overhead: Fleet verbs compile down to native Polars pl.Expr objects.

docs.title: 3. Clarity: Specification-Driven Development
docs.text:
Fleet natively understands the define.yaml specification. You can define your metadata, controlled terminology, and derivation rules in a single, human-readable file.

Fleet can read this YAML to automatically apply derivations, validate data, and generate CDISC-compliant define.xml exports, ensuring your documentation and your code are never out of sync. You can choose to be fully code-driven, fully spec-driven, or a hybrid of both.

docs.title: 4. Flexibility: Built for Extension
docs.text:
Fleet comes with built-in namespaces for core SDTM (df.sdtm), ADaM BDS (df.adam), ADSL (df.adam.adsl), OCCDS (df.adam.occds), and specialized therapeutic areas (Oncology, Ophthalmology, Vaccines, etc.). Fleet also includes verbs for Body Surface Area (bsa), Mean Arterial Pressure (map), corrected QT (qtc), LOCF imputation, summary record derivation, and parameter-level record generation.

If you have proprietary study requirements, Fleet is designed to be easily extended with custom verbs using standard Polars expressions via the .derivation() method, or by subclassing the namespaces to add your own company-specific logic.

docs.title: 5. AI-Native Architecture
docs.text:
Fleet was built with AI code generation in mind from day one. You can stop wrestling with niche SAS macros or fragmented statistical R packages that trip up modern Large Language Models (LLMs).

  • Standardised Foundation: Built entirely on Python and Polars, two of the most widely represented tools in LLM training data.
  • Unified Package: No need to juggle 10 different sub-packages. One import (import fleet) gives agents everything they need.
  • Clear Intent-Driven API: Because derivations are simple verbs (.study_day(), .baseline()), an AI code agent naturally scripts correct, readable pipelines with fewer token hallucinations.
  • Tight AI Feedback Loops: Fleet drastically accelerates the developer and agent feedback cycle. The define.yaml structure is validated through bundled JSON schemas, and CDISC core data validations output structured error arrays. This allows coding agents to course-correct immediately.
  • Readable Specs: The declarative, YAML-based approach limits token overhead and naturally reflects clinical data specification standards, making it the perfect bridge between LLMs and regulatory outputs.
  • Built-in llms.txt: Fleet natively provides structured AI context (like llms.txt and schemas) so your coding agents always know precisely how to write and validate Fleet pipelines.

docs.title: 6. Native CDISC Library Integration
docs.text:
Fleet is the first open-source clinical toolkit with built-in CDISC Library API support. Instead of manually downloading PDF terminology files or maintaining hand-curated codelist dictionaries, Fleet connects directly to the authoritative source.

# Full bootstrapping pipeline: config → define.yaml → codelists.py
fleet init cfg --study-id STUDY01 --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --adam-datasets ADSL,ADVS
fleet init define
fleet init ct

# Or standalone: bootstrap codelists directly from the SDTM IG
fleet init-ct --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --output codelists.py
  • Source of truth is the CDISC Library IG — Fleet queries the Implementation Guide model to discover every variable and codelist for your domains. No manual curation, no guessing concept IDs.
  • IDE auto-completion for CT values — the generated codelists.py gives you typed constants (SEX.M, RACE.WHITE) with full definitions as code comments. Your IDE autocompletes both the codelist name and every permitted submission value.
  • Incremental domain expansion — start with DM and AE, then fleet add-ct --domains LB,CM later. Existing codelists are preserved; only new ones are added.
  • Version-pinned reproducibility — pin your CT package version (e.g. --package sdtmct-2025-09-26) so every team member and CI run generates identical constants.
from codelists import SEX, RACE

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .assign_ct("SEX", source="sex", ct_codelist=SEX)
    .assign_ct("RACE", source="race", ct_codelist=RACE)
    .to_frame()
)

No NCI codes to memorise. No CSV lookups at runtime. Just import the codelist and use it — the _concept_id is carried through for Define-XML generation and P21 validation automatically.

docs.text:
Importing fleet registers two core namespace extensions on every polars.DataFrame. All ADaM sub-structures and TA extensions are accessed as nested properties of df.adam:

import fleet  # registers df.sdtm, df.adam, df.tlg
import polars as pl

pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).sdtm  # SDTM verbs
pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).adam  # ADaM BDS verbs
pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).adam.adsl  # ADSL verbs
pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).adam.occds  # OCCDS verbs
pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).adam.onco  # TA extensions via df.adam.<ta>
pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).adam.pk  # PK (pharmacokinetics) verbs
pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).tlg.ae  # AE summary tables and listings
pl.DataFrame({"x": [1]}).tlg.vs  # Vital-signs summary tables

docs.text:
Bases: SharedADaMVerbsMixin

Immutable pipeline builder for ADaM derivations.

Each verb appends to a lazy expression list; to_frame() materialises everything in one with_columns call (unless the verb requires a join/filter).

Inherits shared verbs from SharedADaMVerbsMixin: source, derivation, assigned, recode, rename, condderivation, whereclauses.

Source code in src/fleet/adam/namespace.py 
@pl.api.register_dataframe_namespace("adam")
class AdamNamespace(SharedADaMVerbsMixin):
    """
    Immutable pipeline builder for ADaM derivations.

    Each verb appends to a lazy expression list; ``to_frame()`` materialises
    everything in one ``with_columns`` call (unless the verb requires a join/filter).

    Inherits shared verbs from ``SharedADaMVerbsMixin``:
    ``source``, ``derivation``, ``assigned``, ``recode``, ``rename``,
    ``condderivation``, ``whereclauses``.
    """

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 7. lookup — merge/join with subset conditions                       #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def lookup(
        self,
        target_cols: list[str] | None = None,
        *,
        dataset: pl.DataFrame,
        on: str | list[str],
        how: str = "left",
        where: str | None = None,
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """SQL-style join against a lookup *dataset*.

        Optionally filters *dataset* with *where* before the join.
        Materialises the current pipeline then returns a fresh namespace.

        Args:
            target_cols: Optional columns to keep from the joined result.
            dataset: The lookup ``pl.DataFrame`` to join.
            on: Key column name(s) for the join.
            how: Join strategy (default ``"left"``).
            where: Optional filter expression applied to *dataset* before
                the join.

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: A fresh namespace wrapping the joined frame.

        Examples:
            Join a parameter-code lookup table on ``VSTESTCD``::

                advs = (
                    vs_df.adam
                    .lookup(
                        dataset=paramcd_lookup,
                        on="VSTESTCD",
                        how="left",
                    )
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        from ..sdtm.utils import parse_expression

        lookup_df = dataset
        if where:
            filter_expr = parse_expression(where)
            lookup_df = dataset.filter(filter_expr)

        joined = self.to_frame().join(lookup_df, on=on, how=how)
        ns = self._materialise_then(joined)
        if target_cols:
            ns._pipeline = [pl.col(c) for c in target_cols]
        return ns

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 9.  baseline — propagate baseline value to all group records        #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def baseline(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        aval: str = "AVAL",
        baseline_flag: str = "ABLFL",
        groups: list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """Derive BASE as the AVAL where the baseline flag equals ``"Y"``.

        Uses a window function so all records in the same group receive the
        same baseline value.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (e.g. ``"BASE"``).
            aval: Analysis value column (default ``"AVAL"``).
            baseline_flag: Flag column indicating the baseline record.
            groups: Partition columns (default ``["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"]``).

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Propagate baseline AVAL to all records::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL",
                              groups=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._chain(
            baseline(aval=aval, baseline_flag_col=baseline_flag, group_by=groups, target=target)
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 10. chg — change from baseline                                      #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def chg(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        aval: str = "AVAL",
        base: str = "BASE",
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """Compute change from baseline: ``CHG = AVAL - BASE``.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (e.g. ``"CHG"``).
            aval: Analysis value column.
            base: Baseline value column.

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Derive CHG from AVAL and BASE::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._chain(chg(aval=aval, base=base, target=target))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 11. pchg — percent change from baseline                             #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def pchg(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        aval: str = "AVAL",
        base: str = "BASE",
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """Compute percent change from baseline.

        ``PCHG = (AVAL - BASE) / BASE * 100``.  Returns null when BASE is
        null or zero.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (e.g. ``"PCHG"``).
            aval: Analysis value column.
            base: Baseline value column.

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Derive PCHG from AVAL and BASE::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .pchg("PCHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._chain(pchg(aval=aval, base=base, target=target))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 13. bmi — Body Mass Index                                            #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def bmi(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        weight: str,
        height: str,
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """Derive Body Mass Index: ``weight_kg / (height_cm / 100) ** 2``.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column.
            weight: Column containing weight in kg.
            height: Column containing height in cm.

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Compute BMI from weight and height::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .bmi("BMI", weight="WEIGHT", height="HEIGHT")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._chain(_bmi_expr(weight=weight, height=height, target=target))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 14. nrind — normal range indicator                                   #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def nrind(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        value: str,
        low: str,
        high: str,
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """Categorise *value* relative to normal range: LOW / NORMAL / HIGH.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (e.g. ``"NRIND"``).
            value: Column containing the numeric result.
            low: Column containing the lower limit of normal.
            high: Column containing the upper limit of normal.

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Derive normal range indicator for lab results::

                adlb = (
                    lb_raw.adam
                    .nrind("NRIND", value="LBSTRESN",
                           low="LBSTNRLO", high="LBSTNRHI")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._chain(_nrind_expr(value=value, low=low, high=high, target=target))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 15. on_treatment — derive ONTRTFL                                    #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def on_treatment(
        self,
        target: str = "ONTRTFL",
        *,
        adt: str,
        trtsdt: str,
        trtedt: str,
        open_ended: bool = True,
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """Set *target* to ``"Y"`` when *adt* is within [trtsdt, trtedt].

        When *open_ended* is ``True`` (default) and *trtedt* is null, the
        interval is treated as ongoing (``adt >= trtsdt`` suffices).

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (default ``"ONTRTFL"``).
            adt: Analysis date column.
            trtsdt: Treatment start date column.
            trtedt: Treatment end date column.
            open_ended: Treat null *trtedt* as open-ended (default ``True``).

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Derive on-treatment flag::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .on_treatment("ONTRTFL", adt="ADT",
                                  trtsdt="TRTSDT", trtedt="TRTEDT")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._chain(
            _on_treatment_expr(
                adt=adt,
                trtsdt=trtsdt,
                trtedt=trtedt,
                target=target,
                open_ended=open_ended,
            )
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 16. shift — baseline-to-post categorical shift string               #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def shift(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        baseline_cat: str,
        post_cat: str,
        sep: str = " to ",
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """Derive a categorical shift label: ``"<baseline><sep><post>"``.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (e.g. ``"SHIFT1"``).
            baseline_cat: Column with baseline category (e.g. ``"BNRIND"``).
            post_cat: Column with post-baseline category (e.g. ``"NRIND"``).
            sep: Separator string (default ``" to "``).

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Create a shift variable from baseline and post normal range::

                adlb = (
                    lb_raw.adam
                    .shift("SHIFT1", baseline_cat="BNRIND",
                           post_cat="NRIND")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._chain(
            _shift_expr(baseline_cat=baseline_cat, post_cat=post_cat, target=target, sep=sep)
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 17. bsa — Body Surface Area                                          #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def bsa(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        weight: str,
        height: str,
        method: str = "Mosteller",
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """Derive Body Surface Area in m².

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column.
            weight: Column containing weight in kg.
            height: Column containing height in cm.
            method: Formula to use — ``"Mosteller"`` (default), ``"DuBois"``,
                ``"Haycock"``, or ``"Gehan-George"``.

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Compute BSA using the Mosteller formula::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .bsa("BSA", weight="WEIGHT", height="HEIGHT")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._chain(_bsa_expr(weight=weight, height=height, method=method, target=target))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 18. map — Mean Arterial Pressure                                     #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def map(
        self,
        target: str = "MAP",
        *,
        systolic: str = "SYSBP",
        diastolic: str = "DIABP",
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """Derive Mean Arterial Pressure: ``DBP + (SBP - DBP) / 3``.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (default ``"MAP"``).
            systolic: Systolic blood pressure column.
            diastolic: Diastolic blood pressure column.

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Compute MAP from blood pressure columns::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .map("MAP", systolic="SYSBP", diastolic="DIABP")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._chain(_map_expr(systolic=systolic, diastolic=diastolic, target=target))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 19. qtc — Corrected QT interval                                      #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def qtc(
        self,
        target: str = "QTC",
        *,
        qt: str = "QT",
        rr: str = "RR",
        method: str = "Fridericia",
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """Derive corrected QT interval.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (default ``"QTC"``).
            qt: QT interval column.
            rr: RR interval column.
            method: Correction formula — ``"Fridericia"`` (default) or
                ``"Bazett"``.

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Derive QTcF from QT and RR::

                adeg = (
                    eg_raw.adam
                    .qtc("QTCF", qt="QT", rr="RR", method="Fridericia")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._chain(_qtc_expr(qt=qt, rr=rr, method=method, target=target))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 20. derive_summary_records — aggregate and append new rows          #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def derive_summary_records(
        self,
        *,
        by_vars: list[str],
        analysis_var: str = "AVAL",
        set_values_to: dict[str, Any],
        stat: str = "mean",
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """
        Compute a summary statistic per group and append the results as new records.

        *set_values_to*: column → value mapping applied to every new record
        (e.g. ``{"PARAMCD": "AVGBP", "DTYPE": "AVERAGE"}``).

        *stat*: ``"mean"`` (default), ``"sum"``, ``"min"``, ``"max"``, ``"median"``,
        ``"count"``.

        Materialises the current pipeline before concatenation.

        Examples:
            Compute mean AVAL per subject and parameter::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .derive_summary_records(
                        by_vars=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"],
                        analysis_var="AVAL",
                        set_values_to={"DTYPE": "AVERAGE"},
                        stat="mean",
                    )
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        stat_lower = stat.lower()
        agg_map = {
            "mean": pl.col(analysis_var).mean(),
            "sum": pl.col(analysis_var).sum(),
            "min": pl.col(analysis_var).min(),
            "max": pl.col(analysis_var).max(),
            "median": pl.col(analysis_var).median(),
            "count": pl.col(analysis_var).count().cast(pl.Float64),
        }
        if stat_lower not in agg_map:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown stat '{stat}'. Supported: {', '.join(agg_map)}.")

        df = self.to_frame()
        summary = df.group_by(by_vars).agg(agg_map[stat_lower].alias(analysis_var))

        # Apply constant values to the summary rows
        for col_name, col_val in set_values_to.items():
            summary = summary.with_columns(pl.lit(col_val).alias(col_name))

        # Align schemas before concat: add missing columns as null in both directions
        for c in df.columns:
            if c not in summary.columns:
                summary = summary.with_columns(pl.lit(None).cast(df.schema[c]).alias(c))
        for c in summary.columns:
            if c not in df.columns:
                df = df.with_columns(pl.lit(None).cast(summary.schema[c]).alias(c))

        col_order = df.columns
        summary = summary.select(col_order)

        combined = pl.concat([df, summary], how="vertical_relaxed")
        return self._materialise_then(combined)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 21. derive_locf_records — last observation carried forward          #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def derive_locf_records(
        self,
        *,
        by_vars: list[str] | None = None,
        analysis_var: str = "AVAL",
        order_by: str = "ADT",
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """
        Forward-fill *analysis_var* within each group (LOCF).

        Sorts by *order_by* within each group defined by *by_vars*,
        then forward-fills null values in *analysis_var*.

        Materialises the current pipeline, applies the fill, and returns.

        Examples:
            Forward-fill AVAL within each subject / parameter::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .derive_locf_records(
                        by_vars=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"],
                        analysis_var="AVAL",
                        order_by="ADT",
                    )
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        grps = by_vars or ["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"]
        df = self.to_frame()
        df = df.sort(grps + [order_by])
        df = df.with_columns(pl.col(analysis_var).forward_fill().over(grps).alias(analysis_var))
        return self._materialise_then(df)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 22. derive_param — append a computed parameter as new records        #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def derive_param(
        self,
        *,
        by_vars: list[str] | None = None,
        set_values_to: dict[str, Any],
        parameter_filter: dict[str, str],
        analysis_value: pl.Expr,
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """
        Derive a new parameter (e.g. BMI) from existing records and append
        the computed rows to the dataset.

        *parameter_filter*: ``{PARAMCD: value}`` pairs identifying the source
        records to pivot on (e.g. ``{"WEIGHT": "WEIGHT", "HEIGHT": "HEIGHT"}``).
        Each key is a local alias; the value is the ``PARAMCD`` it matches.

        *analysis_value*: a Polars expression referencing the aliases to
        compute the new AVAL (e.g. ``pl.col("WEIGHT") / (pl.col("HEIGHT")/100)**2``).

        *set_values_to*: constant columns on the new rows
        (e.g. ``{"PARAMCD": "BMI", "PARAM": "Body Mass Index"}``).

        Materialises the pipeline before appending.

        Examples:
            Derive BMI as a new PARAMCD from WEIGHT and HEIGHT::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .derive_param(
                        by_vars=["USUBJID", "ADT"],
                        set_values_to={"PARAMCD": "BMI",
                                       "PARAM": "Body Mass Index"},
                        parameter_filter={"WEIGHT": "WEIGHT",
                                          "HEIGHT": "HEIGHT"},
                        analysis_value=(
                            pl.col("WEIGHT") / (pl.col("HEIGHT") / 100) ** 2
                        ),
                    )
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        grps = by_vars or ["USUBJID"]
        df = self.to_frame()

        # Pivot: for each alias in parameter_filter, get AVAL as that alias
        pivoted_parts = []
        for alias, paramcd_val in parameter_filter.items():
            part = df.filter(pl.col("PARAMCD") == paramcd_val).select(
                grps + [pl.col("AVAL").alias(alias)]
            )
            pivoted_parts.append(part)

        # Join all pivoted parts on the by_vars
        joined = pivoted_parts[0]
        for part in pivoted_parts[1:]:
            joined = joined.join(part, on=grps, how="inner")

        # Compute the new AVAL
        new_rows = joined.with_columns(analysis_value.alias("AVAL")).select(grps + ["AVAL"])

        # Apply set_values_to constants
        for col_name, col_val in set_values_to.items():
            new_rows = new_rows.with_columns(pl.lit(col_val).alias(col_name))

        # Align schemas and concat
        for c in df.columns:
            if c not in new_rows.columns:
                new_rows = new_rows.with_columns(pl.lit(None).cast(df.schema[c]).alias(c))
        new_rows = new_rows.select(df.columns)

        combined = pl.concat([df, new_rows], how="vertical_relaxed")
        return self._materialise_then(combined)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Private: YAML spec dispatcher for algorithm: std_function           #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def _std_function_dispatch(
        self,
        target: str,
        func: str,
        *,
        analysis_date: str | None = None,
        reference_date: str | None = None,
        aval: str = "AVAL",
        base: str = "BASE",
        weight: str | None = None,
        height: str | None = None,
        systolic: str | None = None,
        diastolic: str | None = None,
        qt: str | None = None,
        rr: str | None = None,
        method: str | None = None,
        baseline_flag: str = "ABLFL",
        baseline_criteria: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
        groups: list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """Route YAML ``algorithm: std_function`` entries to the appropriate typed method."""
        func = func.lower()
        if func == "study_day":
            if not analysis_date or not reference_date:
                raise ValueError("study_day requires analysis_date and reference_date.")
            return self.duration(target, start=reference_date, end=analysis_date)
        elif func == "baseline":
            return self.baseline(target, aval=aval, baseline_flag=baseline_flag, groups=groups)
        elif func == "chg":
            return self.chg(target, aval=aval, base=base)
        elif func == "pchg":
            return self.pchg(target, aval=aval, base=base)
        elif func in ("flag_baseline", "flag"):
            if baseline_criteria is None:
                raise ValueError("flag requires baseline_criteria.")
            return self.flag(target, criteria=baseline_criteria, groups=groups)
        elif func == "bmi":
            if not weight or not height:
                raise ValueError("bmi requires weight and height.")
            return self.bmi(target, weight=weight, height=height)
        elif func == "bsa":
            if not weight or not height:
                raise ValueError("bsa requires weight and height.")
            return self.bsa(target, weight=weight, height=height, method=method or "Mosteller")
        elif func in ("map", "mean_arterial_pressure"):
            if not systolic or not diastolic:
                raise ValueError("map requires systolic and diastolic.")
            return self.map(target, systolic=systolic, diastolic=diastolic)
        elif func == "qtc":
            if not qt or not rr:
                raise ValueError("qtc requires qt and rr.")
            return self.qtc(target, qt=qt, rr=rr, method=method or "Fridericia")
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unknown func='{func}'. "
                "Valid: study_day, baseline, chg, pchg, flag, flag_baseline, "
                "bmi, bsa, map, qtc."
            )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 17. atoxgr — toxicity grading via criteria files                     #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def atoxgr(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        system: str = "ctcae_v5",
        direction: str,
        term_var: str,
        unit_var: str | None = None,
        signif_dig: int = 5,
        indicators: dict[str, list[str]] | None = None,
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """Derive a toxicity grade column using a criteria-file grading system.

        Materialises the pipeline, applies the grading engine for every
        matching lab term, and returns a fresh namespace with *target*
        appended.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output grade column (e.g. ``"ATOXGRL"``).
            system: Grading system name (e.g. ``"ctcae_v5"``, ``"daids"``)
                or path to a custom JSON criteria file.
            direction: ``"L"`` (low) or ``"H"`` (high).
            term_var: Column holding the lab-test / term name.
            unit_var: Optional column holding the unit of measure.
            signif_dig: Significant figures for comparison (default 5).
            indicators: Optional indicator parameter map for branch
                conditions (e.g. ``{"H": ["HIGH"], "L": ["LOW"]}``).

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: A fresh namespace wrapping the graded frame.

        Examples:
            Grade low-direction anemia using CTCAE v5::

                adlb = (
                    lb_raw.adam
                    .atoxgr("ATOXGRL", system="ctcae_v5",
                            direction="L", term_var="PARAMCD",
                            unit_var="AVALU")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        from .grading._compiler import grade_dataset
        from .grading._registry import load_criteria

        criteria = load_criteria(system)
        df = self.to_frame()
        # Provide standard BNRIND defaults when no indicators are given.
        if indicators is None:
            indicators = {
                "high_indicator": ["HIGH", "H"],
                "low_indicator": ["LOW", "L"],
            }
        graded = grade_dataset(
            df,
            criteria,
            target=target,
            direction=direction,
            term_var=term_var,
            unit_var=unit_var,
            signif_dig=signif_dig,
            indicators=indicators,
        )
        return self._materialise_then(graded)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 18. combine_grades — merge low/high toxicity grades                  #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def combine_grades(
        self,
        target: str = "ATOXGR",
        *,
        low_var: str = "ATOXGRL",
        high_var: str = "ATOXGRH",
        low_desc_var: str | None = None,
        high_desc_var: str | None = None,
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """Combine low and high toxicity grades into a signed grade.

        Low grades are prefixed with ``"-"``; high grades are kept as-is.
        Both null → null.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (default ``"ATOXGR"``).
            low_var: Low-direction grade column (default ``"ATOXGRL"``).
            high_var: High-direction grade column (default ``"ATOXGRH"``).
            low_desc_var: Optional low-grade term description column.
            high_desc_var: Optional high-grade term description column.

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Combine low/high grades into ATOXGR::

                adlb = (
                    lb_raw.adam
                    .atoxgr("ATOXGRL", system="ctcae_v5",
                            direction="L", term_var="PARAMCD")
                    .atoxgr("ATOXGRH", system="ctcae_v5",
                            direction="H", term_var="PARAMCD")
                    .combine_grades("ATOXGR")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        from .grading._compiler import combine_grades_expr

        return self._chain(
            combine_grades_expr(
                low_var,
                high_var,
                low_desc_var=low_desc_var,
                high_desc_var=high_desc_var,
            ).alias(target)
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # 19. transform — arbitrary DataFrame → DataFrame function            #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def transform(
        self,
        fn: str | Callable[[pl.DataFrame], pl.DataFrame],
        *,
        label: str | None = None,  # noqa: ARG002  — cosmetic, intentionally unused
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """
        Apply an arbitrary ``(pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame`` function.

        The pending expression pipeline is materialised before the function
        is called, so the function always receives a fully committed frame.

        Args:
            fn: Either a callable directly, or the registered name of a
                transform (see :func:`fleet.adam.transforms.register_transform`).
            label: Optional cosmetic label for documentation/lineage; has no
                effect on the output.

        Raises:
            KeyError: If *fn* is a string that has not been registered.
            TypeError: If *fn* is neither a callable nor a string, or if the
                function does not return a ``pl.DataFrame``.

        Returns:
            AdamNamespace: A fresh namespace wrapping the transformed frame.

        Examples:
            Register and apply a custom age-group transform::

                from fleet.adam.transforms import register_transform

                @register_transform("add_agegr1")
                def add_agegr1(df):
                    return df.with_columns(
                        pl.when(pl.col("AGE") < 65).then(pl.lit("<65"))
                          .otherwise(pl.lit(">=65")).alias("AGEGR1")
                    )

                adsl = (
                    dm_raw.adam
                    .assigned("STUDYID", value="S01")
                    .transform("add_agegr1")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        from .transforms import get_transform

        if isinstance(fn, str):
            fn = get_transform(fn)  # raises KeyError if not found
        elif not callable(fn):
            raise TypeError(
                f"transform() expects a callable or a registered name string, "
                f"got {type(fn).__name__!r}."
            )

        # Materialise pending expressions so the function sees a full frame.
        committed = self.to_frame()
        result = fn(committed)

        if not isinstance(result, pl.DataFrame):
            raise TypeError(
                f"Transform function must return a polars DataFrame, got {type(result).__name__!r}."
            )

        return self._materialise_then(result)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Spec-driven pipeline                                                 #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def from_spec(
        self,
        spec_path: str | Path,
        *,
        dataset: str | None = None,
        only: list[str] | None = None,
        omit: list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> AdamNamespace:
        """
        Build an ADaM derivation pipeline from a YAML specification file.

        Reads a ``define.yaml`` with a top-level ``datasets`` list where each
        variable carries a ``derivation`` block.  Pass *dataset* to select
        which dataset to execute (e.g. ``dataset="ADVS"``).  When the file
        contains only one dataset the *dataset* argument may be omitted.

        *only*: optional allow-list — process only the listed variable names.
        *omit*: optional deny-list — skip the listed variable names; useful when
        you want to override a spec variable with custom inline logic::

            dm.adam.from_spec(..., omit=["MYVAR"]).assigned("MYVAR", value="override")

        ``only`` and ``omit`` are mutually exclusive; specifying both raises
        ``ValueError``.

        For dependency-driven staging, declare
        ``depends_on: [col, ...]`` in the YAML derivation block instead;
        ``from_spec()`` will flush automatically before any variable whose
        declared dependencies are not yet committed to the frame::

            # define.yaml
            - name: ADY
              derivation:
                algorithm: study_day
                analysis_date: ADT
                reference_date: TRTSDT
                depends_on: [ADT]    # flush before ADY if ADT only pending

        With ``depends_on`` set, a single call suffices::

            advs = vs_df.adam.from_spec("specs/.../define.yaml", dataset="ADVS").to_frame()

        Examples:
            Build ADVS from a YAML specification::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .from_spec("examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/define.yaml",
                               dataset="ADVS")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        from .models import ADAMDatasetSpec

        if only is not None and omit is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                "Cannot specify both only= and omit= in from_spec(). "
                "Use only= to allow-list variables, or omit= to deny-list them."
            )

        spec_data = yaml.safe_load(Path(spec_path).read_text())

        # ── Detect format: define.yaml has a top-level "datasets" key ──
        if "datasets" in spec_data:
            variables = self._extract_define_variables(spec_data, dataset)
        else:
            spec = ADAMDatasetSpec(**spec_data)
            variables = spec.variables

        ns: AdamNamespace = self
        for var in variables:
            alg = var.algorithm.value
            target = var.target
            if only is not None and target not in only:
                continue
            if omit is not None and target in omit:
                continue

            # ── auto-flush when a declared dependency is not yet committed ──
            deps = getattr(var, "depends_on", None) or []
            if deps and any(d not in ns._lazy.columns for d in deps):
                ns = ns._materialise_then(ns.to_frame())

            if alg == "source":
                ns = ns.source(target, from_col=var.source)
            elif alg == "derivation":
                ns = ns.derivation(target, expression=var.expression or target)
            elif alg == "assigned":
                ns = ns.assigned(target, value=var.value)
            elif alg == "recode":
                ns = ns.recode(
                    target,
                    source=var.source or target,
                    recode_map=var.recode_map or {},
                    default=var.default,
                )
            elif alg == "rename":
                ns = ns.rename(target, source=var.source or target)
            elif alg == "condderivation":
                ns = ns.condderivation(
                    target, conditions=var.conditions or [], else_value=var.else_value
                )
            # First-class BDS algorithm names usable directly in YAML specs
            elif alg in (
                "study_day",
                "baseline",
                "chg",
                "pchg",
                "bmi",
                "bsa",
                "map",
                "mean_arterial_pressure",
                "qtc",
            ):
                ns = ns._std_function_dispatch(
                    target,
                    func=alg,
                    analysis_date=var.analysis_date,
                    reference_date=var.reference_date,
                    aval=var.aval or "AVAL",
                    base=var.base or "BASE",
                    weight=var.weight,
                    height=var.height,
                    systolic=getattr(var, "systolic", None),
                    diastolic=getattr(var, "diastolic", None),
                    qt=getattr(var, "qt", None),
                    rr=getattr(var, "rr", None),
                    method=getattr(var, "method", None),
                    baseline_flag=var.baseline_flag or "ABLFL",
                    groups=getattr(var, "groups", None),
                )
            elif alg == "flag":
                ns = ns.flag(
                    target,
                    criteria=getattr(var, "criteria", "") or "",
                    groups=getattr(var, "groups", None),
                    order_by=getattr(var, "flag_order_by", None),
                    value_col=getattr(var, "flag_value_col", None),
                    where=getattr(var, "flag_where", None),
                )
            elif alg == "date":
                kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
                if var.source:
                    kwargs["source"] = var.source
                elif getattr(var, "value", None):
                    kwargs["value"] = var.value
                if getattr(var, "output", None):
                    kwargs["output"] = var.output
                if getattr(var, "impute", None):
                    kwargs["impute"] = var.impute
                if getattr(var, "impute_time", None):
                    kwargs["impute_time"] = var.impute_time
                if getattr(var, "flag", None) is not None:
                    kwargs["flag"] = var.flag
                ns = ns.date(target, **kwargs)
            elif alg == "duration":
                ns = ns.duration(
                    target,
                    start=getattr(var, "start", None) or var.analysis_date or "",
                    end=getattr(var, "end", None) or var.reference_date or "",
                    unit=getattr(var, "unit", "days") or "days",
                )
            elif alg == "nrind":
                ns = ns.nrind(
                    target,
                    value=var.aval or "AVAL",
                    low=getattr(var, "low", "LBSTNRLO"),
                    high=getattr(var, "high", "LBSTNRHI"),
                )
            elif alg == "on_treatment":
                ns = ns.on_treatment(
                    target,
                    adt=var.analysis_date or "ADT",
                    trtsdt=var.reference_date or "TRTSDT",
                    trtedt=getattr(var, "trtedt", "TRTEDT"),
                )
            elif alg == "shift":
                ns = ns.shift(
                    target,
                    baseline_cat=getattr(var, "baseline_cat", ""),
                    post_cat=getattr(var, "post_cat", ""),
                )
            elif alg == "whereclauses":
                if var.where:
                    ns = ns.whereclauses(where=var.where)
            elif alg == "pick":
                pick_targets = getattr(var, "targets", None) or [target]
                pick_events = getattr(var, "events", None) or []
                pick_by = getattr(var, "by", None)
                pick_order = getattr(var, "order", None)
                pick_mode = getattr(var, "mode", "first") or "first"
                ns = ns.pick(
                    pick_targets,
                    events=pick_events,
                    by=pick_by,
                    order=pick_order,
                    mode=pick_mode,
                )
            elif alg == "callable":
                fn = _resolve_callable(var.callable_ref or "")
                if hasattr(fn, "kind"):
                    ns = ns.derivation(fn)
                else:
                    ns = ns._materialise_then(fn(ns.to_frame()))
            else:
                import warnings

                warnings.warn(
                    f"from_spec: skipping variable '{target}' — "
                    f"algorithm '{alg}' is not supported in spec-driven mode.",
                    stacklevel=2,
                )

        return ns

    @staticmethod
    def _extract_define_variables(spec_data: dict, dataset: str | None) -> list:
        """Convert define.yaml dataset variables into ADAMVariableSpec objects."""
        from .models import ADAMVariableSpec

        datasets = spec_data["datasets"]
        if dataset is None:
            if len(datasets) != 1:
                names = [d["name"] for d in datasets]
                raise ValueError(
                    f"define.yaml contains {len(datasets)} datasets {names}. "
                    "Pass dataset= to select one."
                )
            ds = datasets[0]
        else:
            matches = [d for d in datasets if d["name"].upper() == dataset.upper()]
            if not matches:
                names = [d["name"] for d in datasets]
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Dataset '{dataset}' not found in define.yaml. Available: {names}"
                )
            ds = matches[0]

        result = []
        for var in ds["variables"]:
            drv = var.get("derivation")
            if not drv:
                continue  # no derivation → carry-through / manual column
            # Backward compat: callable: without algorithm: → inject algorithm.
            if "callable" in drv and "algorithm" not in drv:
                drv = {**drv, "algorithm": "callable"}
            spec = ADAMVariableSpec(
                target=var["name"],
                **drv,
            )
            result.append(spec)
        return result

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # ADaM sub-structures (accessed as df.adam.adsl / df.adam.occds)       #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

def lookup(
    self,
    target_cols: list[str] | None = None,
    *,
    dataset: pl.DataFrame,
    on: str | list[str],
    how: str = "left",
    where: str | None = None,
) -> AdamNamespace:
    """SQL-style join against a lookup *dataset*.

    Optionally filters *dataset* with *where* before the join.
    Materialises the current pipeline then returns a fresh namespace.

    Args:
        target_cols: Optional columns to keep from the joined result.
        dataset: The lookup ``pl.DataFrame`` to join.
        on: Key column name(s) for the join.
        how: Join strategy (default ``"left"``).
        where: Optional filter expression applied to *dataset* before
            the join.

    Returns:
        AdamNamespace: A fresh namespace wrapping the joined frame.

    Examples:
        Join a parameter-code lookup table on ``VSTESTCD``::

            advs = (
                vs_df.adam
                .lookup(
                    dataset=paramcd_lookup,
                    on="VSTESTCD",
                    how="left",
                )
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from ..sdtm.utils import parse_expression

    lookup_df = dataset
    if where:
        filter_expr = parse_expression(where)
        lookup_df = dataset.filter(filter_expr)

    joined = self.to_frame().join(lookup_df, on=on, how=how)
    ns = self._materialise_then(joined)
    if target_cols:
        ns._pipeline = [pl.col(c) for c in target_cols]
    return ns

Materialises the current pipeline before concatenation.

Examples:

Compute mean AVAL per subject and parameter::

advs = (
    vs_raw.adam
    .derive_summary_records(
        by_vars=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"],
        analysis_var="AVAL",
        set_values_to={"DTYPE": "AVERAGE"},
        stat="mean",
    )
    .to_frame()
)

def derive_summary_records(
    self,
    *,
    by_vars: list[str],
    analysis_var: str = "AVAL",
    set_values_to: dict[str, Any],
    stat: str = "mean",
) -> AdamNamespace:
    """
    Compute a summary statistic per group and append the results as new records.

    *set_values_to*: column → value mapping applied to every new record
    (e.g. ``{"PARAMCD": "AVGBP", "DTYPE": "AVERAGE"}``).

    *stat*: ``"mean"`` (default), ``"sum"``, ``"min"``, ``"max"``, ``"median"``,
    ``"count"``.

    Materialises the current pipeline before concatenation.

    Examples:
        Compute mean AVAL per subject and parameter::

            advs = (
                vs_raw.adam
                .derive_summary_records(
                    by_vars=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"],
                    analysis_var="AVAL",
                    set_values_to={"DTYPE": "AVERAGE"},
                    stat="mean",
                )
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    stat_lower = stat.lower()
    agg_map = {
        "mean": pl.col(analysis_var).mean(),
        "sum": pl.col(analysis_var).sum(),
        "min": pl.col(analysis_var).min(),
        "max": pl.col(analysis_var).max(),
        "median": pl.col(analysis_var).median(),
        "count": pl.col(analysis_var).count().cast(pl.Float64),
    }
    if stat_lower not in agg_map:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown stat '{stat}'. Supported: {', '.join(agg_map)}.")

    df = self.to_frame()
    summary = df.group_by(by_vars).agg(agg_map[stat_lower].alias(analysis_var))

    # Apply constant values to the summary rows
    for col_name, col_val in set_values_to.items():
        summary = summary.with_columns(pl.lit(col_val).alias(col_name))

    # Align schemas before concat: add missing columns as null in both directions
    for c in df.columns:
        if c not in summary.columns:
            summary = summary.with_columns(pl.lit(None).cast(df.schema[c]).alias(c))
    for c in summary.columns:
        if c not in df.columns:
            df = df.with_columns(pl.lit(None).cast(summary.schema[c]).alias(c))

    col_order = df.columns
    summary = summary.select(col_order)

    combined = pl.concat([df, summary], how="vertical_relaxed")
    return self._materialise_then(combined)

    by_vars: list[str] | None = None,
    analysis_var: str = "AVAL",
    order_by: str = "ADT",
) -> AdamNamespace:

    Forward-fill *analysis_var* within each group (LOCF).

    then forward-fills null values in *analysis_var*.

    Materialises the current pipeline, applies the fill, and returns.

    Examples:

                vs_raw.adam
                .derive_locf_records(
                    by_vars=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"],

    df = df.sort(grps + [order_by])

    return self._materialise_then(df)

                       "PARAM": "Body Mass Index"},

                          "HEIGHT": "HEIGHT"},

def derive_param(
    self,
    *,
    by_vars: list[str] | None = None,
    set_values_to: dict[str, Any],
    parameter_filter: dict[str, str],
    analysis_value: pl.Expr,
) -> AdamNamespace:
    """
    Derive a new parameter (e.g. BMI) from existing records and append
    the computed rows to the dataset.

    *parameter_filter*: ``{PARAMCD: value}`` pairs identifying the source
    records to pivot on (e.g. ``{"WEIGHT": "WEIGHT", "HEIGHT": "HEIGHT"}``).
    Each key is a local alias; the value is the ``PARAMCD`` it matches.

    *analysis_value*: a Polars expression referencing the aliases to
    compute the new AVAL (e.g. ``pl.col("WEIGHT") / (pl.col("HEIGHT")/100)**2``).

    *set_values_to*: constant columns on the new rows
    (e.g. ``{"PARAMCD": "BMI", "PARAM": "Body Mass Index"}``).

    Materialises the pipeline before appending.

    Examples:
        Derive BMI as a new PARAMCD from WEIGHT and HEIGHT::

            advs = (
                vs_raw.adam
                .derive_param(
                    by_vars=["USUBJID", "ADT"],
                    set_values_to={"PARAMCD": "BMI",
                                   "PARAM": "Body Mass Index"},
                    parameter_filter={"WEIGHT": "WEIGHT",
                                      "HEIGHT": "HEIGHT"},
                    analysis_value=(
                        pl.col("WEIGHT") / (pl.col("HEIGHT") / 100) ** 2
                    ),
                )
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    grps = by_vars or ["USUBJID"]
    df = self.to_frame()

    # Pivot: for each alias in parameter_filter, get AVAL as that alias
    pivoted_parts = []
    for alias, paramcd_val in parameter_filter.items():
        part = df.filter(pl.col("PARAMCD") == paramcd_val).select(
            grps + [pl.col("AVAL").alias(alias)]
        )
        pivoted_parts.append(part)

    # Join all pivoted parts on the by_vars
    joined = pivoted_parts[0]
    for part in pivoted_parts[1:]:
        joined = joined.join(part, on=grps, how="inner")

    # Compute the new AVAL
    new_rows = joined.with_columns(analysis_value.alias("AVAL")).select(grps + ["AVAL"])

    # Apply set_values_to constants
    for col_name, col_val in set_values_to.items():
        new_rows = new_rows.with_columns(pl.lit(col_val).alias(col_name))

    # Align schemas and concat
    for c in df.columns:
        if c not in new_rows.columns:
            new_rows = new_rows.with_columns(pl.lit(None).cast(df.schema[c]).alias(c))
    new_rows = new_rows.select(df.columns)

    combined = pl.concat([df, new_rows], how="vertical_relaxed")
    return self._materialise_then(combined)

def atoxgr(
    self,
    target: str,
    *,
    system: str = "ctcae_v5",
    direction: str,
    term_var: str,
    unit_var: str | None = None,
    signif_dig: int = 5,
    indicators: dict[str, list[str]] | None = None,
) -> AdamNamespace:
    """Derive a toxicity grade column using a criteria-file grading system.

    Materialises the pipeline, applies the grading engine for every
    matching lab term, and returns a fresh namespace with *target*
    appended.

    Args:
        target: Name of the output grade column (e.g. ``"ATOXGRL"``).
        system: Grading system name (e.g. ``"ctcae_v5"``, ``"daids"``)
            or path to a custom JSON criteria file.
        direction: ``"L"`` (low) or ``"H"`` (high).
        term_var: Column holding the lab-test / term name.
        unit_var: Optional column holding the unit of measure.
        signif_dig: Significant figures for comparison (default 5).
        indicators: Optional indicator parameter map for branch
            conditions (e.g. ``{"H": ["HIGH"], "L": ["LOW"]}``).

    Returns:
        AdamNamespace: A fresh namespace wrapping the graded frame.

    Examples:
        Grade low-direction anemia using CTCAE v5::

            adlb = (
                lb_raw.adam
                .atoxgr("ATOXGRL", system="ctcae_v5",
                        direction="L", term_var="PARAMCD",
                        unit_var="AVALU")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from .grading._compiler import grade_dataset
    from .grading._registry import load_criteria

    criteria = load_criteria(system)
    df = self.to_frame()
    # Provide standard BNRIND defaults when no indicators are given.
    if indicators is None:
        indicators = {
            "high_indicator": ["HIGH", "H"],
            "low_indicator": ["LOW", "L"],
        }
    graded = grade_dataset(
        df,
        criteria,
        target=target,
        direction=direction,
        term_var=term_var,
        unit_var=unit_var,
        signif_dig=signif_dig,
        indicators=indicators,
    )
    return self._materialise_then(graded)

                .atoxgr("ATOXGRH", system="ctcae_v5",
                        direction="H", term_var="PARAMCD")
                .combine_grades("ATOXGR")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from .grading._compiler import combine_grades_expr

    return self._chain(
        combine_grades_expr(
            low_var,
            high_var,
            low_desc_var=low_desc_var,
            high_desc_var=high_desc_var,
        ).alias(target)
    )

The pending expression pipeline is materialised before the function is called, so the function always receives a fully committed frame.

Examples:

Register and apply a custom age-group transform::

        pl.when(pl.col("AGE") < 65).then(pl.lit("<65"))
