docs.title: fleet.adam.FlagCriterionMixin
docs.text:
Mixin providing flag() and criterion() to any namespace.

Both SDTM (df.sdtm) and all ADaM namespaces inherit from this mixin. The methods rely on _chain() and _materialise_then() which every concrete namespace class must provide.

Source code in src/fleet/adam/_mixins.py 
class FlagCriterionMixin:
    """Mixin providing ``flag()`` and ``criterion()`` to any namespace.

    Both SDTM (``df.sdtm``) and all ADaM namespaces inherit from this
    mixin.  The methods rely on ``_chain()`` and ``_materialise_then()``
    which every concrete namespace class must provide.
    """

    _lazy: pl.LazyFrame

    # Subclasses must provide these — declared here for type-checker only.
    def _chain(self, *exprs: pl.Expr) -> Self: ...  # noqa: E704
    def _materialise_then(self, df: pl.DataFrame) -> Self: ...  # noqa: E704

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Flag — generalised "Y" / null flagging                               #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def flag(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        criteria: str | pl.Expr,
        groups: list[str] | None = None,
        order_by: str | list[str] | None = None,
        value_col: str | None = None,
        where: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
        from_dataset: pl.DataFrame | list[pl.DataFrame] | None = None,
        on: list[str] | None = None,
        source_filter: pl.Expr | None = None,
        condition: pl.Expr | None = None,
        inclusive: bool = True,
        flag_no_ref_groups: bool = True,
        flag_all: bool = False,
        flag_value: str = "Y",
        false_value: str | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Set *target* to *flag_value* for records matching *criteria*.

        Supports row-level boolean expressions and built-in shortcuts:

        - ``"first"`` / ``"last"`` — rank-based edge detection within groups.
        - ``"max"`` / ``"min"`` — value-based extreme within groups.
        - ``"exists"`` — set-membership from external dataset(s).
        - ``"before"`` / ``"after"`` — relative to a landmark condition.
        - ``"exists_after"`` / ``"exists_before"`` — temporal/self-join flag.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output flag column.
            criteria: A Polars expression, or one of ``"first"``,
                ``"last"``, ``"max"``, ``"min"``, ``"exists"``,
                ``"before"``, ``"after"``, ``"exists_after"``,
                ``"exists_before"``.
            groups: Partition columns (default ``["USUBJID"]``).
            order_by: Sort column(s) required for ``"first"``/``"last"``
                and ``"before"``/``"after"``.
            value_col: Value column required for ``"max"``/``"min"``.
            where: Optional pre-filter — only matching rows are candidates.
            from_dataset: External dataset(s) for ``"exists"`` and
                ``"exists_after"``/``"exists_before"`` criteria.
            on: Join key columns for ``"exists"`` criteria.
            source_filter: Filter applied to *from_dataset* before key
                extraction or join.
            condition: Boolean expression identifying landmark rows for
                ``"before"``/``"after"`` or the current-row condition for
                ``"exists_after"``/``"exists_before"``.
            inclusive: Whether the landmark row itself is included in the
                flag (for ``"before"``/``"after"``). Default ``True``.
            flag_no_ref_groups: If ``False``, groups without a landmark
                condition match get ``None`` instead of being flagged
                (for ``"before"``/``"after"``). Default ``True``.
            flag_all: If ``True``, all tied extreme values receive the
                flag (for ``"first"``/``"last"``). Default ``False``.
            flag_value: Value to assign when condition is met (default
                ``"Y"``).
            false_value: Value to assign when condition is not met.
                Default ``None`` (null).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Examples:
            First observation per group::

                advs = (
                    vs_raw.adam
                    .flag("ABLFL", criteria="first", order_by="AVISITN",
                          groups=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
                    .to_frame()
                )

            Existence flag from external dataset::

                adsl = (
                    dm.adam.adsl
                    .flag("VSEVALFL", criteria="exists",
                          from_dataset=advs, on=["USUBJID"],
                          source_filter=pl.col("AVISIT") == "BASELINE")
                    .to_frame()
                )

            Relative flag — before first PD::

                result = (
                    response.adam
                    .flag("ANL02FL", criteria="before",
                          condition=pl.col("AVALC") == "PD",
                          order_by="AVISITN", groups=["USUBJID"],
                          inclusive=True)
                    .to_frame()
                )

            Population flag on SDTM::

                dm = (
                    raw_df.sdtm
                    .flag("SAFFL", criteria=pl.col("EXDOSE") > 0,
                          groups=["USUBJID"])
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

        grps = groups or ["USUBJID"]
        order_cols: list[str] | None = None
        if order_by is not None:
            order_cols = [order_by] if isinstance(order_by, str) else list(order_by)

        where_expr: pl.Expr | None = None
        if where is not None:
            where_expr = where if isinstance(where, pl.Expr) else parse_expression(str(where))

        false_lit = pl.lit(false_value) if false_value is not None else pl.lit(None)

        criteria_lower = criteria.lower() if isinstance(criteria, str) else None

        if criteria_lower in ("first", "last"):
            return self._flag_ranked(
                target,
                criteria_lower=criteria_lower,
                grps=grps,
                order_cols=order_cols,
                where_expr=where_expr,
                flag_all=flag_all,
                flag_value=flag_value,
                false_value=false_value,
                false_lit=false_lit,
            )
        elif criteria_lower in ("max", "min"):
            return self._flag_extreme(
                target,
                criteria_lower=criteria_lower,
                grps=grps,
                value_col=value_col,
                where_expr=where_expr,
                flag_value=flag_value,
                false_lit=false_lit,
            )
        elif criteria_lower == "exists":
            return self._flag_exists(
                target,
                grps=grps,
                from_dataset=from_dataset,
                on=on,
                source_filter=source_filter,
                flag_value=flag_value,
                false_value=false_value,
                false_lit=false_lit,
            )
        elif criteria_lower in ("before", "after"):
            return self._flag_relative(
                target,
                criteria_lower=criteria_lower,
                grps=grps,
                order_cols=order_cols,
                condition=condition,
                inclusive=inclusive,
                flag_no_ref_groups=flag_no_ref_groups,
                flag_value=flag_value,
                false_value=false_value,
            )
        elif criteria_lower in ("exists_after", "exists_before"):
            return self._flag_temporal_exists(
                target,
                criteria_lower=criteria_lower,
                from_dataset=from_dataset,
                on=on,
                order_cols=order_cols,
                condition=condition,
                source_filter=source_filter,
                flag_value=flag_value,
            )
        else:
            return self._flag_expression(
                target,
                criteria=criteria,
                where_expr=where_expr,
                flag_value=flag_value,
                false_lit=false_lit,
            )

    def _flag_ranked(
        self,
        target,
        *,
        criteria_lower,
        grps,
        order_cols,
        where_expr,
        flag_all,
        flag_value,
        false_value,
        false_lit,
    ) -> Self:
        """Handle first/last rank-based flag criteria."""
        if not order_cols:
            raise ValueError(f"flag criteria='{criteria_lower}' requires order_by.")
        descending = criteria_lower == "last"

        df = self._lazy.collect()
        df = df.with_row_index("__flag_orig_idx__")
        null_mask = pl.all_horizontal([pl.col(c).is_not_null() for c in order_cols])

        if flag_all:
            if len(order_cols) == 1:
                val_expr = pl.col(order_cols[0])
            else:
                val_expr = pl.struct(order_cols)
            extreme = val_expr.max().over(grps) if descending else val_expr.min().over(grps)
            row_cond = null_mask & (val_expr == extreme)
            if where_expr is not None:
                row_cond = where_expr & row_cond
            expr = pl.when(row_cond).then(pl.lit(flag_value)).otherwise(false_lit).alias(target)
            result_df = df.with_columns(expr).sort("__flag_orig_idx__").drop("__flag_orig_idx__")
            return self._materialise_then(result_df)

        sort_descending = [descending] * len(order_cols)
        null_last = [True] * len(order_cols)

        eligible = df.filter(null_mask)
        if where_expr is not None:
            eligible = eligible.filter(where_expr)

        eligible_sorted = eligible.sort(
            order_cols, descending=sort_descending, nulls_last=null_last
        )
        first_per_group = eligible_sorted.group_by(grps, maintain_order=True).first()
        flagged_indices = set(first_per_group["__flag_orig_idx__"].to_list())

        flags = [
            flag_value if idx in flagged_indices else (false_value if false_value else None)
            for idx in df["__flag_orig_idx__"].to_list()
        ]
        result_df = (
            df.with_columns(pl.Series(target, flags))
            .sort("__flag_orig_idx__")
            .drop("__flag_orig_idx__")
        )
        return self._materialise_then(result_df)

    def _flag_extreme(
        self,
        target,
        *,
        criteria_lower,
        grps,
        value_col,
        where_expr,
        flag_value,
        false_lit,
    ) -> Self:
        """Handle max/min value-based extreme flag criteria."""
        if not value_col:
            raise ValueError(f"flag criteria='{criteria_lower}' requires value_col.")
        if where_expr is not None:
            masked_val = pl.when(where_expr).then(pl.col(value_col)).otherwise(pl.lit(None))
            agg_val = (
                masked_val.max().over(grps)
                if criteria_lower == "max"
                else masked_val.min().over(grps)
            )
            row_cond = where_expr & (pl.col(value_col) == agg_val)
        else:
            agg_val = (
                pl.col(value_col).max().over(grps)
                if criteria_lower == "max"
                else pl.col(value_col).min().over(grps)
            )
            row_cond = pl.col(value_col) == agg_val
        expr = pl.when(row_cond).then(pl.lit(flag_value)).otherwise(false_lit).alias(target)
        return self._chain(expr)

    def _flag_exists(
        self,
        target,
        *,
        grps,
        from_dataset,
        on,
        source_filter,
        flag_value,
        false_value,
        false_lit,
    ) -> Self:
        """Handle exists set-membership flag criteria."""
        if from_dataset is None or on is None:
            raise ValueError("flag criteria='exists' requires from_dataset and on.")
        datasets = from_dataset if isinstance(from_dataset, list) else [from_dataset]
        key_frames: list[pl.DataFrame] = []
        for ds in datasets:
            filtered = ds
            if source_filter is not None:
                filtered = ds.filter(source_filter)
            key_frames.append(filtered.select(on).unique())
        all_keys = pl.concat(key_frames).unique()

        df = self._lazy.collect()

        if len(on) == 1:
            is_member = pl.col(on[0]).is_in(all_keys[on[0]].to_list())
            expr = pl.when(is_member).then(pl.lit(flag_value)).otherwise(false_lit).alias(target)
            return self._chain(expr)

        # Multi-column join path
        df_with_idx = df.with_row_index("__flag_idx__")
        result = (
            (df_with_idx.drop(target) if target in df_with_idx.columns else df_with_idx)
            .join(
                df_with_idx.select(on + ["__flag_idx__"])
                .unique()
                .join(all_keys, on=on, how="semi")
                .with_columns(pl.lit(flag_value).alias(target)),
                on="__flag_idx__",
                how="left",
            )
            .with_columns(
                pl.col(target).fill_null(pl.lit(false_value) if false_value else pl.lit(None))
            )
            .drop("__flag_idx__")
        )
        return self._materialise_then(result)

    def _flag_relative(
        self,
        target,
        *,
        criteria_lower,
        grps,
        order_cols,
        condition,
        inclusive,
        flag_no_ref_groups,
        flag_value,
        false_value,
    ) -> Self:
        """Handle before/after relative-to-landmark flag criteria."""
        if condition is None:
            raise ValueError(f"flag criteria='{criteria_lower}' requires condition.")
        if not order_cols:
            raise ValueError(f"flag criteria='{criteria_lower}' requires order_by.")

        df = self._lazy.collect()
        df = df.with_row_index("__orig_idx__")
        df_sorted = df.sort(order_cols)

        cond_col = "__flag_cond__"
        df_sorted = df_sorted.with_columns(condition.cast(pl.Boolean).alias(cond_col))

        result_parts: list[pl.DataFrame] = []
        for _, grp_df in df_sorted.group_by(grps, maintain_order=True):
            cond_mask = grp_df[cond_col].to_list()
            first_cond_idx: int | None = None
            for i, v in enumerate(cond_mask):
                if v is True:
                    first_cond_idx = i
                    break

            n = len(grp_df)
            if first_cond_idx is None:
                if flag_no_ref_groups:
                    if criteria_lower == "before":
                        flags = [flag_value] * n
                    else:
                        flags = [false_value] * n
                else:
                    flags = [false_value if false_value else None] * n
            else:
                flags = []
                for i in range(n):
                    if criteria_lower == "before":
                        flagged = i <= first_cond_idx if inclusive else i < first_cond_idx
                    else:
                        flagged = i >= first_cond_idx if inclusive else i > first_cond_idx
                    flags.append(flag_value if flagged else (false_value if false_value else None))
            result_parts.append(grp_df.with_columns(pl.Series(target, flags)))

        result_df = pl.concat(result_parts)
        result_df = result_df.sort("__orig_idx__").drop(["__orig_idx__", cond_col])
        return self._materialise_then(result_df)

    def _flag_temporal_exists(
        self,
        target,
        *,
        criteria_lower,
        from_dataset,
        on,
        order_cols,
        condition,
        source_filter,
        flag_value,
    ) -> Self:
        """Handle exists_after/exists_before temporal join flag criteria."""
        if from_dataset is None or condition is None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"flag criteria='{criteria_lower}' requires from_dataset and condition."
            )
        if on is None:
            raise ValueError(f"flag criteria='{criteria_lower}' requires on.")

        df = self._lazy.collect()
        src = from_dataset if isinstance(from_dataset, pl.DataFrame) else pl.concat(from_dataset)
        if source_filter is not None:
            src = src.filter(source_filter)

        if order_cols:
            time_col = order_cols[0]
        else:
            common_time = [
                c for c in ["AVISITN", "ADY", "ADT", "ADTM"] if c in df.columns and c in src.columns
            ]
            if not common_time:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"flag criteria='{criteria_lower}' requires order_by or a "
                    "common temporal column (AVISITN, ADY, ADT, ADTM)."
                )
            time_col = common_time[0]

        df = df.with_row_index("__flag_idx__")
        cond_df = df.filter(condition)

        flags = [None] * len(df)
        for row in cond_df.iter_rows(named=True):
            src_filtered = src
            for key in on:
                src_filtered = src_filtered.filter(pl.col(key) == row[key])
            if len(src_filtered) == 0:
                continue
            row_time = row[time_col]
            if criteria_lower == "exists_after":
                matches = src_filtered.filter(pl.col(time_col) > row_time)
            else:
                matches = src_filtered.filter(pl.col(time_col) < row_time)
            if len(matches) > 0:
                flags[row["__flag_idx__"]] = flag_value

        result_df = df.drop("__flag_idx__").with_columns(pl.Series(target, flags))
        return self._materialise_then(result_df)

    def _flag_expression(
        self,
        target,
        *,
        criteria,
        where_expr,
        flag_value,
        false_lit,
    ) -> Self:
        """Handle direct expression-based flag criteria."""
        from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

        if isinstance(criteria, pl.Expr):
            row_cond = criteria
        else:
            row_cond = parse_expression(str(criteria))
        final_cond = (where_expr & row_cond) if where_expr is not None else row_cond
        expr = pl.when(final_cond).then(pl.lit(flag_value)).otherwise(false_lit).alias(target)
        return self._chain(expr)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Criterion — CRITy / CRITyFL / CRITyFN triple-output                 #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def criterion(
        self,
        number: int,
        *,
        condition: pl.Expr,
        description: str | None = None,
        prefix: str = "CRIT",
    ) -> Self:
        """Derive criterion flag triple: CRITy, CRITyFL, CRITyFN.

        Produces three columns following CDISC ADaM conventions:

        - ``{prefix}{number}`` — the criterion description (constant string).
        - ``{prefix}{number}FL`` — ``"Y"`` if condition is met, ``"N"`` otherwise.
        - ``{prefix}{number}FN`` — ``1`` if met, ``0`` otherwise.

        Args:
            number: Criterion number (e.g. 1 → CRIT1, CRIT1FL, CRIT1FN).
            condition: Boolean Polars expression defining the criterion.
            description: Human-readable description stored in CRITy column.
                If ``None``, the column is still created with null values.
            prefix: Column name prefix (default ``"CRIT"``).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with three new columns appended; call
                ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

        Examples:
            Flag records where AVAL >= 10::

                adlb = (
                    lb_df.adam
                    .criterion(1, condition=pl.col("AVAL") >= 10,
                               description="AVAL >= 10")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        col_crit = f"{prefix}{number}"
        col_fl = f"{prefix}{number}FL"
        col_fn = f"{prefix}{number}FN"

        desc_expr = (
            pl.lit(description).alias(col_crit)
            if description is not None
            else pl.lit(None).cast(pl.String).alias(col_crit)
        )
        fl_expr = pl.when(condition).then(pl.lit("Y")).otherwise(pl.lit("N")).alias(col_fl)
        fn_expr = pl.when(condition).then(pl.lit(1)).otherwise(pl.lit(0)).alias(col_fn)

        return self._chain(desc_expr, fl_expr, fn_expr)

flag(
    target,
    *,
    criteria,
    groups=None,
    order_by=None,
    value_col=None,
    where=None,
    from_dataset=None,
    on=None,
    source_filter=None,
    condition=None,
    inclusive=True,
    flag_no_ref_groups=True,
    flag_all=False,
    flag_value="Y",
    false_value=None
)

Set target to flag_value for records matching criteria.

Supports row-level boolean expressions and built-in shortcuts:

  • "first" / "last" — rank-based edge detection within groups.
  • "max" / "min" — value-based extreme within groups.
  • "exists" — set-membership from external dataset(s).
  • "before" / "after" — relative to a landmark condition.
  • "exists_after" / "exists_before" — temporal/self-join flag.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default target str

Name of the output flag column.

required criteria str | Expr

A Polars expression, or one of "first", "last", "max", "min", "exists", "before", "after", "exists_after", "exists_before".

required groups list[str] | None

Partition columns (default ["USUBJID"]).

None order_by str | list[str] | None

Sort column(s) required for "first"/"last" and "before"/"after".

None value_col str | None

Value column required for "max"/"min".

None where str | Expr | None

Optional pre-filter — only matching rows are candidates.

None from_dataset DataFrame | list[DataFrame] | None

External dataset(s) for "exists" and "exists_after"/"exists_before" criteria.

None on list[str] | None

Join key columns for "exists" criteria.

None source_filter Expr | None

Filter applied to from_dataset before key extraction or join.

None condition Expr | None

Boolean expression identifying landmark rows for "before"/"after" or the current-row condition for "exists_after"/"exists_before".

None inclusive bool

Whether the landmark row itself is included in the flag (for "before"/"after"). Default True.

True flag_no_ref_groups bool

def flag(
    self,
    target: str,
    *,
    criteria: str | pl.Expr,
    groups: list[str] | None = None,
    order_by: str | list[str] | None = None,
    value_col: str | None = None,
    where: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
    from_dataset: pl.DataFrame | list[pl.DataFrame] | None = None,
    on: list[str] | None = None,
    source_filter: pl.Expr | None = None,
    condition: pl.Expr | None = None,
    inclusive: bool = True,
    flag_no_ref_groups: bool = True,
    flag_all: bool = False,
    flag_value: str = "Y",
    false_value: str | None = None,
) -> Self:
    """Set *target* to *flag_value* for records matching *criteria*.

    Supports row-level boolean expressions and built-in shortcuts:

    - ``"first"`` / ``"last"`` — rank-based edge detection within groups.
    - ``"max"`` / ``"min"`` — value-based extreme within groups.
    - ``"exists"`` — set-membership from external dataset(s).
    - ``"before"`` / ``"after"`` — relative to a landmark condition.
    - ``"exists_after"`` / ``"exists_before"`` — temporal/self-join flag.

    Args:
        target: Name of the output flag column.
        criteria: A Polars expression, or one of ``"first"``,
            ``"last"``, ``"max"``, ``"min"``, ``"exists"``,
            ``"before"``, ``"after"``, ``"exists_after"``,
            ``"exists_before"``.
        groups: Partition columns (default ``["USUBJID"]``).
        order_by: Sort column(s) required for ``"first"``/``"last"``
            and ``"before"``/``"after"``.
        value_col: Value column required for ``"max"``/``"min"``.
        where: Optional pre-filter — only matching rows are candidates.
        from_dataset: External dataset(s) for ``"exists"`` and
            ``"exists_after"``/``"exists_before"`` criteria.
        on: Join key columns for ``"exists"`` criteria.
        source_filter: Filter applied to *from_dataset* before key
            extraction or join.
        condition: Boolean expression identifying landmark rows for
            ``"before"``/``"after"`` or the current-row condition for
            ``"exists_after"``/``"exists_before"``.
        inclusive: Whether the landmark row itself is included in the
            flag (for ``"before"``/``"after"``). Default ``True``.
        flag_no_ref_groups: If ``False``, groups without a landmark
            condition match get ``None`` instead of being flagged
            (for ``"before"``/``"after"``). Default ``True``.
        flag_all: If ``True``, all tied extreme values receive the
            flag (for ``"first"``/``"last"``). Default ``False``.
        flag_value: Value to assign when condition is met (default
            ``"Y"``).
        false_value: Value to assign when condition is not met.
            Default ``None`` (null).

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with *target* appended; call
            ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Examples:
        First observation per group::

            advs = (
                vs_raw.adam
                .flag("ABLFL", criteria="first", order_by="AVISITN",
                      groups=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
                .to_frame()
            )

        Existence flag from external dataset::

            adsl = (
                dm.adam.adsl
                .flag("VSEVALFL", criteria="exists",
                      from_dataset=advs, on=["USUBJID"],
                      source_filter=pl.col("AVISIT") == "BASELINE")
                .to_frame()
            )

        Relative flag — before first PD::

            result = (
                response.adam
                .flag("ANL02FL", criteria="before",
                      condition=pl.col("AVALC") == "PD",
                      order_by="AVISITN", groups=["USUBJID"],
                      inclusive=True)
                .to_frame()
            )

        Population flag on SDTM::

            dm = (
                raw_df.sdtm
                .flag("SAFFL", criteria=pl.col("EXDOSE") > 0,
                      groups=["USUBJID"])
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

    grps = groups or ["USUBJID"]
    order_cols: list[str] | None = None
    if order_by is not None:
        order_cols = [order_by] if isinstance(order_by, str) else list(order_by)

    where_expr: pl.Expr | None = None
    if where is not None:
        where_expr = where if isinstance(where, pl.Expr) else parse_expression(str(where))

    false_lit = pl.lit(false_value) if false_value is not None else pl.lit(None)

    criteria_lower = criteria.lower() if isinstance(criteria, str) else None

    if criteria_lower in ("first", "last"):
        return self._flag_ranked(
            target,
            criteria_lower=criteria_lower,
            grps=grps,
            order_cols=order_cols,
            where_expr=where_expr,
            flag_all=flag_all,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_value=false_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )
    elif criteria_lower in ("max", "min"):
        return self._flag_extreme(
            target,
            criteria_lower=criteria_lower,
            grps=grps,
            value_col=value_col,
            where_expr=where_expr,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )
    elif criteria_lower == "exists":
        return self._flag_exists(
            target,
            grps=grps,
            from_dataset=from_dataset,
            on=on,
            source_filter=source_filter,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_value=false_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )
    elif criteria_lower in ("before", "after"):
        return self._flag_relative(
            target,
            criteria_lower=criteria_lower,
            grps=grps,
            order_cols=order_cols,
            condition=condition,
            inclusive=inclusive,
            flag_no_ref_groups=flag_no_ref_groups,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_value=false_value,
        )
    elif criteria_lower in ("exists_after", "exists_before"):
        return self._flag_temporal_exists(
            target,
            criteria_lower=criteria_lower,
            from_dataset=from_dataset,
            on=on,
            order_cols=order_cols,
            condition=condition,
            source_filter=source_filter,
            flag_value=flag_value,
        )
    else:
        return self._flag_expression(
            target,
            criteria=criteria,
            where_expr=where_expr,
            flag_value=flag_value,
            false_lit=false_lit,
        )

def criterion(
    self,
    number: int,
    *,
    condition: pl.Expr,
    description: str | None = None,
    prefix: str = "CRIT",
) -> Self:
    """Derive criterion flag triple: CRITy, CRITyFL, CRITyFN.

    Produces three columns following CDISC ADaM conventions:

    - ``{prefix}{number}`` — the criterion description (constant string).
    - ``{prefix}{number}FL`` — ``"Y"`` if condition is met, ``"N"`` otherwise.
    - ``{prefix}{number}FN`` — ``1`` if met, ``0`` otherwise.

    Args:
        number: Criterion number (e.g. 1 → CRIT1, CRIT1FL, CRIT1FN).
        condition: Boolean Polars expression defining the criterion.
        description: Human-readable description stored in CRITy column.
            If ``None``, the column is still created with null values.
        prefix: Column name prefix (default ``"CRIT"``).

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with three new columns appended; call
            ``.to_frame()`` to materialise.

    Examples:
        Flag records where AVAL >= 10::

            adlb = (
                lb_df.adam
                .criterion(1, condition=pl.col("AVAL") >= 10,
                           description="AVAL >= 10")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    col_crit = f"{prefix}{number}"
    col_fl = f"{prefix}{number}FL"
    col_fn = f"{prefix}{number}FN"

    desc_expr = (
        pl.lit(description).alias(col_crit)
        if description is not None
        else pl.lit(None).cast(pl.String).alias(col_crit)
    )
    fl_expr = pl.when(condition).then(pl.lit("Y")).otherwise(pl.lit("N")).alias(col_fl)
    fn_expr = pl.when(condition).then(pl.lit(1)).otherwise(pl.lit(0)).alias(col_fn)

    return self._chain(desc_expr, fl_expr, fn_expr)

class ADSLNamespace(SharedADaMVerbsMixin):
    """
    Immutable pipeline builder for ADSL (one-row-per-subject) derivations.

    Inherits shared verbs from ``SharedADaMVerbsMixin``
    (source, derivation, assigned, recode, rename, condderivation,
    whereclauses) and adds ADSL-specific verbs that pull summary
    statistics from event-level datasets (AE, CM, MH, EX…).
    """

    def __init__(self, df: pl.DataFrame) -> None:
        super().__init__(df)
        self._domain = "ADSL"

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # ADSL-specific verbs                                                  #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def first_date(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        from_dataset: pl.DataFrame,
        date_col: str,
        where: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
        groups: list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Derive *target* as the earliest date in *date_col* from *from_dataset*.

        Materialises the current pipeline, aggregates *from_dataset* to
        subject level, then left-joins.  Useful for ASTDTM, TRTSDT, etc.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output date column.
            from_dataset: Source ``pl.DataFrame`` to aggregate.
            date_col: Date column to take the minimum of.
            where: Optional filter applied to *from_dataset* before aggregation.
            groups: Join key columns (default ``["USUBJID"]``).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Derive earliest serious AE start date::

                adsl = (
                    dm_raw.adam.adsl
                    .first_date("AESTDTM", from_dataset=ae_sdtm,
                                date_col="AESTDTC",
                                where='pl.col("AESER") == "Y"')
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._date_agg(
            target,
            from_dataset=from_dataset,
            date_col=date_col,
            where=where,
            groups=groups,
            agg_fn="min",
        )

    def last_date(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        from_dataset: pl.DataFrame,
        date_col: str,
        where: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
        groups: list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Derive *target* as the latest date in *date_col* from *from_dataset*.

        Useful for AENDTM, TRTEDT, DTHDT, etc.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output date column.
            from_dataset: Source ``pl.DataFrame`` to aggregate.
            date_col: Date column to take the maximum of.
            where: Optional filter applied to *from_dataset* before aggregation.
            groups: Join key columns (default ``["USUBJID"]``).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Derive latest treatment end date::

                adsl = (
                    dm_raw.adam.adsl
                    .last_date("TRTEDT", from_dataset=ex_sdtm,
                               date_col="EXENDTC")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        return self._date_agg(
            target,
            from_dataset=from_dataset,
            date_col=date_col,
            where=where,
            groups=groups,
            agg_fn="max",
        )

    def _date_agg(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        from_dataset: pl.DataFrame,
        date_col: str,
        where: str | pl.Expr | None,
        groups: list[str] | None,
        agg_fn: str,
    ) -> Self:
        """Shared implementation for first_date/last_date."""
        from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

        grps = groups or ["USUBJID"]
        src = from_dataset
        if where is not None:
            where_expr = where if isinstance(where, pl.Expr) else parse_expression(str(where))
            src = src.filter(where_expr)
        col = pl.col(date_col)
        agg_expr = (col.min() if agg_fn == "min" else col.max()).alias(target)
        agg_df = src.group_by(grps).agg(agg_expr)
        df = self.to_frame().join(agg_df, on=grps, how="left")
        return self._materialise_then(df)

    def count_events(
        self,
        target: str,
        *,
        from_dataset: pl.DataFrame,
        where: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
        groups: list[str] | None = None,
    ) -> Self:
        """Derive *target* as the count of matching records in *from_dataset*.

        Returns 0 for subjects with no matching records (never null).

        Args:
            target: Name of the output count column.
            from_dataset: Source ``pl.DataFrame`` to count.
            where: Optional filter applied before counting.
            groups: Join key columns (default ``["USUBJID"]``).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Count total AE records per subject::

                adsl = (
                    dm_raw.adam.adsl
                    .count_events("NUMAE", from_dataset=ae_sdtm)
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

        grps = groups or ["USUBJID"]
        src = from_dataset
        if where is not None:
            where_expr = where if isinstance(where, pl.Expr) else parse_expression(str(where))
            src = src.filter(where_expr)
        agg_df = src.group_by(grps).agg(pl.len().alias(target))
        df = self.to_frame().join(agg_df, on=grps, how="left")
        df = df.with_columns(pl.col(target).fill_null(0))
        return self._materialise_then(df)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # ADSL: age_years — unit-aware age conversion                         #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def age_years(
        self,
        target: str = "AAGE",
        *,
        age_col: str = "AGE",
        age_unit_col: str = "AGEU",
    ) -> Self:
        """Convert age to years, handling common unit strings.

        Recognises *AGEU* values: ``YEARS``, ``MONTHS``, ``WEEKS``, ``DAYS``
        (case-insensitive).  Unknown units produce null.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (default ``"AAGE"``).
            age_col: Source age column.
            age_unit_col: Column containing the age unit string.

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Derive age in years from DM variables::

                adsl = (
                    dm_raw.adam.adsl
                    .age_years("AAGE", age_col="AGE", age_unit_col="AGEU")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        from fleet.adam.utils import age_in_years as _age_in_years_expr

        return self._chain(
            _age_in_years_expr(age_col=age_col, age_unit_col=age_unit_col, target=target)
        )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # ADSL: age_from_dates — date-based age calculation                   #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def age_from_dates(
        self,
        target: str = "AAGE",
        *,
        birth_date: str = "BRTHDT",
        reference_date: str = "TRTSDT",
        round_digits: int | None = 1,
    ) -> Self:
        """Compute age in years from two date columns.

        Uses ``(reference_date - birth_date) / 365.25`` for a more precise
        calculation than unit-conversion from ``AGE``.  Null when either
        date is missing.

        Args:
            target: Name of the output column (default ``"AAGE"``).
            birth_date: Date-of-birth column (``pl.Date``).
            reference_date: Reference date column (``pl.Date``).
            round_digits: Decimal places to round to (default ``1``).

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with *target* appended.

        Examples:
            Derive age from birth and randomisation dates::

                adsl = (
                    dm_raw.adam.adsl
                    .age_from_dates("AAGE", birth_date="BRTHDT",
                                    reference_date="RANDDT")
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        days = (
            pl.col(reference_date).cast(pl.Date) - pl.col(birth_date).cast(pl.Date)
        ).dt.total_days()
        expr = days / 365.25
        if round_digits is not None:
            expr = expr.round(round_digits)
        return self._chain(expr.alias(target))

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # ADSL: derive_period — Subperiod / Phase variables                   #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def derive_period(
        self,
        *,
        periods: list[dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> Self:
        """Create standard Subperiod / Phase variables.

        Generates ``AP{nn}SDT``, ``AP{nn}EDT``, and optionally
        ``TRT{nn:02d}P`` columns for each period.

        Args:
            periods: List of dicts each with ``"number"``, ``"start"``,
                ``"end"``, and optionally ``"treatment"``.

        Returns:
            Self: The namespace with period columns appended.

        Examples:
            Define two treatment periods::

                adsl = (
                    dm_raw.adam.adsl
                    .derive_period(
                        periods=[
                            {"number": 1, "start": "AP01SDT",
                             "end": "AP01EDT", "treatment": "TRT01P"},
                            {"number": 2, "start": "AP02SDT",
                             "end": "AP02EDT", "treatment": "TRT02P"},
                        ],
                    )
                    .to_frame()
                )
        """
        exprs: list[pl.Expr] = []
        for period in periods:
            n = period["number"]
            prefix = f"AP{n:02d}"
            sdt_col = period["start"]
            edt_col = period["end"]

            exprs.append(pl.col(sdt_col).alias(f"{prefix}SDT"))
            exprs.append(pl.col(edt_col).alias(f"{prefix}EDT"))

            trt = period.get("treatment")
            if trt is not None:
                trt_target = f"TRT{n:02d}P"
                if trt in self._lazy.collect_schema().names():
                    exprs.append(pl.col(trt).alias(trt_target))
                else:
                    exprs.append(pl.lit(trt).alias(trt_target))

        return self._chain(*exprs)

                .last_date("TRTEDT", from_dataset=ex_sdtm,
                           date_col="EXENDTC")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    return self._date_agg(
        target,
        from_dataset=from_dataset,
        date_col=date_col,
        where=where,
        groups=groups,
        agg_fn="max",
    )

Derive target as the count of matching records in from_dataset.

Source code in src/fleet/adam/adsl_namespace.py 
def count_events(
    self,
    target: str,
    *,
    from_dataset: pl.DataFrame,
    where: str | pl.Expr | None = None,
    groups: list[str] | None = None,
) -> Self:
    """Derive *target* as the count of matching records in *from_dataset*.

    Returns 0 for subjects with no matching records (never null).

    Args:
        target: Name of the output count column.
        from_dataset: Source ``pl.DataFrame`` to count.
        where: Optional filter applied before counting.
        groups: Join key columns (default ``["USUBJID"]``).

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with *target* appended.

    Examples:
        Count total AE records per subject::

            adsl = (
                dm_raw.adam.adsl
                .count_events("NUMAE", from_dataset=ae_sdtm)
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    from fleet.sdtm.utils import parse_expression

    grps = groups or ["USUBJID"]
    src = from_dataset
    if where is not None:
        where_expr = where if isinstance(where, pl.Expr) else parse_expression(str(where))
        src = src.filter(where_expr)
    agg_df = src.group_by(grps).agg(pl.len().alias(target))
    df = self.to_frame().join(agg_df, on=grps, how="left")
    df = df.with_columns(pl.col(target).fill_null(0))
    return self._materialise_then(df)

Compute age in years from two date columns.

Uses (reference_date - birth_date) / 365.25 for a more precise calculation than unit-conversion from AGE. Null when either date is missing.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default target str

Name of the output column (default "AAGE").

'AAGE' birth_date str

Date-of-birth column (pl.Date).

'BRTHDT' reference_date str

Reference date column (pl.Date).

Decimal places to round to (default 1).

Name Type Description Self Self

The namespace with target appended.

Examples:

Derive age from birth and randomisation dates::

adsl = (
    dm_raw.adam.adsl

                    reference_date="RANDDT")

Source code in src/fleet/adam/adsl_namespace.py 
def age_from_dates(
    self,
    target: str = "AAGE",
    *,
    birth_date: str = "BRTHDT",
    reference_date: str = "TRTSDT",
    round_digits: int | None = 1,
) -> Self:
    """Compute age in years from two date columns.

    Uses ``(reference_date - birth_date) / 365.25`` for a more precise
    calculation than unit-conversion from ``AGE``.  Null when either
    date is missing.

    Args:
        target: Name of the output column (default ``"AAGE"``).
        birth_date: Date-of-birth column (``pl.Date``).
        reference_date: Reference date column (``pl.Date``).
        round_digits: Decimal places to round to (default ``1``).

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with *target* appended.

    Examples:
        Derive age from birth and randomisation dates::

            adsl = (
                dm_raw.adam.adsl
                .age_from_dates("AAGE", birth_date="BRTHDT",
                                reference_date="RANDDT")
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    days = (
        pl.col(reference_date).cast(pl.Date) - pl.col(birth_date).cast(pl.Date)
    ).dt.total_days()
    expr = days / 365.25
    if round_digits is not None:
        expr = expr.round(round_digits)
    return self._chain(expr.alias(target))

    dm_raw.adam.adsl

            {"number": 1, "start": "AP01SDT",
             "end": "AP01EDT", "treatment": "TRT01P"},

def derive_period(
    self,
    *,
    periods: list[dict[str, Any]],
) -> Self:
    """Create standard Subperiod / Phase variables.

    Generates ``AP{nn}SDT``, ``AP{nn}EDT``, and optionally
    ``TRT{nn:02d}P`` columns for each period.

    Args:
        periods: List of dicts each with ``"number"``, ``"start"``,
            ``"end"``, and optionally ``"treatment"``.

    Returns:
        Self: The namespace with period columns appended.

    Examples:
        Define two treatment periods::

            adsl = (
                dm_raw.adam.adsl
                .derive_period(
                    periods=[
                        {"number": 1, "start": "AP01SDT",
                         "end": "AP01EDT", "treatment": "TRT01P"},
                        {"number": 2, "start": "AP02SDT",
                         "end": "AP02EDT", "treatment": "TRT02P"},
                    ],
                )
                .to_frame()
            )
    """
    exprs: list[pl.Expr] = []
    for period in periods:
        n = period["number"]
        prefix = f"AP{n:02d}"
        sdt_col = period["start"]
        edt_col = period["end"]

        exprs.append(pl.col(sdt_col).alias(f"{prefix}SDT"))
        exprs.append(pl.col(edt_col).alias(f"{prefix}EDT"))

        trt = period.get("treatment")
        if trt is not None:
            trt_target = f"TRT{n:02d}P"
            if trt in self._lazy.collect_schema().names():
                exprs.append(pl.col(trt).alias(trt_target))
            else:
                exprs.append(pl.lit(trt).alias(trt_target))

    return self._chain(*exprs)

docs.title: Verb Cheat Sheet
docs.text:
This cheat sheet summarises the most common verbs across Fleet namespaces. Every verb name in this page is a clickable link to its docstring, rendered directly from the source code in the corresponding namespace page.

Single source of truth

Fleet's documentation is generated directly from Python docstrings via mkdocstrings and cross-linked with autorefs. The verb name you click here resolves to the exact method signature, parameters, and examples that the runtime executes — there is no separately maintained reference that can drift out of sync. Renaming a parameter in the source automatically updates this page on the next build.

docs.title: Core verbs (available everywhere)
docs.text: Verb Description Example .to_frame() Materialises the pipeline into a Polars DataFrame. Must be called at the end. .to_frame() .derivation() Injects an arbitrary Polars expression. .derivation("AGE", expression="pl.col('AGE_RAW').cast(pl.Int64)") .source() Passes a column through (renaming if from_col is provided). .source("USUBJID") .assigned() Hardcodes a constant literal for all rows. .assigned("DOMAIN", value="DM") .inspect() Hard checkpoint — materialises and prints schema/shape/head. .inspect("after rename") .explain() Prints the Polars query plan without materialising. .explain()

docs.title: How linking works
docs.text:
Click any verb name in the tables above. Your browser navigates to the corresponding namespace API page and scrolls to the auto-generated heading anchor for that method — a heading rendered live from the Python docstring.

This means:

  1. Parameter accuracy — the cheat sheet links never describe a parameter that doesn't exist in code.
  2. Examples stay current — code samples in docstrings are the same ones the test suite exercises.
  3. Discoverability — IDE hover, docs site, and help() in a REPL all read from the same docstring.

If you find a verb missing from this cheat sheet, file an issue or add a row — the link target itself is generated automatically once the method exists in source.

docs.title: Study Codelists (CDISCPILOT01)
docs.text:
This page documents the auto-generated codelist module that ships with the CDISCPILOT01 example study (examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/codelists.py). It is generated from the CDISC Library by CodelistGenerator and is regenerated whenever a new domain is added.

One source of truth — three audiences served

The same Python module powers:

- **IDE auto-completion** for programmers writing pipelines (`SEX.M`, `RACE.WHITE`).
- **Live runtime validation** through [`assign_ct`][fleet.sdtm.SDTMNamespace.assign_ct]
  and [`hardcode_ct`][fleet.sdtm.SDTMNamespace.hardcode_ct].
- **Direct hyperlinks to the CDISC Library Browser** for reviewers and auditors,
  via the `_cdisc_url` attribute on every codelist class.

No separate spreadsheet, no copy-pasted concept IDs, no drift between code and CT.

docs.title: In a standalone study project (recommended)
docs.text:
When your study lives in its own directory with a study_config.yaml, use import_codelists() to load the generated module without sys.path hacks:

from fleet.ct import import_codelists

# Auto-discovers codelists.py via study_config.yaml in CWD
ct = import_codelists()

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign_ct("SEX", source="sex", ct_codelist=ct.SEX)
    .assign_ct("RACE", source="race", ct_codelist=ct.RACE)
    .hardcode_ct("AGEU", value="YEARS", ct_codelist=ct.AGEU)
    .to_frame()
)

Or register the module so bare from codelists import ... works:

from fleet.ct import import_codelists

import_codelists()  # registers 'codelists' in sys.modules
from codelists import SEX, RACE, AGEU  # now works everywhere in the session

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign_ct("SEX", source="sex", ct_codelist=SEX)
    .assign_ct("RACE", source="race", ct_codelist=RACE)
    .hardcode_ct("AGEU", value="YEARS", ct_codelist=AGEU)
    .to_frame()
)

You can also pass an explicit path if your codelists file lives somewhere non-standard:

ct = import_codelists("path/to/my_codelists.py")

docs.title: Within the Fleet repo (example studies)
docs.text:
from examples.cdiscpilot01.sdtm.codelists import SEX, RACE, AGEU

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign_ct("SEX", source="sex", ct_codelist=SEX)
    .assign_ct("RACE", source="race", ct_codelist=RACE)
    .hardcode_ct("AGEU", value="YEARS", ct_codelist=AGEU)
    .to_frame()
)

Each codelist class exposes:

Attribute Description _concept_id NCI concept ID (e.g. "C66731"). _cdisc_url Deep link to the CDISC Library Browser entry. _preferred_term Preferred term as published by CDISC (when include_docs=True). <TERM> One class attribute per submission value (SEX.M, SEX.F, …).

docs.text:
FRM (C66726).

The form of the completed pharmaceutical product, e.g. tablet, capsule,

injection, elixir, suppository. Dosage form can have a significant effect on the onset, duration and intensity of the pharmacological action of a drug. A pharmaceutical dosage form controls the rate at which the drug is released into the biological fluids. This release rate affects its intrinsic absorption pattern and therefore, the bioavailability of the drug.

class StudyContext:
    """Runtime context that resolves configured study paths."""

    def __init__(self, study_root: Path, config: StudyConfig) -> None:
        self.study_root = study_root
        self.config = config

    @property
    def study_id(self) -> str:
        return self.config.study_id

    def resolve(self, relative_path: str) -> Path:
        """Resolve a configured relative path under study root."""
        return (self.study_root / relative_path).resolve()

    @property
    def raw_data_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.resolve(self.config.paths.raw_data)

    @property
    def sdtm_data_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.resolve(self.config.paths.sdtm_data)

    @property
    def adam_data_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.resolve(self.config.paths.adam_data)

    @property
    def metadata_sdtm_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.resolve(self.config.paths.metadata_sdtm)

    @property
    def metadata_adam_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.resolve(self.config.paths.metadata_adam)

    @property
    def define_xml_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.resolve(self.config.paths.define_xml)

    @property
    def outputs_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.resolve(self.config.paths.outputs)

    @property
    def programs_sdtm_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.resolve(self.config.paths.programs_sdtm)

    @property
    def programs_adam_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.resolve(self.config.paths.programs_adam)

    @property
    def programs_tlg_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.resolve(self.config.paths.programs_tlg)

    @property
    def rules_sdtm_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.resolve(self.config.paths.rules_sdtm)

    @property
    def rules_adam_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.resolve(self.config.paths.rules_adam)

    @property
    def programs_misc_dir(self) -> Path:
        return self.resolve(self.config.paths.programs_misc)

    @property
    def codelists_file(self) -> Path:
        """Resolve the generated codelists.py path (inside SDTM metadata dir)."""
        return self.metadata_sdtm_dir / "codelists.py"

    @property
    def custom_rules_dir(self) -> Path | None:
        """Resolve the custom validation rules directory, or None if not configured."""
        if self.config.validation.custom_rules is None:
            return None
        return self.resolve(self.config.validation.custom_rules)

    def raw_file(self, file_name: str) -> Path:
        return self.raw_data_dir / file_name

    def sdtm_file(self, file_name: str) -> Path:
        return self.sdtm_data_dir / file_name

    def adam_file(self, file_name: str) -> Path:
        return self.adam_data_dir / file_name

    def sdtm_spec(self, file_name: str) -> Path:
        return self.metadata_sdtm_dir / file_name

    def adam_spec(self, file_name: str) -> Path:
        return self.metadata_adam_dir / file_name

    def define_yaml(self, file_name: str = "define.yaml") -> Path:
        return self.define_xml_dir / file_name

    def define_schema(self, file_name: str = "define_xml_2_1_schema.json") -> Path:
        return self.define_xml_dir / file_name

    @classmethod
    def init(
        cls,
        study_root: str | Path,
        study_id: str,
        company: str | None = None,
        protocol_name: str | None = None,
        description: str = "",
        paths: "StudyPathConfig | None" = None,
        sdtm: "SDTMConfig | None" = None,
        adam: "ADAMConfig | None" = None,
        ct: "CTConfig | None" = None,
        validation: "ValidationConfig | None" = None,
    ) -> "StudyContext":
        """Scaffold a new study workspace and return a ready-to-use StudyContext.

        Creates the directory layout defined by StudyPathConfig and writes
        ``study_config.yaml``.  Define specs and codelists are created by
        subsequent pipeline steps (``fleet init define``, ``fleet init ct``).

        Directories are created silently if they already exist.  If
        ``study_config.yaml`` already exists the method raises
        ``StudyConfigError`` to protect in-progress work.

        Args:
            study_root: Root directory for the study (created if absent).
            study_id:   Study identifier (e.g. ``"STUDY01"``).
            company:    Optional originator / company name.
            protocol_name: Optional protocol identifier.
            description: Optional study description.
            paths:      Custom path config; defaults to ``StudyPathConfig`` defaults.
            sdtm:       SDTM IG configuration (version, domains).
            adam:        ADaM IG configuration (version, datasets).
            ct:         CT package configuration.
            validation: Validation engine configuration (engine path, custom rules).

        Returns:
            Initialized ``StudyContext`` pointing at the new workspace.

        Raises:
            StudyConfigError: If ``study_config.yaml`` already exists.
        """
        study_root = Path(study_root).resolve()
        config = StudyConfig(
            study_id=study_id,
            company=company,
            protocol_name=protocol_name,
            description=description,
            paths=paths or StudyPathConfig(),
            sdtm=sdtm or SDTMConfig(),
            adam=adam or ADAMConfig(),
            ct=ct or CTConfig(),
            validation=validation or ValidationConfig(),
        )
        ctx = cls(study_root=study_root, config=config)

        # ── Guard: refuse to overwrite existing config ────────────────────
        config_file = study_root / "study_config.yaml"
        if config_file.exists():
            raise StudyConfigError(
                f"Study already initialized — '{config_file}' already exists. "
                "Use load_study_context() to load an existing study."
            )

        # ── Create directory tree (idempotent) ────────────────────────────
        for dir_path in (
            ctx.raw_data_dir,
            ctx.sdtm_data_dir,
            ctx.adam_data_dir,
            ctx.metadata_sdtm_dir,
            ctx.metadata_adam_dir,
            ctx.define_xml_dir,
            ctx.outputs_dir,
            ctx.rules_sdtm_dir,
            ctx.rules_adam_dir,
            ctx.programs_sdtm_dir,
            ctx.programs_adam_dir,
            ctx.programs_tlg_dir,
            ctx.programs_misc_dir,
        ):
            dir_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        # ── Create derivations package stub ──────────────────────────────
        derivations_dir = ctx.programs_adam_dir.parent / "derivations"
        derivations_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        derivations_init = derivations_dir / "__init__.py"
        if not derivations_init.exists():
            derivations_init.write_text(
                "# Auto-generated by fleet init cfg.\n"
                "# Import study-specific derivations here so they are auto-registered.\n",
                encoding="utf-8",
            )

        # ── Write study_config.yaml ───────────────────────────────────────
        config_data = config.model_dump(exclude_none=True)
        # Drop empty defaults to keep the file lean
        if not config_data.get("description"):
            config_data.pop("description", None)
        config_file.write_text(
            yaml.dump(config_data, default_flow_style=False, allow_unicode=True, sort_keys=False),
            encoding="utf-8",
        )

        return ctx

def load_study_context(config_path: Path) -> StudyContext:
    """Load study configuration and return a resolved context.

    Args:
        config_path: Path to study_config.yaml

    Returns:
        StudyContext with resolved paths

    Raises:
        StudyConfigError: If the config file is missing or invalid
    """
    if not config_path.exists():
        raise StudyConfigError(f"Study configuration file not found: {config_path}")

    try:
        with open(config_path) as f:
            config_data = yaml.safe_load(f) or {}
    except yaml.YAMLError as e:
        raise StudyConfigError(f"Invalid YAML in study configuration: {e}") from e

    try:
        config = StudyConfig(**config_data)
    except Exception as e:
        raise StudyConfigError(f"Invalid study configuration schema: {e}") from e

    return StudyContext(study_root=config_path.parent, config=config)

@dataclass
class PipelineDAG:
    """Directed Acyclic Graph of pipeline dataset dependencies.

    Build with :func:`build_dag` rather than constructing directly.
    """

    nodes: dict[str, PipelineNode] = field(default_factory=dict)

    # ── queries ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #

    def execution_order(self) -> list[str]:
        """Return all node names in a safe topological execution order.

        Uses Kahn's algorithm (BFS on in-degree).

        Raises
        ------
        ValueError
            If the graph contains a cycle (should have been caught by
            :func:`build_dag`, but re-checked here for safety).
        """
        in_degree: dict[str, int] = {n: 0 for n in self.nodes}
        for node in self.nodes.values():
            for upstream in node.inputs:
                if upstream in in_degree:
                    in_degree[node.name] += 1

        queue: deque[str] = deque(n for n, deg in in_degree.items() if deg == 0)
        order: list[str] = []

        while queue:
            n = queue.popleft()
            order.append(n)
            for downstream in self._downstream(n):
                in_degree[downstream] -= 1
                if in_degree[downstream] == 0:
                    queue.append(downstream)

        if len(order) != len(self.nodes):
            raise ValueError("DAG contains a cycle — cannot produce a linear execution order.")

        return order

    def impacted_by(self, name: str) -> list[str]:
        """Return all nodes that must be rerun when *name* changes.

        Performs a BFS downstream from *name*, then returns the results
        in topological execution order so callers get a ready-made run
        schedule.

        Parameters
        ----------
        name:
            Logical node name (dataset or raw source) that changed.

        Returns
        -------
        list[str]
            Topologically-ordered list of node names to rerun, inclusive
            of *name* itself.

        Raises
        ------
        KeyError
            If *name* is not a node in this DAG.
        """
        if name not in self.nodes:
            raise KeyError(f"Node '{name}' not found in DAG. Available nodes: {sorted(self.nodes)}")

        visited: set[str] = set()
        queue: deque[str] = deque([name])
        while queue:
            n = queue.popleft()
            if n in visited:
                continue
            visited.add(n)
            queue.extend(self._downstream(n))

        return [n for n in self.execution_order() if n in visited]

    def _downstream(self, name: str) -> list[str]:
        """Direct downstream dependents of *name* (nodes that list it in inputs)."""
        return [n.name for n in self.nodes.values() if name in n.inputs]

    # ── lineage injection ───────────────────────────────────────────────── #

    def inject_lineage(self, namespace: Any, dataset_name: str) -> None:
        """Merge variable-level and pin lineage from *namespace* into the DAG.

        Populates ``variables`` on the node named *dataset_name* and, for
        each ``PinDependency``, adds the pinned source domain to the
        node's ``inputs`` if it is not already present (creating the
        cross-domain edge in the DAG).

        Args:
            namespace: A namespace instance with ``_lineage`` and
                optionally ``_pin_lineage`` attributes.
            dataset_name: The logical node name to attach lineage to.
        """
        node = self.nodes.get(dataset_name)
        if node is None:
            return

        from fleet.core.lineage import lineage_of, pin_lineage_of

        # Merge intra-frame variable lineage
        for vnode in lineage_of(namespace):
            node.variables[vnode.name] = vnode

        # Merge pin lineage → enrich variable nodes + add DAG edges
        for pdep in pin_lineage_of(namespace):
            if pdep.target_col in node.variables:
                vnode = node.variables[pdep.target_col]
                vnode.pin_sources.append(pdep)
            # Ensure the source domain is an input edge
            if pdep.source_domain in self.nodes and pdep.source_domain not in node.inputs:
                node.inputs.append(pdep.source_domain)

    def trace(self, dataset: str, variable: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        """Return full provenance chain for a single variable.

        Follows both intra-frame sources and cross-domain pin sources.

        Args:
            dataset: Logical node name (e.g. ``"AE"``).
            variable: Column name (e.g. ``"AESTDY"``).

        Returns:
            list[dict]: Ordered provenance entries from output back to
                source, each with ``name``, ``verb``, ``sources``,
                and optional ``pin_sources``.
        """
        node = self.nodes.get(dataset)
        if node is None:
            return []
        vnode = node.variables.get(variable)
        if vnode is None:
            return []
        chain: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
            {
                "name": vnode.name,
                "verb": vnode.verb,
                "sources": vnode.sources,
                "domain": vnode.domain,
                "pin_sources": [
                    {
                        "source_domain": p.source_domain,
                        "source_cols": p.source_cols,
                        "join_key": p.join_key,
                        "relationship": p.relationship,
                    }
                    for p in vnode.pin_sources
                ],
            }
        ]
        return chain

    # ── export ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── #

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        """Return a JSON-serializable adjacency representation.

        Shape::

            {
              "dm_raw": {"node_type": "raw",  "path": "datasets/.../dm_raw.csv", "inputs": []},
              "DM":     {"node_type": "sdtm", "path": "outputs/.../dm.parquet",  "inputs": ["dm_raw"]},
              "ADSL":   {"node_type": "adam", "path": "outputs/.../adsl.parquet","inputs": ["DM"]},
              ...
            }
        """
        return {
            name: {
                "node_type": node.node_type,
                "path": node.path,
                "inputs": node.inputs,
                **(
                    {
                        "variables": {
                            v.name: {
                                "verb": v.verb,
                                "sources": v.sources,
                                "method": v.method,
                                "cdisc_ref": v.cdisc_ref,
                                **(
                                    {
                                        "pin_sources": [
                                            {
                                                "source_domain": p.source_domain,
                                                "source_cols": p.source_cols,
                                                "join_key": p.join_key,
                                                "relationship": p.relationship,
                                            }
                                            for p in v.pin_sources
                                        ]
                                    }
                                    if v.pin_sources
                                    else {}
                                ),
                            }
                            for v in node.variables.values()
                        }
                    }
                    if node.variables
                    else {}
                ),
            }
            for name, node in self.nodes.items()
        }

    def to_snakemake(self) -> dict:
        """Return a Snakemake-compatible rule dict.

        Each entry maps a logical name to ``{"input": [...paths...], "output": path}``.
        Drop this into a Snakefile generator to produce concrete rules::

            for name, rule in dag.to_snakemake().items():
                # rule["input"]  → list of input file paths
                # rule["output"] → output file path

        Raw nodes are included with an empty ``input`` list and the source
        file as ``output``, so Snakemake can model them as source checkpoints.
        """
        rules: dict[str, dict] = {}
        for name, node in self.nodes.items():
            input_paths: list[str] = []
            for upstream_name in node.inputs:
                upstream = self.nodes.get(upstream_name)
                if upstream and upstream.path:
                    input_paths.append(upstream.path)
                else:
                    input_paths.append(upstream_name)
            rules[name] = {
                "input": input_paths,
                "output": node.path,
                "node_type": node.node_type,
            }
        return rules

    def to_airflow(self) -> dict:
        """Return an Airflow-compatible task dependency dict.

        Shape::

            {
              "DM":   [],           # no upstream tasks
              "ADSL": ["DM"],
              "ADVS": ["VS", "ADSL"],
            }

        Wire operators in a DAG file with::

            for task_id, upstreams in dag.to_airflow().items():
                for u in upstreams:
                    tasks[u] >> tasks[task_id]
        """
        return {name: list(node.inputs) for name, node in self.nodes.items()}

    def generate(self, output_path: str | Path) -> None:
        """Write the DAG to *output_path* as a JSON file.

        The file contains the full adjacency representation produced by
        :meth:`to_dict` plus the topological execution order, so it is
        self-contained and can be consumed by external tools without needing
        to re-parse the define YAMLs.

        Parameters
        ----------
        output_path:
            Destination path for the ``.json`` file (e.g.
            ``outputs/cdiscpilot01/pipeline_dag.json``).

        Example
        -------
        ::

            dag = build_dag(
                "examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/define.yaml",
                "examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/define.yaml",
                output_dir="outputs/cdiscpilot01",
            )
            dag.generate("outputs/cdiscpilot01/pipeline_dag.json")
        """
        import json

        out = Path(output_path)
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        payload = {
            "execution_order": self.execution_order(),
            "nodes": self.to_dict(),

Uses Kahn's algorithm (BFS on in-degree).

def execution_order(self) -> list[str]:
    """Return all node names in a safe topological execution order.

    Uses Kahn's algorithm (BFS on in-degree).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the graph contains a cycle (should have been caught by
        :func:`build_dag`, but re-checked here for safety).
    """
    in_degree: dict[str, int] = {n: 0 for n in self.nodes}
    for node in self.nodes.values():
        for upstream in node.inputs:
            if upstream in in_degree:
                in_degree[node.name] += 1

    queue: deque[str] = deque(n for n, deg in in_degree.items() if deg == 0)
    order: list[str] = []

    while queue:
        n = queue.popleft()
        order.append(n)
        for downstream in self._downstream(n):
            in_degree[downstream] -= 1
            if in_degree[downstream] == 0:
                queue.append(downstream)

    if len(order) != len(self.nodes):
        raise ValueError("DAG contains a cycle — cannot produce a linear execution order.")

    return order

def impacted_by(self, name: str) -> list[str]:
    """Return all nodes that must be rerun when *name* changes.

    Performs a BFS downstream from *name*, then returns the results
    in topological execution order so callers get a ready-made run
    schedule.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name:
        Logical node name (dataset or raw source) that changed.

    Returns
    -------
    list[str]
        Topologically-ordered list of node names to rerun, inclusive
        of *name* itself.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError
        If *name* is not a node in this DAG.
    """
    if name not in self.nodes:
        raise KeyError(f"Node '{name}' not found in DAG. Available nodes: {sorted(self.nodes)}")

    visited: set[str] = set()
    queue: deque[str] = deque([name])
    while queue:
        n = queue.popleft()
        if n in visited:
            continue
        visited.add(n)
        queue.extend(self._downstream(n))

    return [n for n in self.execution_order() if n in visited]

Populates variables on the node named dataset_name and, for each PinDependency, adds the pinned source domain to the node's inputs if it is not already present (creating the cross-domain edge in the DAG).

def inject_lineage(self, namespace: Any, dataset_name: str) -> None:
    """Merge variable-level and pin lineage from *namespace* into the DAG.

    Populates ``variables`` on the node named *dataset_name* and, for
    each ``PinDependency``, adds the pinned source domain to the
    node's ``inputs`` if it is not already present (creating the
    cross-domain edge in the DAG).

    Args:
        namespace: A namespace instance with ``_lineage`` and
            optionally ``_pin_lineage`` attributes.
        dataset_name: The logical node name to attach lineage to.
    """
    node = self.nodes.get(dataset_name)
    if node is None:
        return

    from fleet.core.lineage import lineage_of, pin_lineage_of

    # Merge intra-frame variable lineage
    for vnode in lineage_of(namespace):
        node.variables[vnode.name] = vnode

    # Merge pin lineage → enrich variable nodes + add DAG edges
    for pdep in pin_lineage_of(namespace):
        if pdep.target_col in node.variables:
            vnode = node.variables[pdep.target_col]
            vnode.pin_sources.append(pdep)
        # Ensure the source domain is an input edge
        if pdep.source_domain in self.nodes and pdep.source_domain not in node.inputs:
            node.inputs.append(pdep.source_domain)

def trace(self, dataset: str, variable: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return full provenance chain for a single variable.

    Follows both intra-frame sources and cross-domain pin sources.

    Args:
        dataset: Logical node name (e.g. ``"AE"``).
        variable: Column name (e.g. ``"AESTDY"``).

    Returns:
        list[dict]: Ordered provenance entries from output back to
            source, each with ``name``, ``verb``, ``sources``,
            and optional ``pin_sources``.
    """
    node = self.nodes.get(dataset)
    if node is None:
        return []
    vnode = node.variables.get(variable)
    if vnode is None:
        return []
    chain: list[dict[str, Any]] = [
        {
            "name": vnode.name,
            "verb": vnode.verb,
            "sources": vnode.sources,
            "domain": vnode.domain,
            "pin_sources": [
                {
                    "source_domain": p.source_domain,
                    "source_cols": p.source_cols,
                    "join_key": p.join_key,
                    "relationship": p.relationship,
                }
                for p in vnode.pin_sources
            ],
        }
    ]
    return chain

def to_dict(self) -> dict:
    """Return a JSON-serializable adjacency representation.

    Shape::

        {
          "dm_raw": {"node_type": "raw",  "path": "datasets/.../dm_raw.csv", "inputs": []},
          "DM":     {"node_type": "sdtm", "path": "outputs/.../dm.parquet",  "inputs": ["dm_raw"]},
          "ADSL":   {"node_type": "adam", "path": "outputs/.../adsl.parquet","inputs": ["DM"]},
          ...
        }
    """
    return {
        name: {
            "node_type": node.node_type,
            "path": node.path,
            "inputs": node.inputs,
            **(
                {
                    "variables": {
                        v.name: {
                            "verb": v.verb,
                            "sources": v.sources,
                            "method": v.method,
                            "cdisc_ref": v.cdisc_ref,
                            **(
                                {
                                    "pin_sources": [
                                        {
                                            "source_domain": p.source_domain,
                                            "source_cols": p.source_cols,
                                            "join_key": p.join_key,
                                            "relationship": p.relationship,
                                        }
                                        for p in v.pin_sources
                                    ]
                                }
                                if v.pin_sources
                                else {}
                            ),
                        }
                        for v in node.variables.values()
                    }
                }
                if node.variables
                else {}
            ),
        }
        for name, node in self.nodes.items()
    }

def to_snakemake(self) -> dict:
    """Return a Snakemake-compatible rule dict.

    Each entry maps a logical name to ``{"input": [...paths...], "output": path}``.
    Drop this into a Snakefile generator to produce concrete rules::

        for name, rule in dag.to_snakemake().items():
            # rule["input"]  → list of input file paths
            # rule["output"] → output file path

    Raw nodes are included with an empty ``input`` list and the source
    file as ``output``, so Snakemake can model them as source checkpoints.
    """
    rules: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for name, node in self.nodes.items():
        input_paths: list[str] = []
        for upstream_name in node.inputs:
            upstream = self.nodes.get(upstream_name)
            if upstream and upstream.path:
                input_paths.append(upstream.path)
            else:
                input_paths.append(upstream_name)
        rules[name] = {
            "input": input_paths,
            "output": node.path,
            "node_type": node.node_type,
        }
    return rules

def to_airflow(self) -> dict:
    """Return an Airflow-compatible task dependency dict.

    Shape::

        {
          "DM":   [],           # no upstream tasks
          "ADSL": ["DM"],
          "ADVS": ["VS", "ADSL"],
        }

    Wire operators in a DAG file with::

        for task_id, upstreams in dag.to_airflow().items():
            for u in upstreams:
                tasks[u] >> tasks[task_id]
    """
    return {name: list(node.inputs) for name, node in self.nodes.items()}
