@dataclass
class CDISCClientConfig:
    """Configuration for the CDISC Library API client.

    Values are resolved in order:
    1. Explicit constructor arguments.
    2. Environment variables (``CDISC_API_KEY``, ``CDISC_BASE_URL``).
    3. A ``.env`` file in the working directory (loaded lazily via *dotenv*
       if the ``python-dotenv`` package is installed).

    Args:
        api_key: CDISC Library API key.
        base_url: Root URL for the CDISC Library API.
    """

    api_key: str = ""
    base_url: str = _DEFAULT_BASE_URL

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if not self.api_key:
            _try_load_dotenv()
            self.api_key = os.environ.get("CDISC_API_KEY", "")
        if self.base_url == _DEFAULT_BASE_URL:
            env_url = os.environ.get("CDISC_BASE_URL", "")
            if env_url:
                self.base_url = env_url.rstrip("/")

docs.title: Codelist Code Generator
docs.text: The CodelistGenerator converts CDISC Library JSON responses into a Python module containing typed classes — one per codelist — with human-readable aliases and IDE auto-completion support.

docs.title: Recommended workflow
docs.text:
# Bootstrap from the SDTM IG (source of truth)
fleet init-ct --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --output specs/my_study/sdtm/codelists.py

# Add domains later (preserves existing codelists)
fleet add-ct --domains LB,CM --output specs/my_study/sdtm/codelists.py

docs.title: Programmatic usage
docs.text:
from fleet.ct.api import CDISCClient
from fleet.ct.generator import CodelistGenerator

with CDISCClient() as client:
    # Recommended: derive codelists from the SDTM IG
    gen = CodelistGenerator.from_sdtm_ig(
        client,
        domains=["DM", "AE", "VS", "EX"],
        package="sdtmct-2025-09-26",
    )
    gen.write("specs/my_study/sdtm/codelists.py")

docs.title: Generated output
docs.text:
The generated codelists.py contains:

  • One class per codelist with _concept_id, _cdisc_url, and submission-value constants:
class C66731:
    """SEX (C66731).

    The assemblage of physical properties or qualities by which male is
    distinguished from female.

    See: https://library.cdisc.org/browser/#/codelist/C66731
    """

    _concept_id = "C66731"
    _cdisc_url = "https://library.cdisc.org/browser/#/codelist/C66731"
    F = "F"
    M = "M"
    U = "U"

!!! tip "Direct line to the source of truth" The _cdisc_url attribute and the See: line in each docstring point to the codelist's entry in the CDISC Library Browser. When a reviewer or auditor reads pipeline code, hovering SEX in an IDE shows the URL; clicking the link in the docs site takes them straight to the authoritative CDISC definition. There is no separate lookup table to maintain — the URL is constructed from the NCI concept ID at generation time.

  • Human-readable aliases derived from the CDISC submission value:
SEX = C66731
RACE = C74457
  • __all__ for clean wildcard imports:
from codelists import SEX, RACE

# or
from codelists import *

docs.title: Importing codelists in standalone study projects
docs.text:
When your study lives in its own directory (not inside the Fleet repo), the generated codelists.py isn't on the Python path by default. Use import_codelists() to load it dynamically:

from fleet.ct import import_codelists

# Strategy 1: auto-discover via study_config.yaml in CWD
ct = import_codelists()
SEX = ct.SEX

# Strategy 2: register in sys.modules so bare imports work
import_codelists()  # one-time call
from codelists import SEX, RACE  # works for the rest of the session

# Strategy 3: explicit path (non-standard locations)
ct = import_codelists("/absolute/path/to/codelists.py")

Resolution order

When called without arguments, import_codelists() resolves the file as follows:

  1. study_config.yaml in CWD → reads paths.metadata_sdtm → appends /codelists.py
  2. Falls back to <CWD>/metadata/sdtm/codelists.py

This means cd-ing into your study root before running a script is all you need.

docs.title: Using generated codelists in pipelines
docs.text:
from fleet.ct import import_codelists

ct = import_codelists()

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign_ct("SEX", source="sex", ct_codelist=ct.SEX)
    .assign_ct("RACE", source="race", ct_codelist=ct.RACE)
    .to_frame()
)

assign_ct accepts either a codelist class (SEX) or a raw NCI concept ID string ("C66731"). The class form is preferred for readability and auto-completion.

@dataclass
class CodelistGenerator:
    """Accumulates CDISC codelist JSON responses and renders them as Python.

    Args:
        include_docs: If ``True`` (default), inject ``definition`` and
            ``preferredTerm`` from the CDISC JSON into class/attribute
            docstrings for richer AI context.
        cdisc_url_template: URL template used to build the
            ``_cdisc_url`` class attribute and the ``See:`` reference in
            each codelist's docstring.  Substitution fields available:
            ``{concept_id}``, ``{package}`` (e.g. ``sdtmct-2024-12-13``),
            and ``{date}`` (the package date suffix).  Defaults to the
            CDISC Library Browser deep link, which requires all three.
    """

    include_docs: bool = True
    cdisc_url_template: str = (
        "https://library.cdisc.org/browser/#/mdr/ct/{date}/packages/"
        "{package}/codelists/{concept_id}"
    )
    _codelists: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list, init=False)

    def add_codelist(
        self,
        codelist_json: dict[str, Any],
        *,
        package: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Register a raw CDISC Library codelist JSON response.

        Args:
            codelist_json: Dict returned by ``CDISCClient.get_codelist``.
                Must contain at least ``conceptId`` and ``terms``.
            package: Optional CT package the codelist was fetched from
                (e.g. ``"sdtmct-2024-12-13"``).  Stored on the codelist
                dict as ``_package`` so the rendered ``_cdisc_url`` can
                include the correct package + date context required by
                the CDISC Library Browser.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If required keys are missing.
        """
        if "conceptId" not in codelist_json:
            raise ValueError("codelist JSON must contain 'conceptId'")
        if package is not None:
            codelist_json = {**codelist_json, "_package": package}
        self._codelists.append(codelist_json)

    @property
    def concept_ids(self) -> set[str]:
        """Return the set of concept IDs already loaded."""
        return {cl["conceptId"] for cl in self._codelists}

    @classmethod
    def from_concept_ids(
        cls,
        client: CDISCClient,
        concept_ids: set[str],
        *,
        package: str = "sdtmct-2023-12-15",
        include_docs: bool = True,
    ) -> CodelistGenerator:
        """Build a generator from an explicit set of NCI concept IDs.

        Args:
            client: An authenticated ``CDISCClient`` instance.
            concept_ids: Set of NCI concept ID strings to download.
            package: CT package version to download from.
            include_docs: Whether to include definitions in generated output.

        Returns:
            A ``CodelistGenerator`` populated with the requested codelists.

        Examples:
            Generate codelists for specific concept IDs::

                from fleet.ct.api import CDISCClient
                from fleet.ct.generator import CodelistGenerator

                with CDISCClient() as client:
                    gen = CodelistGenerator.from_concept_ids(
                        client,
                        {"C66731", "C74457"},
                    )
                    gen.write("codelists.py")
        """
        gen = cls(include_docs=include_docs)
        for cid in sorted(concept_ids):
            try:
                gen.add_codelist(
                    client.get_codelist(cid, package=package),
                    package=package,
                )
            except Exception:
                logger.warning(
                    "Codelist %s not found in package %s — skipping.",
                    cid,
                    package,
                )
        return gen

    @classmethod
    def from_sdtm_ig(
        cls,
        client: CDISCClient,
        domains: list[str],
        *,
        ig_version: str = "3-4",
        package: str = "sdtmct-2023-12-15",
        include_docs: bool = True,
    ) -> CodelistGenerator:
        """Build a generator from the SDTM IG — the authoritative source of truth.

        Queries the CDISC Library for the specified SDTM IG version,
        extracts every codelist referenced by variables in the requested
        domains, and downloads the corresponding CT definitions.

        Args:
            client: An authenticated ``CDISCClient`` instance.
            domains: List of SDTM domain abbreviations to include
                (e.g. ``["DM", "AE", "VS", "EX"]``).
            ig_version: SDTM IG version (default ``"3-4"``).
            package: CT package version to download terms from.
            include_docs: Whether to include definitions in generated output.

        Returns:
            A ``CodelistGenerator`` populated with all referenced codelists.

        Examples:
            Generate codelists for DM and AE from SDTM IG 3.4::

                from fleet.ct.api import CDISCClient
                from fleet.ct.generator import CodelistGenerator

                with CDISCClient() as client:
                    gen = CodelistGenerator.from_sdtm_ig(
                        client,
                        domains=["DM", "AE", "VS", "EX"],
                    )
                    gen.write("examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/codelists.py")
        """
        concept_ids = extract_ig_concept_ids(client, ig_version, domains)
        return cls.from_concept_ids(
            client,
            concept_ids,
            package=package,
            include_docs=include_docs,
        )

    def render(self) -> str:
        """Render accumulated codelists as a Python module string.

        Returns:
            A complete, syntactically valid Python source string.
        """
        sorted_cls = sorted(self._codelists, key=lambda c: c["conceptId"])

        lines: list[str] = [
            '"""Auto-generated CDISC Controlled Terminology constants.',
            "",
            "Do not edit manually — regenerate with ``fleet.ct.generator``.",
            '"""',
            "",
        ]

        # Class definitions
        for cl in sorted_cls:
            lines.extend(self._render_class(cl))
            lines.append("")

        # Human-readable aliases  (e.g.  SEX = C66731)
        aliases: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        for cl in sorted_cls:
            concept_id = cl["conceptId"]
            class_name = _safe_identifier(concept_id)
            alias = self._alias_for(cl)
            if alias and alias != class_name:
                aliases.append((alias, class_name))

        if aliases:
            lines.append("")
            lines.append("# Human-readable aliases")
            for alias, class_name in sorted(aliases):
                lines.append(f"{alias} = {class_name}")
            lines.append("")

        # __all__
        all_names: list[str] = [_safe_identifier(cl["conceptId"]) for cl in sorted_cls]
        all_names.extend(alias for alias, _ in sorted(aliases))
        all_names.sort()
        all_repr = ", ".join(f'"{n}"' for n in all_names)
        lines.append(f"__all__ = [{all_repr}]")
        lines.append("")

        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

    def write(self, path: str | Path) -> Path:
        """Render and write the module to *path*.

        Parent directories are created if they do not exist.

        Args:
            path: Destination file path.

        Returns:
            Resolved ``Path`` of the written file.
        """
        dest = Path(path)
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        dest.write_text(self.render(), encoding="utf-8")
        return dest.resolve()

    # -- private -------------------------------------------------------- #

    def _render_class(self, cl: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
        concept_id: str = cl["conceptId"]
        class_name = _safe_identifier(concept_id)
        submission_value: str = cl.get("submissionValue", concept_id)
        preferred_term: str = cl.get("preferredTerm", "")
        definition: str = cl.get("definition", "")
        cdisc_url: str | None = self._build_cdisc_url(cl)

        # Class docstring
        doc_parts = [f"{submission_value} ({concept_id})."]
        if self.include_docs and definition:
            doc_parts.append("")
            doc_parts.append(textwrap.fill(definition, width=76))
        # Always add the CDISC Library reference so reviewers can jump from
        # generated code to the authoritative source-of-truth definition.
        if cdisc_url:
            doc_parts.append("")
            doc_parts.append(f"See: {cdisc_url}")

        class_doc = "\n    ".join(doc_parts)
        lines = [
            f"class {class_name}:",
            f'    """{class_doc}"""',
            "",
            f"    _concept_id = {concept_id!r}",
        ]
        if cdisc_url:
            lines.append(f"    _cdisc_url = {cdisc_url!r}")

        if self.include_docs and preferred_term:
            lines.append(f"    _preferred_term = {preferred_term!r}")
        lines.append("")

        terms: list[dict[str, Any]] = cl.get("terms", [])
        if not terms:
            lines.append("    pass")
            return lines

        for term in sorted(terms, key=lambda t: t.get("submissionValue", "")):
            sv: str = term.get("submissionValue", "")
            if not sv:
                continue
            attr = _safe_identifier(sv)
            lines.append(f"    {attr} = {sv!r}")

            if self.include_docs:
                term_def = term.get("definition", "")
                if term_def:
                    comment = textwrap.shorten(term_def, width=72)
                    lines.append(f"    # {comment}")

        return lines

    def _build_cdisc_url(self, cl: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
        """Format the CDISC Library Browser URL for *cl*.

        Returns ``None`` when the template requires a ``{package}`` or
        ``{date}`` field but no package was recorded for this codelist
        (e.g. when ``add_codelist`` was called without ``package=``).
        """
        concept_id: str = cl["conceptId"]
        package: str | None = cl.get("_package")
        date: str | None = None
        if package and "-" in package:
            # e.g. "sdtmct-2024-12-13" -> "2024-12-13"
            _, _, date = package.partition("-")
        # If the template needs package/date context but none was
        # recorded, skip the URL rather than emit a broken link.
        needs_package = "{package}" in self.cdisc_url_template
        needs_date = "{date}" in self.cdisc_url_template
        if (needs_package and not package) or (needs_date and not date):
            return None
        try:
            return self.cdisc_url_template.format(
                concept_id=concept_id,
                package=package or "",
                date=date or "",
            )
        except KeyError:
            return None

    @staticmethod
    def _alias_for(cl: dict[str, Any]) -> str | None:
        """Derive a human-readable alias from the codelist submission value.

        Returns a valid Python identifier (e.g. ``"SEX"``, ``"RACE"``,
        ``"ETHNIC"``) or ``None`` when no usable name can be derived.
        """
        sv: str = cl.get("submissionValue", "")
        if not sv:
            return None
        return _safe_identifier(sv)

        codelist_json: Dict returned by ``CDISCClient.get_codelist``.
            Must contain at least ``conceptId`` and ``terms``.
        package: Optional CT package the codelist was fetched from
            (e.g. ``"sdtmct-2024-12-13"``).  Stored on the codelist
            dict as ``_package`` so the rendered ``_cdisc_url`` can
            include the correct package + date context required by
            the CDISC Library Browser.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If required keys are missing.
    """
    if "conceptId" not in codelist_json:
        raise ValueError("codelist JSON must contain 'conceptId'")
    if package is not None:
        codelist_json = {**codelist_json, "_package": package}
    self._codelists.append(codelist_json)

@classmethod
def from_concept_ids(
    cls,
    client: CDISCClient,
    concept_ids: set[str],
    *,
    package: str = "sdtmct-2023-12-15",
    include_docs: bool = True,
) -> CodelistGenerator:
    """Build a generator from an explicit set of NCI concept IDs.

    Args:
        client: An authenticated ``CDISCClient`` instance.
        concept_ids: Set of NCI concept ID strings to download.
        package: CT package version to download from.
        include_docs: Whether to include definitions in generated output.

    Returns:
        A ``CodelistGenerator`` populated with the requested codelists.

    Examples:
        Generate codelists for specific concept IDs::

            from fleet.ct.api import CDISCClient
            from fleet.ct.generator import CodelistGenerator

            with CDISCClient() as client:
                gen = CodelistGenerator.from_concept_ids(
                    client,
                    {"C66731", "C74457"},
                )
                gen.write("codelists.py")
    """
    gen = cls(include_docs=include_docs)
    for cid in sorted(concept_ids):
        try:
            gen.add_codelist(
                client.get_codelist(cid, package=package),
                package=package,
            )
        except Exception:
            logger.warning(
                "Codelist %s not found in package %s — skipping.",
                cid,
                package,
            )
    return gen

    ig_version: str = "3-4",

) -> CodelistGenerator:

    Queries the CDISC Library for the specified SDTM IG version,
    extracts every codelist referenced by variables in the requested
    domains, and downloads the corresponding CT definitions.

    Args:
        client: An authenticated ``CDISCClient`` instance.
        domains: List of SDTM domain abbreviations to include
            (e.g. ``["DM", "AE", "VS", "EX"]``).

        client,

def render(self) -> str:
    """Render accumulated codelists as a Python module string.

    Returns:
        A complete, syntactically valid Python source string.
    """
    sorted_cls = sorted(self._codelists, key=lambda c: c["conceptId"])

    lines: list[str] = [
        '"""Auto-generated CDISC Controlled Terminology constants.',
        "",
        "Do not edit manually — regenerate with ``fleet.ct.generator``.",
        '"""',
        "",
    ]

    # Class definitions
    for cl in sorted_cls:
        lines.extend(self._render_class(cl))
        lines.append("")

    # Human-readable aliases  (e.g.  SEX = C66731)
    aliases: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    for cl in sorted_cls:
        concept_id = cl["conceptId"]
        class_name = _safe_identifier(concept_id)
        alias = self._alias_for(cl)
        if alias and alias != class_name:
            aliases.append((alias, class_name))

    if aliases:
        lines.append("")
        lines.append("# Human-readable aliases")
        for alias, class_name in sorted(aliases):
            lines.append(f"{alias} = {class_name}")
        lines.append("")

    # __all__
    all_names: list[str] = [_safe_identifier(cl["conceptId"]) for cl in sorted_cls]
    all_names.extend(alias for alias, _ in sorted(aliases))
    all_names.sort()
    all_repr = ", ".join(f'"{n}"' for n in all_names)
    lines.append(f"__all__ = [{all_repr}]")
    lines.append("")

    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"

def write(self, path: str | Path) -> Path:
    """Render and write the module to *path*.

    Parent directories are created if they do not exist.

    Args:
        path: Destination file path.

    Returns:
        Resolved ``Path`` of the written file.
    """
    dest = Path(path)
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    dest.write_text(self.render(), encoding="utf-8")
    return dest.resolve()

Dynamically import a generated codelists.py module.

Resolves the codelist module location using these strategies (in order):

  2. Look for study_config.yaml in the current working directory and resolve the SDTM metadata path from it.
  3. Fall back to metadata/sdtm/codelists.py relative to CWD.

def import_codelists(
    path: str | Path | None = None,
    *,
    module_name: str = "codelists",
) -> ModuleType:
    """Dynamically import a generated ``codelists.py`` module.

    Resolves the codelist module location using these strategies (in order):

    1. If *path* is given explicitly, use it directly.
    2. Look for ``study_config.yaml`` in the current working directory and
       resolve the SDTM metadata path from it.
    3. Fall back to ``metadata/sdtm/codelists.py`` relative to CWD.

    The module is registered in ``sys.modules`` under *module_name* so that
    subsequent ``from codelists import SEX`` statements work as expected
    throughout the session.

    Args:
        path: Explicit path to the ``codelists.py`` file.  When ``None``,
            auto-discovery is attempted.
        module_name: Name to register the module under in ``sys.modules``.
            Defaults to ``"codelists"``.

    Returns:
        The imported codelists module.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If no ``codelists.py`` could be located.

    Examples:
        Auto-discover from study config::

            from fleet.ct import import_codelists

            ct = import_codelists()
            SEX = ct.SEX

        Or register so bare imports work::

            from fleet.ct import import_codelists

            import_codelists()  # registers as 'codelists' in sys.modules
            from codelists import SEX, RACE  # now works anywhere
    """
    resolved = _resolve_codelists_path(path)
    if not resolved.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"Codelists module not found at: {resolved}\n"
            "Run `fleet init ct` to generate it, or pass an explicit path."
        )

    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(module_name, resolved)
    if spec is None or spec.loader is None:
        raise ImportError(f"Cannot create module spec for: {resolved}")

    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules[module_name] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module

docs.title: CT Validator
docs.text: The singleton CTValidator provides runtime validation of values against loaded codelists.

docs.title: How CT validation works
docs.text:
Validation fires at pipeline-build time — when you call .hardcode_ct() or .assign_ct() in Python, not when you call .to_frame(). The check happens during the method call itself, before any data is processed.

The validator is opt-in via initialization. Fleet ships a module-level singleton that starts empty. You must load CT data into it before using ct_codelist= parameters. If the singleton has no data loaded, validation is silently skipped and the value is assigned as-is — no error, no warning.

Failures warn, they do not block. If a value is not a valid CDISC submission term, a Python UserWarning is emitted via warnings.warn(). The pipeline continues and the value is still written to the output. This design keeps pipelines runnable during development even before CT packages are fully loaded.

docs.title: Step-by-step — enabling CT validation
docs.text:
import warnings
from fleet import load_controlled_terminology, get_validator

# 1. Load the CT package once, at script/session start.
#    The file is a YAML or CSV produced by `fleet init ct` or `fleet init-ct`.
load_controlled_terminology("examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/ct_package.yaml")

# 2. Import the generated codelist classes.
from fleet.ct import import_codelists

ct = import_codelists()
AGEU = ct.AGEU
SEX = ct.SEX

# 3. Build your pipeline — validation fires here on each verb call.
import warnings

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")
    dm = (
        raw_df.sdtm.hardcode_ct("AGEU", value="YEARS", ct_codelist=AGEU)  # OK — valid term
        .hardcode_ct("AGEU", value="YRS", ct_codelist=AGEU)  # Warns immediately
        .to_frame()
    )

# Any invalid values produce a warning at the .hardcode_ct() call site,
# not when .to_frame() runs.
for w in caught:
    print(w.message)
# UserWarning: Value 'YRS' not in codelist 'C66781'. Valid values: DAYS, HOURS, MINUTES, MONTHS, WEEKS, YEARS

Validator for CDISC Controlled Terminology.

Provides caching, lazy loading, and validation of SDTM/ADaM values against CDISC controlled terminology codelists. Supports both NCI codelist codes (e.g., C66731) and human-readable aliases (e.g., SEX).

Usage

from fleet import get_validator validator = get_validator() validator.load_ct_file("ct/cdisc_ct.yaml", aliases={"SEX": "C66731"}) validator.validate_value("SEX", "M") (True, "Value 'M' is valid for codelist 'C66731'")

Source code in src/fleet/ct/validator.py 
class CTValidator:
    """Validator for CDISC Controlled Terminology.

    Provides caching, lazy loading, and validation of SDTM/ADaM values
    against CDISC controlled terminology codelists. Supports both NCI
    codelist codes (e.g., C66731) and human-readable aliases (e.g., SEX).

    Usage:
        >>> from fleet import get_validator
        >>> validator = get_validator()
        >>> validator.load_ct_file("ct/cdisc_ct.yaml", aliases={"SEX": "C66731"})
        >>> validator.validate_value("SEX", "M")
        (True, "Value 'M' is valid for codelist 'C66731'")
    """

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._lock = Lock()
        self._ct_cache: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
        self._codelist_aliases: dict[str, str] = {}
        self._ct_path: Path | None = None
        self._initialized: bool = False

    @classmethod
    def get_instance(cls) -> CTValidator:
        """Return the module-level singleton. Kept for backward compatibility."""
        return _validator

    def load_ct_file(
        self,
        ct_path: Path | str,
        aliases: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Load all codelists from a YAML or CSV file into the cache.

        Args:
            ct_path: Path or URL to the CT file (.yaml, .yml, .csv).
            aliases: Optional mapping of human-readable names to codelist codes,
                     e.g., {"SEX": "C66731", "RACE": "C74457"}.

        Raises:
            CTError: If the file cannot be loaded.
        """
        with self._lock:
            try:
                logger.info("Loading CT file from: %s", ct_path)
                self._ct_cache = load_controlled_terminology(ct_path)
                self._ct_path = Path(ct_path) if isinstance(ct_path, str) else ct_path
                self._initialized = True
                if aliases:
                    self._codelist_aliases.update(aliases)
                logger.info("Loaded %d codelists from %s", len(self._ct_cache), ct_path)
            except CTError:
                raise

    def load_codelist(
        self,
        ct_path: Path | str,
        codelist_name: str,
        alias: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Lazy-load a single codelist from a file (skips if already cached).

        Args:
            ct_path: Path or URL to the CT file.
            codelist_name: Name or NCI code of codelist to load.
            alias: Optional human-readable name to register for this codelist.
        """
        with self._lock:
            if codelist_name in self._ct_cache:
                logger.debug("Codelist %s already cached", codelist_name)
                return
            try:
                data = load_controlled_terminology(ct_path, codelist_name)
                self._ct_cache.update(data)
                if alias:
                    self._codelist_aliases[alias] = codelist_name
                logger.info("Lazy-loaded codelist: %s", codelist_name)
            except CTError as e:
                logger.warning(
                    "Could not load codelist '%s': %s. Validation will pass by default.",
                    codelist_name,
                    e,
                )

    def register_alias(self, alias: str, codelist_name: str) -> None:
        """Register a human-readable alias for a codelist code.

        Args:
            alias: Human-readable name, e.g., "SEX".
            codelist_name: NCI codelist code, e.g., "C66731".
        """
        self._codelist_aliases[alias] = codelist_name

    def validate_value(
        self,
        codelist_name: str,
        value: str | None,
        allow_null: bool = False,
    ) -> tuple[bool, str]:
        """Validate a single value against a codelist.

        Args:
            codelist_name: Codelist name or alias (e.g., "SEX" or "C66731").
            value: The value to validate (None is handled by allow_null).
            allow_null: Whether None is considered valid.

        Returns:
            Tuple (is_valid, message).
        """
        if value is None:
            if allow_null:
                return (True, f"Null value allowed for codelist '{codelist_name}'")
            return (False, f"Null value not allowed for codelist '{codelist_name}'")

        actual_cl = self._codelist_aliases.get(codelist_name, codelist_name)

        if actual_cl not in self._ct_cache:
            logger.warning(
                "Codelist '%s' not loaded — validation skipped for value '%s'",
                actual_cl,
                value,
            )
            return (True, f"Codelist '{actual_cl}' not loaded - validation skipped")

        codelist = self._ct_cache[actual_cl]
        if value in codelist:
            return (True, f"Value '{value}' is valid for codelist '{actual_cl}'")

        valid_str = ", ".join(sorted(codelist.keys()))
        return (
            False,
            f"Value '{value}' not in codelist '{actual_cl}'. Valid values: {valid_str}",
        )

    def get_valid_values(self, codelist_name: str) -> list[str]:
        """Return all valid codes for a codelist.

        Args:
            codelist_name: Codelist name or alias.

        Returns:
            Sorted list of valid code strings, empty if codelist not loaded.
        """
        actual_cl = self._codelist_aliases.get(codelist_name, codelist_name)
        codelist = self._ct_cache.get(actual_cl, {})
        return sorted(codelist.keys())

    def get_cache_info(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        """Return diagnostic information about the current cache state."""
        return {
            "codelists_loaded": list(self._ct_cache.keys()),
            "aliases": dict(self._codelist_aliases),
            "ct_path": str(self._ct_path) if self._ct_path else None,
            "initialized": self._initialized,
        }

    def apply_ct_mapping(self, codelist_name: str, value: str | None) -> str | None:
        """Map an SDTM code to its decoded CT value (e.g., "M" → "Male").

        Returns the original value if the codelist is not loaded or value not found.
        """
        if value is None:
            return None
        actual_cl = self._codelist_aliases.get(codelist_name, codelist_name)
        codelist = self._ct_cache.get(actual_cl, {})
        return codelist.get(value, value)

    def get_decode_map(self, codelist_name: str) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Return a code-to-preferred-term mapping for a codelist.

        Each key is the submission value (e.g. ``"M"``) and the value is
        the preferred term / decode (e.g. ``"Male"``).  Returns an empty
        dict if the codelist is not loaded.

        Args:
            codelist_name: Codelist name, alias, or NCI concept ID.

        Returns:
            Dictionary mapping coded values to their preferred terms.
        """
        actual_cl = self._codelist_aliases.get(codelist_name, codelist_name)
        codelist = self._ct_cache.get(actual_cl, {})
        return {
            coded: info.get("preferred_term", coded) if isinstance(info, dict) else coded
            for coded, info in codelist.items()
        }

def validate_value(
    self,
    codelist_name: str,
    value: str | None,
    allow_null: bool = False,
) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Validate a single value against a codelist.

    Args:
        codelist_name: Codelist name or alias (e.g., "SEX" or "C66731").
        value: The value to validate (None is handled by allow_null).
        allow_null: Whether None is considered valid.

    Returns:
        Tuple (is_valid, message).
    """
    if value is None:
        if allow_null:
            return (True, f"Null value allowed for codelist '{codelist_name}'")
        return (False, f"Null value not allowed for codelist '{codelist_name}'")

    actual_cl = self._codelist_aliases.get(codelist_name, codelist_name)

    if actual_cl not in self._ct_cache:
        logger.warning(
            "Codelist '%s' not loaded — validation skipped for value '%s'",
            actual_cl,
            value,
        )
        return (True, f"Codelist '{actual_cl}' not loaded - validation skipped")

    codelist = self._ct_cache[actual_cl]
    if value in codelist:
        return (True, f"Value '{value}' is valid for codelist '{actual_cl}'")

    valid_str = ", ".join(sorted(codelist.keys()))
    return (
        False,
        f"Value '{value}' not in codelist '{actual_cl}'. Valid values: {valid_str}",
    )

def get_decode_map(self, codelist_name: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return a code-to-preferred-term mapping for a codelist.

    Each key is the submission value (e.g. ``"M"``) and the value is
    the preferred term / decode (e.g. ``"Male"``).  Returns an empty
    dict if the codelist is not loaded.

def load_controlled_terminology(
    ct_path: Path | str,
    codelist_name: str | None = None,
) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:
    """Load CDISC controlled terminology from a YAML or CSV file (or URL).

    Args:
        ct_path: Path or URL to CT file. Supported formats: .yaml, .yml, .csv.
        codelist_name: If given, only load this specific codelist.

    Returns:
        Nested dict mapping codelist_name -> {code: decoded_value}.

    Raises:
        CTError: If the file cannot be found, read, or is in an unsupported format.
    """
    if isinstance(ct_path, str):
        if ct_path.startswith("http"):
            ct_path = _download_ct(ct_path)
        else:
            ct_path = Path(ct_path)

    if not ct_path.exists():
        raise CTError(f"CT file not found: {ct_path}")

    suffix = ct_path.suffix.lower()
    if suffix in (".yaml", ".yml"):
        return _load_ct_yaml(ct_path, codelist_name)
    elif suffix == ".csv":
        return _load_ct_csv(ct_path, codelist_name)
    else:
        raise CTError(f"Unsupported CT file type: {suffix}. Use .yaml or .csv")

class DefineXMLGenerator:
    """Generate CDISC Define-XML 2.1 from a YAML specification file."""

    def __init__(self, define_yaml_path: Path) -> None:
        self.define_data = yaml.safe_load(Path(define_yaml_path).read_text())

    def generate(self, output_path: Path) -> None:
        """Write a Define-XML 2.1 ODM XML file to *output_path*."""
        root = self._build_odm()
        xml_bytes = self._serialize(root)
        output_path = Path(output_path)
        output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        output_path.write_bytes(xml_bytes)
        print(f"Define-XML generated: {output_path}")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # ODM / Study / MetaDataVersion                                       #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def _build_odm(self) -> etree._Element:
        hdr = self.define_data["odm_header"]
        attribs: dict[str, str] = {
            "ODMVersion": hdr["odm_version"],
            "FileOID": hdr["file_oid"],
            "FileType": hdr["file_type"],
            "CreationDateTime": hdr["creation_date_time"],
            "Originator": hdr["originator"],
            _def("Context"): hdr["def_context"],
        }
        if hdr.get("source_system"):
            attribs["SourceSystem"] = hdr["source_system"]
        if hdr.get("source_system_version"):
            attribs["SourceSystemVersion"] = hdr["source_system_version"]

        odm = etree.Element(_odm("ODM"), attrib=attribs, nsmap=_NSMAP)
        odm.append(
            self._build_study(self.define_data["study"], self.define_data["metadata_version"])
        )
        return odm

    def _build_study(self, study_data: dict[str, Any], metadata: dict[str, Any]) -> etree._Element:
        study = etree.Element(_odm("Study"), {"OID": study_data["oid"]})
        gv_data = study_data["global_variables"]
        gv = etree.SubElement(study, _odm("GlobalVariables"))
        etree.SubElement(gv, _odm("StudyName")).text = gv_data["study_name"]
        etree.SubElement(gv, _odm("StudyDescription")).text = gv_data["study_description"]
        etree.SubElement(gv, _odm("ProtocolName")).text = gv_data["protocol_name"]
        study.append(self._build_metadata_version(metadata))
        return study

    def _build_metadata_version(self, metadata: dict[str, Any]) -> etree._Element:
        attribs = {
            "OID": metadata["oid"],
            "Name": metadata["name"],
            "Description": metadata["description"],
            _def("DefineVersion"): metadata["define_version"],
        }
        mdv = etree.Element(_odm("MetaDataVersion"), attrib=attribs)

        standards = metadata.get("standards", [])
        if standards:
            stds_container = etree.SubElement(mdv, _def("Standards"))
            for std in standards:
                stds_container.append(self._build_standard(std))

        if metadata.get("supporting_documents"):
            acrf = etree.SubElement(mdv, _def("AnnotatedCRF"))
            for doc_ref in metadata["supporting_documents"]:
                etree.SubElement(acrf, _def("DocumentRef"), {"leafID": doc_ref["leaf_id"]})

        for ig in metadata.get("item_group_defs", []):
            mdv.append(self._build_item_group_def(ig))
        for item in metadata.get("item_defs", []):
            mdv.append(self._build_item_def(item))
        for cl in metadata.get("code_lists", []):
            mdv.append(self._build_codelist(cl))
        for method in metadata.get("method_defs", []):
            mdv.append(self._build_method_def(method))
        for comment in metadata.get("comment_defs", []):
            mdv.append(self._build_comment_def(comment))
        for leaf in metadata.get("leaf_defs", []):
            mdv.append(self._build_leaf(leaf))

        return mdv

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Element builders                                                     #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    @staticmethod
    def _build_standard(std: dict[str, Any]) -> etree._Element:
        attribs = {
            "OID": std["oid"],
            "Name": std["name"],
            "Type": std["type"],
            "Version": std["version"],
        }
        if std.get("status"):
            attribs["Status"] = std["status"]
        if std.get("publishing_set"):
            attribs["PublishingSet"] = std["publishing_set"]
        if std.get("comment_oid"):
            attribs[_def("CommentOID")] = std["comment_oid"]
        return etree.Element(_def("Standard"), attrib=attribs)

    def _build_item_group_def(self, ig: dict[str, Any]) -> etree._Element:
        attribs = {
            "OID": ig["oid"],
            "Name": ig["name"],
            "Repeating": ig["repeating"],
            "IsReferenceData": ig["is_reference_data"],
            "SASDatasetName": ig["sas_dataset_name"],
            "Domain": ig.get("domain", ig["name"]),
            _def("Structure"): ig["structure"],
        }
        for k, a in [
            ("purpose", "Purpose"),
            ("standard_oid", _def("StandardOID")),
            ("archive_location_id", _def("ArchiveLocationID")),
            ("comment_oid", _def("CommentOID")),
        ]:
            if ig.get(k):
                attribs[a] = ig[k]

        elem = etree.Element(_odm("ItemGroupDef"), attrib=attribs)
        self._append_description(elem, ig.get("description", {}))

        if ig.get("class"):
            cls_elem = etree.SubElement(elem, _def("Class"), {"Name": ig["class"]["name"]})
            if ig["class"].get("subclass"):
                etree.SubElement(cls_elem, _def("SubClass")).text = ig["class"]["subclass"]

        for ref in ig.get("item_refs", []):
            ref_attribs = {
                "ItemOID": ref["item_oid"],
                "OrderNumber": str(ref["order_number"]),
                "Mandatory": ref.get("mandatory", "No"),
            }
            if ref.get("key_sequence") is not None:
                ref_attribs["KeySequence"] = str(ref["key_sequence"])
            if ref.get("method_oid"):
                ref_attribs["MethodOID"] = ref["method_oid"]
            if ref.get("role"):
                ref_attribs["Role"] = ref["role"]
            etree.SubElement(elem, _odm("ItemRef"), attrib=ref_attribs)

        if ig.get("leaf"):
            leaf_d = ig["leaf"]
            leaf_attrs: dict[str, str] = {"ID": leaf_d["id"], _xl("href"): leaf_d["href"]}
            if leaf_d.get("title"):
                leaf_attrs[_xl("title")] = leaf_d["title"]
            etree.SubElement(elem, _def("leaf"), attrib=leaf_attrs)

        return elem

    def _build_item_def(self, item: dict[str, Any]) -> etree._Element:
        attribs: dict[str, str] = {
            "OID": item["oid"],
            "Name": item["name"],
            "DataType": item["data_type"],
        }
        for k, a in [
            ("length", "Length"),
            ("sas_field_name", "SASFieldName"),
            ("significant_digits", "SignificantDigits"),
            ("display_format", _def("DisplayFormat")),
            ("comment_oid", _def("CommentOID")),
        ]:
            if item.get(k) is not None:
                attribs[a] = str(item[k])

        elem = etree.Element(_odm("ItemDef"), attrib=attribs)
        self._append_description(elem, item.get("description", {}))

        cl_ref = item.get("codelist_ref", {})
        if isinstance(cl_ref, dict) and cl_ref.get("codelist_oid"):
            etree.SubElement(elem, _odm("CodeListRef"), {"CodeListOID": cl_ref["codelist_oid"]})

        origin = item.get("origin", {})
        if origin and origin.get("type"):
            orig_attrs: dict[str, str] = {"Type": origin["type"]}
            if origin.get("source"):
                orig_attrs["Source"] = origin["source"]
            orig_elem = etree.SubElement(elem, _def("Origin"), attrib=orig_attrs)
            if origin.get("description"):
                d = etree.SubElement(orig_elem, _odm("Description"))
                tt = etree.SubElement(
                    d,
                    _odm("TranslatedText"),
                    {"{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}lang": origin.get("lang", "en")},
                )
                tt.text = origin["description"]
            for doc_ref in origin.get("document_refs", []):
                self._append_doc_ref(orig_elem, doc_ref)

        if item.get("value_list_ref"):
            etree.SubElement(elem, _def("ValueListRef"), {"ValueListOID": item["value_list_ref"]})

        # fleet_algorithm is intentionally not emitted in the XML output
        return elem

    def _build_codelist(self, cl: dict[str, Any]) -> etree._Element:
        attribs: dict[str, str] = {
            "OID": cl["oid"],
            "Name": cl["name"],
            "DataType": cl["data_type"],
        }
        if cl.get("standard_oid"):
            attribs[_def("StandardOID")] = cl["standard_oid"]
        if cl.get("comment_oid"):
            attribs[_def("CommentOID")] = cl["comment_oid"]

        elem = etree.Element(_odm("CodeList"), attrib=attribs)

        for item in cl.get("code_list_items", []):
            ia: dict[str, str] = {"CodedValue": item["coded_value"]}
            for k, a in [("rank", "Rank"), ("order_number", "OrderNumber")]:
                if item.get(k) is not None:
                    ia[a] = str(item[k])
            if item.get("extended_value"):
                ia[_def("ExtendedValue")] = item["extended_value"]
            item_elem = etree.SubElement(elem, _odm("CodeListItem"), attrib=ia)
            decode = item.get("decode", {})
            if decode and decode.get("text"):
                d = etree.SubElement(item_elem, _odm("Decode"))
                tt = etree.SubElement(
                    d,
                    _odm("TranslatedText"),
                    {"{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}lang": decode.get("lang", "en")},
                )
                tt.text = decode["text"]
            alias = item.get("alias", {})
            if alias and alias.get("name"):
                alias_attrs: dict[str, str] = {"Name": alias["name"]}
                if alias.get("context"):
                    alias_attrs["Context"] = alias["context"]
                etree.SubElement(item_elem, _odm("Alias"), attrib=alias_attrs)

        for enum in cl.get("enumerated_items", []):
            ea: dict[str, str] = {"CodedValue": enum["coded_value"]}
            for k, a in [("rank", "Rank"), ("order_number", "OrderNumber")]:
                if enum.get(k) is not None:
                    ea[a] = str(enum[k])
            enum_elem = etree.SubElement(elem, _odm("EnumeratedItem"), attrib=ea)
            if enum.get("alias"):
                alias_attrs = {"Name": enum["alias"]["name"]}
                if enum["alias"].get("context"):
                    alias_attrs["Context"] = enum["alias"]["context"]
                etree.SubElement(enum_elem, _odm("Alias"), attrib=alias_attrs)

        return elem

    def _build_method_def(self, method: dict[str, Any]) -> etree._Element:
        attribs: dict[str, str] = {
            "OID": method["oid"],
            "Name": method["name"],
            "Type": method["type"],
        }
        if method.get("comment_oid"):
            attribs[_def("CommentOID")] = method["comment_oid"]
        elem = etree.Element(_odm("MethodDef"), attrib=attribs)
        self._append_description(elem, method.get("description", {}))
        for expr in method.get("formal_expressions", []):
            expr_elem = etree.SubElement(
                elem, _odm("FormalExpression"), {"Context": expr["context"]}
            )
            expr_elem.text = expr["expression"]
        for doc_ref in method.get("document_refs", []):
            self._append_doc_ref(elem, doc_ref)
        return elem

    def _build_comment_def(self, comment: dict[str, Any]) -> etree._Element:
        elem = etree.Element(_def("CommentDef"), {"OID": comment["oid"]})
        self._append_description(elem, comment.get("description", {}))
        for doc_ref in comment.get("document_refs", []):
            self._append_doc_ref(elem, doc_ref)
        return elem

    def _build_leaf(self, leaf: dict[str, Any]) -> etree._Element:
        attribs: dict[str, str] = {"ID": leaf["id"], _xl("href"): leaf["href"]}
        elem = etree.Element(_def("leaf"), attrib=attribs)
        if leaf.get("title"):
            if leaf["href"].lower().endswith(".xpt"):
                elem.set(_xl("title"), leaf["title"])
            else:
                etree.SubElement(elem, _def("title")).text = leaf["title"]
        return elem

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Helpers                                                              #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    @staticmethod
    def _append_description(parent: etree._Element, desc: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        if desc and desc.get("text"):
            d = etree.SubElement(parent, _odm("Description"))
            tt = etree.SubElement(
                d,
                _odm("TranslatedText"),
                {"{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}lang": desc.get("lang", "en")},
            )
            tt.text = desc["text"]

    @staticmethod
    def _append_doc_ref(parent: etree._Element, doc_ref: dict[str, Any]) -> etree._Element:
        dr = etree.SubElement(parent, _def("DocumentRef"), {"leafID": doc_ref["leaf_id"]})
        for pr in doc_ref.get("pdf_page_refs", []):
            pr_attrs: dict[str, str] = {"PageRefs": pr["page_ref"], "Type": pr["type"]}
            if pr.get("first_page"):
                pr_attrs["FirstPage"] = pr["first_page"]
            if pr.get("last_page"):
                pr_attrs["LastPage"] = pr["last_page"]
            etree.SubElement(dr, _def("PDFPageRef"), attrib=pr_attrs)
        return dr

    @staticmethod
    def _serialize(root: etree._Element) -> bytes:
        """Serialize the element tree to pretty-printed UTF-8 XML bytes."""
        xml_bytes = etree.tostring(
            root,
            pretty_print=True,
            xml_declaration=True,
            encoding="utf-8",
        )
        # Insert XSL processing instruction after the XML declaration
        decl_end = xml_bytes.index(b"?>") + 2
        pi = b'\n<?xml-stylesheet type="text/xsl" href="define2-1.xsl"?>'
        return xml_bytes[:decl_end] + pi + xml_bytes[decl_end:]

class DefineSpecGenerator:
    """Generate Define-XML 2.1 from a simplified Fleet define YAML spec.

    Parameters
    ----------
    define_yaml_path:
        Path to a simplified define YAML file that conforms to
        ``define_spec_schema.json``.
    validate_schema:
        When *True* (default), validates the YAML against the JSON schema
        before generating and raises ``ValueError`` on schema violations.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        define_yaml_path: str | Path,
        *,
        validate_schema: bool = True,
        enrich_methods: bool = False,
    ) -> None:
        self._path = Path(define_yaml_path)
        self._data: dict[str, Any] = yaml.safe_load(self._path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self._enrich_methods = enrich_methods
        # Populated by _build_item_def via _register_method when
        # enrich_methods is True; rendered into MethodDef elements at the
        # end of MetaDataVersion.
        self._method_defs: dict[str, dict[str, str]] = {}
        # Resolve the CRF page map once (merges external page_map with
        # inline crf_pages; inline takes precedence).
        self._page_map: dict[str, str | dict[str, Any]] = self._load_page_map()
        if validate_schema:
            self._validate()

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Public API                                                           #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def generate(
        self,
        output_path: str | Path,
        *,
        html_preview: bool = True,
        xsl_path: str | Path | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        """Write a Define-XML 2.1 document to *output_path*.

        Parameters
        ----------
        output_path:
            Destination path for the ``.xml`` file.
        html_preview:
            When ``True`` (default), also write an HTML preview by applying
            the CDISC ``define2-1.xsl`` stylesheet via lxml.  The HTML file
            is written alongside the XML with a ``_preview.html`` suffix
            (e.g. ``define_sdtm.xml`` → ``define_sdtm_preview.html``).
        xsl_path:
            Path to the ``define2-1.xsl`` stylesheet.  Defaults to
            ``define2-1.xsl`` in the same directory as *output_path*, which
            is the standard layout used by Fleet.
        """
        root = self._build_odm()
        xml_str = self._to_pretty_xml(root)
        out = Path(output_path)
        out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out.write_text(xml_str, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"Define-XML generated: {out}")

        if html_preview:
            self._write_html_preview(out, xsl_path)

    def _write_html_preview(
        self,
        xml_path: Path,
        xsl_path: str | Path | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Apply the define2-1.xsl transform and write an HTML preview file."""
        resolved_xsl = Path(xsl_path) if xsl_path else xml_path.parent / "define2-1.xsl"

        if not resolved_xsl.exists():
            print(
                f"HTML preview skipped: XSL stylesheet not found at '{resolved_xsl}'. "
                "Place define2-1.xsl in the same directory as the XML output, "
                "or pass xsl_path= explicitly."
            )
            return

        xml_doc = lxml_etree.parse(str(xml_path))  # noqa: S320 — local file, not user input
        xsl_doc = lxml_etree.parse(str(resolved_xsl))  # noqa: S320 — local file, not user input
        transform = lxml_etree.XSLT(xsl_doc)
        html_doc = transform(xml_doc)

        html_path = xml_path.with_name(xml_path.stem + "_preview.html")
        html_path.write_bytes(lxml_etree.tostring(html_doc, pretty_print=True, method="html"))
        print(f"HTML preview generated: {html_path}")

    def to_xml_string(self) -> str:
        """Return the Define-XML as a formatted string without writing a file."""
        return self._to_pretty_xml(self._build_odm())

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # CRF page map                                                         #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def _load_page_map(self) -> dict[str, str | dict[str, Any]]:
        """Build a merged CRF page map from external file and inline values.

        Returns a dict keyed by ``"DOMAIN.VARIABLE"`` whose values are
        either a plain page-number string (Layer 1) or a dict with rich
        reference info (Layer 2).  Inline ``crf_pages`` on each variable
        take precedence over entries in the external ``page_map`` file.
        """
        merged: dict[str, str | dict[str, Any]] = {}

        # Layer 3: external page_map YAML
        docs = self._data.get("study", {}).get("documents", {})
        acrf = docs.get("annotated_crf", {})
        page_map_path = acrf.get("page_map")
        if page_map_path:
            resolved = (self._path.parent / page_map_path).resolve()
            if resolved.is_file():
                raw = yaml.safe_load(resolved.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
                if isinstance(raw, dict):
                    merged.update(raw)

        # Layer 1 / 2: inline crf_pages on each variable (overrides external)
        for ds in self._data.get("datasets", []):
            ds_name = ds["name"]
            for var in ds.get("variables", []):
                crf = var.get("crf_pages")
                if crf is not None:
                    merged[f"{ds_name}.{var['name']}"] = crf

        return merged

    def _get_acrf_config(self) -> dict[str, str] | None:
        """Return the annotated CRF document config, or None if absent."""
        docs = self._data.get("study", {}).get("documents", {})
        return docs.get("annotated_crf")

    def _acrf_leaf_id(self) -> str:
        return "LF.acrf"

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Schema validation                                                    #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def _validate(self) -> None:
        schema = json.loads(_SCHEMA_PATH.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        validator = jsonschema.Draft202012Validator(schema)
        errors = list(validator.iter_errors(self._data))
        if errors:
            msgs = "\n".join(f"  - {e.json_path}: {e.message}" for e in errors[:5])
            raise ValueError(f"define YAML failed schema validation:\n{msgs}")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # ODM root                                                             #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def _build_odm(self) -> ET.Element:
        study = self._data["study"]
        std_oid = _STANDARD_OIDS.get(study["standard"], f"STD.{study['standard']}")
        ts = datetime.now(UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
        file_oid = f"CDISC.{study['id']}.1.Define-XML_2.1.0"
        attribs: dict[str, str] = {
            "xmlns": _NS_ODM,
            "xmlns:xlink": _NS_XLINK,
            "xmlns:def": _NS_DEF,
            "ODMVersion": "1.3.2",
            "FileOID": file_oid,
            "FileType": "Snapshot",
            "CreationDateTime": ts,
            "Originator": study["originator"],
            "SourceSystem": study.get("source_system", "Fleet"),
            "SourceSystemVersion": study.get("source_system_version", "0.1.0"),
            "def:Context": "Submission",
        }
        odm = ET.Element("ODM", attrib=attribs)
        odm.append(self._build_study(study, std_oid))
        return odm

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Study / MetaDataVersion                                              #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    def _build_study(self, study: dict[str, Any], std_oid: str) -> ET.Element:
        elem = ET.Element("Study", {"OID": f"STDY.{study['id']}"})
        gv = ET.SubElement(elem, "GlobalVariables")
        ET.SubElement(gv, "StudyName").text = study["name"]
        ET.SubElement(gv, "StudyDescription").text = study["description"].strip()
        ET.SubElement(gv, "ProtocolName").text = study["protocol_name"]
        elem.append(self._build_metadata_version(study, std_oid))
        return elem

    def _build_metadata_version(self, study: dict[str, Any], std_oid: str) -> ET.Element:
        ig = study["standard"]
        mdv_oid = f"MDV.{study['id']}.1.{ig}.{study['standard_version']}"
        attribs = {
            "OID": mdv_oid,
            "Name": f"{study['id']} {ig} Data Definitions",
            "Description": f"Dataset metadata for {study['id']} {ig} datasets",
            "def:DefineVersion": "2.1.0",
        }
        mdv = ET.Element("MetaDataVersion", attrib=attribs)

        # Standards list — must be wrapped in def:Standards per Define-XML 2.1 spec
        stds_container = ET.SubElement(mdv, "def:Standards")
        stds_container.append(
            self._build_standard(std_oid, study["standard"], "IG", study["standard_version"])
        )
        if study.get("ct_version"):
            stds_container.append(
                self._build_standard(
                    _CT_OID,
                    "CDISC/NCI",
                    "CT",
                    study["ct_version"],
                    publishing_set=study["standard"],
                )
            )

        # AnnotatedCRF — emitted when study.documents.annotated_crf is set
        acrf_cfg = self._get_acrf_config()
        if acrf_cfg:
            acrf_elem = ET.SubElement(mdv, "def:AnnotatedCRF")
            ET.SubElement(acrf_elem, "def:DocumentRef", {"leafID": self._acrf_leaf_id()})

        # SupplementalDoc — additional supporting documents
        docs = self._data.get("study", {}).get("documents", {})
        supp_docs = docs.get("supplemental_docs", [])
        if supp_docs:
            supp_elem = ET.SubElement(mdv, "def:SupplementalDoc")
            for sd in supp_docs:
                ET.SubElement(supp_elem, "def:DocumentRef", {"leafID": sd["id"]})

        # ItemGroupDefs (one per dataset)
        datasets: list[dict[str, Any]] = self._data.get("datasets", [])
        for ds in datasets:
            mdv.append(self._build_item_group_def(ds, study["id"]))

        # ItemDefs (collect all unique variables across datasets)
        mdv.extend(self._build_all_item_defs(datasets))

        # CodeLists
        for cl in self._data.get("codelists", []):
            mdv.append(self._build_codelist(cl))

        # MethodDefs (only populated when enrich_methods=True; lazily
        # registered by _build_item_def via _register_method).
        for method_oid in sorted(self._method_defs):
            mdv.append(self._build_method_def(method_oid, self._method_defs[method_oid]))

        # LeafDefs (one per dataset)
        for ds in datasets:
            mdv.append(self._build_leaf(ds))

        # Annotated CRF leaf
        if acrf_cfg:
            acrf_leaf = ET.Element(
                "def:leaf",
                {
                    "ID": self._acrf_leaf_id(),
                    "xlink:href": acrf_cfg["href"],
                },
            )
            ET.SubElement(acrf_leaf, "def:title").text = acrf_cfg.get(
                "title", "Annotated Case Report Form"
            )
            mdv.append(acrf_leaf)

        # Supplemental document leaves
        for sd in supp_docs:
            sd_leaf = ET.Element("def:leaf", {"ID": sd["id"], "xlink:href": sd["href"]})
            ET.SubElement(sd_leaf, "def:title").text = sd["title"]
            mdv.append(sd_leaf)

        return mdv

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Element builders                                                     #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    @staticmethod
    def _build_standard(
        oid: str, name: str, kind: str, version: str, publishing_set: str | None = None
    ) -> ET.Element:
        attribs: dict[str, str] = {
            "OID": oid,
            "Name": name,
            "Type": kind,
            "Version": version,
            "Status": "Final",
        }
        if publishing_set:
            attribs["PublishingSet"] = publishing_set
        return ET.Element("def:Standard", attrib=attribs)

    def _build_item_group_def(self, ds: dict[str, Any], study_id: str) -> ET.Element:
        name = ds["name"]
        ig_oid = f"IG.{name}"
        leaf_id = f"LF.{name}"
        std_oid = _STANDARD_OIDS.get(self._data["study"]["standard"], "STD.IG")
        repeating = "Yes" if ds.get("repeating", True) else "No"

        attribs: dict[str, str] = {
            "OID": ig_oid,
            "Name": name,
            "Repeating": repeating,
            "IsReferenceData": "No",
            "SASDatasetName": name,
            "Domain": name,
            "def:Structure": ds["structure"],
            "Purpose": "Tabulation" if self._data["study"]["standard"] == "SDTMIG" else "Analysis",
            "def:StandardOID": std_oid,
            "def:ArchiveLocationID": leaf_id,
        }
        elem = ET.Element("ItemGroupDef", attrib=attribs)

        desc = ET.SubElement(elem, "Description")
        ET.SubElement(desc, "TranslatedText", {"xml:lang": "en"}).text = ds["label"]

        if ds.get("class"):
            ET.SubElement(elem, "def:Class", {"Name": ds["class"]})

        key_vars: set[str] = set(ds.get("keys", []))
        key_order: dict[str, int] = {v: i + 1 for i, v in enumerate(ds.get("keys", []))}

        for order, var in enumerate(ds["variables"], start=1):
            var_name = var["name"]
            item_oid = self._item_oid(name, var_name)
            ref_attrs: dict[str, str] = {
                "ItemOID": item_oid,
                "OrderNumber": str(order),
                "Mandatory": "Yes" if var.get("mandatory") else "No",
            }
            if var_name in key_vars:
                ref_attrs["KeySequence"] = str(key_order[var_name])
            ET.SubElement(elem, "ItemRef", attrib=ref_attrs)

        # Leaf reference
        ET.SubElement(
            elem,
            "def:leaf",
            {
                "ID": leaf_id,
                "xlink:href": f"{name.lower()}.xpt",
                "xlink:title": f"{name.lower()}.xpt",
            },
        )

        return elem

    def _build_all_item_defs(self, datasets: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[ET.Element]:
        """Build ItemDef elements; shared variables (same name & type) share an OID."""
        seen: dict[str, ET.Element] = {}  # item_oid → element
        result: list[ET.Element] = []
        for ds in datasets:
            for var in ds["variables"]:
                item_oid = self._item_oid(ds["name"], var["name"])
                if item_oid not in seen:
                    elem = self._build_item_def(item_oid, var, ds["name"])
                    seen[item_oid] = elem
                    result.append(elem)
        return result

    def _build_item_def(self, item_oid: str, var: dict[str, Any], dataset_name: str) -> ET.Element:
        attribs: dict[str, str] = {
            "OID": item_oid,
            "Name": var["name"],
            "DataType": _TYPE_TO_ODM[var["type"]],
            "SASFieldName": var["name"],
        }
        if var.get("length") is not None:
            attribs["Length"] = str(var["length"])

        elem = ET.Element("ItemDef", attrib=attribs)

        desc = ET.SubElement(elem, "Description")
        ET.SubElement(desc, "TranslatedText", {"xml:lang": "en"}).text = var["label"]

        if var.get("codelist"):
            ET.SubElement(elem, "CodeListRef", {"CodeListOID": var["codelist"]})

        origin_type = var.get("origin", "Derived")
        orig_elem = ET.SubElement(elem, "def:Origin", {"Type": origin_type})

        # Build the human-readable origin description.  When
        # enrich_methods is on we resolve the verb (or callable) docstring
        # so reviewers see the exact computational method without leaving
        # the Define-XML.
        comment = var.get("comment") or ""
        derivation = var.get("derivation") or {}
        method_oid: str | None = None
        if self._enrich_methods and derivation:
            method_oid, summary = self._register_method(derivation)
            if summary:
                comment = f"{comment} {summary}".strip() if comment else summary
        if comment:
            orig_desc = ET.SubElement(orig_elem, "Description")
            ET.SubElement(orig_desc, "TranslatedText", {"xml:lang": "en"}).text = comment

        # CRF page references — emit DocumentRef/PDFPageRef inside Origin
        self._append_crf_page_ref(orig_elem, dataset_name, var["name"])

        # MethodOID is an ItemDef attribute per Define-XML 2.1; emit only
        # when enrichment produced one.
        if method_oid:
            elem.set("MethodOID", method_oid)

        return elem

    def _register_method(
        self,
        derivation: dict[str, Any],
    ) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
        """Resolve a derivation block to a MethodDef and return its OID + summary.

        Looks up either the ``callable`` dotted path (UC-5) or the
        ``algorithm`` verb name (UC-4) and registers a MethodDef entry on
        ``self._method_defs`` keyed by a stable OID.  Returns the OID and
        the docstring summary so the caller can also append the summary
        to the Origin description.
        """
        callable_path = derivation.get("callable")
        algorithm = derivation.get("algorithm") or ""
        expression = derivation.get("expression") or ""

        if callable_path:
            # Prefer Derivation.dotted_path when the object is registered.
            try:
                from fleet.adam.transforms import get_transform

                obj = get_transform(str(callable_path))
                if hasattr(obj, "dotted_path"):
                    # Derivation object — use its dotted_path and fn docstring.
                    summary = (obj.fn.__doc__ or "").splitlines()[0].strip()
                    dotted = obj.dotted_path
                else:
                    summary, dotted = resolve_callable_docstring(str(callable_path))
            except (KeyError, Exception):
                summary, dotted = resolve_callable_docstring(str(callable_path))
            if not dotted:
                return (None, "")
            method_name = dotted.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
            method_oid = f"MT.{method_name}"
            self._method_defs.setdefault(
                method_oid,
                {
                    "name": method_name,
                    "description": summary or f"Custom callable: {dotted}",
                    "expression": expression or dotted,
                    "context": "Python",
                },
            )
            return (method_oid, summary or "")

        if not algorithm:
            return (None, "")

        summary, dotted = resolve_algorithm_docstring(str(algorithm))
        if not dotted:
            return (None, "")
        method_oid = f"MT.{algorithm}"
        self._method_defs.setdefault(
            method_oid,
            {
                "name": algorithm,
                "description": summary or f"Fleet verb: {algorithm}",
                "expression": expression or f".{algorithm}(...)",
                "context": "Python/Fleet",
            },
        )
        return (method_oid, summary or "")

    @staticmethod
    def _build_method_def(method_oid: str, info: dict[str, str]) -> ET.Element:
        """Render a Define-XML 2.1 ``MethodDef`` element.

        See CDISC Define-XML 2.1 §4.2.2 for the FormalExpression contract.
        """
        elem = ET.Element(
            "MethodDef",
            {"OID": method_oid, "Name": info["name"], "Type": "Computation"},
        )
        desc = ET.SubElement(elem, "Description")
        ET.SubElement(desc, "TranslatedText", {"xml:lang": "en"}).text = info["description"]
        formal = ET.SubElement(elem, "FormalExpression", {"Context": info["context"]})
        formal.text = info["expression"]
        return elem

    @staticmethod
    def _build_codelist(cl: dict[str, Any]) -> ET.Element:
        attribs: dict[str, str] = {
            "OID": cl["oid"],
            "Name": cl["name"],
            "DataType": _TYPE_TO_ODM[cl["type"]],
        }
        elem = ET.Element("CodeList", attrib=attribs)
        for item in cl.get("items", []):
            ci = ET.SubElement(elem, "CodeListItem", {"CodedValue": item["coded_value"]})
            if item.get("decode"):
                decode = ET.SubElement(ci, "Decode")
                ET.SubElement(decode, "TranslatedText", {"xml:lang": "en"}).text = item["decode"]
        return elem

    @staticmethod
    def _build_leaf(ds: dict[str, Any]) -> ET.Element:
        name = ds["name"]
        leaf_id = f"LF.{name}"
        href = f"{name.lower()}.xpt"
        return ET.Element("def:leaf", {"ID": leaf_id, "xlink:href": href, "xlink:title": href})

    def _append_crf_page_ref(
        self, origin_elem: ET.Element, dataset_name: str, var_name: str
    ) -> None:
        """Append a ``def:DocumentRef`` with ``def:PDFPageRef`` to an Origin element.

        Resolves CRF page info from the merged page map.  Supports both
        the simple string form (Layer 1) and the rich dict form (Layer 2).
        """
        key = f"{dataset_name}.{var_name}"
        crf_ref = self._page_map.get(key)
        if crf_ref is None:
            return

        acrf_cfg = self._get_acrf_config()
        default_leaf_id = self._acrf_leaf_id()

        if isinstance(crf_ref, str):
            # Layer 1: simple page string — "7" or "8 9"
            if not acrf_cfg:
                return  # no aCRF document configured; skip silently
            doc_ref = ET.SubElement(origin_elem, "def:DocumentRef", {"leafID": default_leaf_id})
            ET.SubElement(
                doc_ref,
                "def:PDFPageRef",
                {"PageRefs": crf_ref, "Type": "PhysicalRef"},
            )
        elif isinstance(crf_ref, dict):
            # Layer 2: rich reference with optional doc, type, ranges
            doc_href = crf_ref.get("doc")
            if doc_href and acrf_cfg and doc_href != acrf_cfg.get("href"):
                # Reference to a non-default document — resolve leaf ID
                leaf_id = f"LF.{Path(doc_href).stem}"
            else:
                leaf_id = default_leaf_id

            if not acrf_cfg and leaf_id == default_leaf_id:
                return

            doc_ref = ET.SubElement(origin_elem, "def:DocumentRef", {"leafID": leaf_id})
            pages = crf_ref.get("pages")
            ref_type = crf_ref.get("type", "PhysicalRef")
            first_page = crf_ref.get("first_page")
            last_page = crf_ref.get("last_page")

            if pages or first_page:
                pr_attrs: dict[str, str] = {"Type": ref_type}
                if pages:
                    pr_attrs["PageRefs"] = pages
                if first_page:
                    pr_attrs["FirstPage"] = first_page
                if last_page:
                    pr_attrs["LastPage"] = last_page
                ET.SubElement(doc_ref, "def:PDFPageRef", pr_attrs)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
    # Helpers                                                              #
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

    @staticmethod
    def _item_oid(dataset_name: str, var_name: str) -> str:
        """Build a stable ItemDef OID.

        Common variables (STUDYID, USUBJID, ...) that appear in multiple datasets
        are given a shared OID *without* the dataset prefix so they share a single
        ItemDef element in the XML — matching CDISC best practice.
        """
        _SHARED = {
            "STUDYID",
            "USUBJID",
            "DOMAIN",
            "SUBJID",
            "SITEID",
            "AGE",
            "AGEU",
            "SEX",
            "RACE",
            "ETHNIC",
            "ARMCD",
            "ARM",
            "ACTARMCD",
            "ACTARM",
        }
        if var_name in _SHARED:
            return f"IT.{var_name}"
        return f"IT.{dataset_name}.{var_name}"

    @staticmethod
    def _to_pretty_xml(root: ET.Element) -> str:
        raw = ET.tostring(root, encoding="unicode", method="xml")
        dom = xml.dom.minidom.parseString(raw)
        pretty = dom.toprettyxml(indent="  ", encoding="utf-8").decode("utf-8")
        lines = [ln for ln in pretty.split("\n") if ln.strip()]
        if lines and lines[0].startswith("<?xml"):
            lines.insert(1, '<?xml-stylesheet type="text/xsl" href="define2-1.xsl"?>')
        return "\n".join(lines)

The HTML file is written alongside the XML with a _preview.html suffix (e.g. define_sdtm.xml → define_sdtm_preview.html). xsl_path: Path to the define2-1.xsl stylesheet. Defaults to define2-1.xsl in the same directory as output_path, which is the standard layout used by Fleet.

Source code in src/fleet/define_xml/spec_generator.py 
def generate(
    self,
    output_path: str | Path,
    *,
    html_preview: bool = True,
    xsl_path: str | Path | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Write a Define-XML 2.1 document to *output_path*.

    Parameters
    ----------
    output_path:
        Destination path for the ``.xml`` file.
    html_preview:
        When ``True`` (default), also write an HTML preview by applying
        the CDISC ``define2-1.xsl`` stylesheet via lxml.  The HTML file
        is written alongside the XML with a ``_preview.html`` suffix
        (e.g. ``define_sdtm.xml`` → ``define_sdtm_preview.html``).
    xsl_path:
        Path to the ``define2-1.xsl`` stylesheet.  Defaults to
        ``define2-1.xsl`` in the same directory as *output_path*, which
        is the standard layout used by Fleet.
    """
    root = self._build_odm()
    xml_str = self._to_pretty_xml(root)
    out = Path(output_path)
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(xml_str, encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"Define-XML generated: {out}")

    if html_preview:
        self._write_html_preview(out, xsl_path)

docs.title: Method enrichment (enrich_methods=True)
docs.text:
When constructed with enrich_methods=True, DefineSpecGenerator walks each variable's derivation: block and emits a Define-XML 2.1 <MethodDef> element linked to the corresponding <ItemDef> via a MethodOID attribute. The <Description> of the method is taken from the Python docstring of the referenced verb (algorithm:) or callable (callable: — full dotted path), and a <FormalExpression Context="Python/Fleet"> records the verb signature.

This makes the docstring of every Fleet verb the single source of truth for the regulatory description in Define-XML — no duplicated prose.

from fleet import DefineSpecGenerator

DefineSpecGenerator(
    "examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/define.yaml",
    enrich_methods=True,
).generate("outputs/define_sdtm.xml")

CLI equivalent:

uv run fleet define-xml \
  --spec examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/define.yaml \
  --output outputs/define_sdtm.xml \
  --enrich-methods

The derivation block accepts either form:

# Standard verb — resolves against fleet.sdtm / fleet.adam namespaces
derivation:
  algorithm: assign_ct
  source: sex
  ct_codelist: C66731

# Study-specific callable — full dotted path importable at generation time
derivation:
  callable: examples.cdiscpilot01.adam.derivations.derive_aval
