def render_listing_pptx(
    model: ListingModel,
    path: str | Path,
    *,
    theme: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> Path:
    """Render a ``ListingModel`` to a PPTX slide deck.

    Each slide contains a flat data listing as an editable PowerPoint
    table.  The listing can be modified after export.

    Args:
        model: The display-ready listing model from ``listing_to_model()``.
        path: Output ``.pptx`` file path.
        theme: Optional dict of style overrides.

    Returns:
        Path: The written ``.pptx`` path.

    Raises:
        ImportError: If ``python-pptx`` is not installed.

    Examples:
        Render an AE listing to editable slides::

            from fleet.tlg import listing_to_model, RenderMetadata
            from fleet.tlg.render.slides import render_listing_pptx

            meta = RenderMetadata(title="Listing 16.2.7.1", subtitle="AE Listing")
            model = listing_to_model(listing_df, meta)
            render_listing_pptx(model, "ae_listing.pptx")
    """
    try:
        from pptx import Presentation  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
        from pptx.util import Emu, Inches, Pt  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    except ImportError:
        raise ImportError(
            "python-pptx is required for PPTX slide export.\n"
            "Install it with:  uv add python-pptx\n"
            "Or:  pip install fleet-cdisc[tlg-pptx]"
        ) from None

    from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
    from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN  # type: ignore[import-untyped]

    th = _resolve_theme(theme)

    prs = Presentation()
    prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
    prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

    slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank
    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)

    # ── Title + subtitle ──
    top = Inches(0.3)
    if model.metadata.title:
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.5))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = model.metadata.title
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_title"])
        p.font.bold = True
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        top += Inches(0.45)

    if model.metadata.subtitle:
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), top, Inches(12), Inches(0.4))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = model.metadata.subtitle
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_subtitle"])
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        top += Inches(0.4)

    top += Inches(0.1)

    # ── Table ──
    n_cols = len(model.column_labels)
    n_rows = 1 + len(model.data)  # header + data

    table_width = Inches(12.3)
    table_height = min(Inches(0.3) * n_rows, Inches(5.5))
    table_left = Inches(0.5)

    tbl_shape = slide.shapes.add_table(n_rows, n_cols, table_left, top, table_width, table_height)
    table = tbl_shape.table

    col_width = int(table_width / max(n_cols, 1))
    for ci in range(n_cols):
        table.columns[ci].width = Emu(col_width)

    # Headers
    for ci, lbl in enumerate(model.column_labels):
        cell = table.cell(0, ci)
        cell.text = ""
        p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = lbl
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_body"])
        p.font.bold = True
        p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
        cell.fill.solid()
        cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(th["header_bg"])
        p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(th["header_fg"])

    # Data rows
    for ri, row_data in enumerate(model.data, start=1):
        bg = th["alt_row_bg"] if ri % 2 == 0 else None
        for ci, lbl in enumerate(model.column_labels):
            cell = table.cell(ri, ci)
            cell.text = ""
            p = cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0]
            p.text = row_data.get(lbl, "")
            p.font.name = th["font_name"]
            p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_body"])
            p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT
            if bg:
                cell.fill.solid()
                cell.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string(bg)

    # ── Footnotes ──
    if model.metadata.footnotes:
        fn_top = top + table_height + Inches(0.15)
        fn_text = "\n".join(model.metadata.footnotes)
        txbox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.5), fn_top, Inches(12), Inches(0.8))
        tf = txbox.text_frame
        tf.word_wrap = True
        p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        p.text = fn_text
        p.font.size = Pt(th["font_size_footnote"])
        p.font.name = th["font_name"]
        p.font.color.rgb = RGBColor.from_string("666666")

    # ── Write ──
    p_out = Path(path)
    p_out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    prs.save(str(p_out))
    return p_out

docs.title: Advanced Patterns
docs.text: Fleet provides significant flexibility to handle complex clinical trial scenarios that don't fit perfectly into standard CDISC verbs.

docs.title: Custom Derivations with Polars Expressions
docs.text: While Fleet provides verbs like .study_day() or .baseline(), you will often need custom logic to derive variables specific to a study.

docs.title: Simple Inline Derivations
docs.text:
For row-by-row logic or straightforward column math, use the .derivation() verb. It accepts four forms:

String expression (YAML-compatible, AST-sandboxed):

adsl = (
    dm.adam.adsl
    .derivation("AGEGR1", expression="pl.when(pl.col('AGE') < 65).then(pl.lit('<65 yrs')).otherwise(pl.lit('>=65 yrs'))")
    .to_frame()
)

Direct pl.Expr (full Polars power):

import polars as pl

adsl = (
    dm.adam.adsl
    .derivation(
        "AGEGR1",
        expression=(
            pl.when(pl.col("AGE") < 18).then(pl.lit("<18"))
            .when(pl.col("AGE") <= 65).then(pl.lit("18-65"))
            .otherwise(pl.lit(">65"))
        ),
    )
    .to_frame()
)

Lambda returning pl.Expr (inline, IDE auto-complete, no string sandbox):

adsl = (
    dm.adam.adsl
    .derivation("AGEGR1", expression=lambda: (
        pl.when(pl.col("AGE") < 65).then(pl.lit("<65 yrs"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit(">=65 yrs"))
    ))
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: @derivation — File-Based, Lineage-Tracked Derivations
docs.text: For study-specific logic that should be versioned, reused, and automatically documented in Define-XML, use the @derivation decorator. This is the primary escape-hatch pattern for anything too complex for a one-liner.

docs.title: Three kind values
docs.text: Kind When to use Signature column Row-by-row expression (no DataFrame needed) () -> pl.Expr frame Multi-column or aggregation logic (df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame param By-group reshape (e.g. tall/narrow BDS rows) (df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame + by= / set_values_to=

docs.title: kind="column" example
docs.text:
# examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/derivations/AGEGR1.py
from fleet.core.derivation import derivation
import polars as pl

@derivation
def AGEGR1() -> pl.Expr:
    """Classify AGE into pooled age groups for ADSL."""
    return (
        pl.when(pl.col("AGE") < 65)
        .then(pl.lit("<65 yrs"))
        .otherwise(pl.lit(">=65 yrs"))
    ).alias("AGEGR1")

Use it directly in a pipeline:

from examples.cdiscpilot01.adam.derivations import AGEGR1

adsl = (
    dm.adam.adsl
    .derivation(AGEGR1)
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: kind="frame" example
docs.text:
@derivation(targets=["SAFFL", "ITTFL"])
def add_pop_flags(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Add SAFFL and ITTFL population flags."""
    return df.with_columns(
        pl.lit("Y").alias("SAFFL"),
        pl.lit("Y").alias("ITTFL"),
    )

docs.title: kind="param" example
docs.text:
@derivation(
    by=["USUBJID", "ADT"],
    set_values_to={"PARAMCD": "BMI", "PARAM": "Body Mass Index"},
)
def BMI(df: pl.DataFrame) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Compute BMI per subject visit."""
    return df.with_columns(
        (pl.col("WEIGHT") / (pl.col("HEIGHT") / 100) ** 2).alias("AVAL")
    )

docs.title: Derivations folder convention
docs.text:
Study derivations live under:

specs/<study_id>/adam/derivations/
    __init__.py        # auto-updated by `fleet derivation add`
    AGEGR1.py
    BMI.py

Scaffold a new derivation with the CLI:

fleet derivation add AGEGR1 --dataset ADSL --kind column

docs.title: Complex Multi-Dataset Derivations (Escaping the Pipeline)
docs.text:
For highly complex, advanced logic—such as derivations requiring customized multi-dataset joins, complex rolling window aggregations, or logic that simply cannot be expressed linearly in standard verbs—the recommended pattern is to "escape" the automated pipeline.

Because Fleet is built securely on Polars DataFrames, you can drop out to native Polars, compute your advanced logic, merge it back, and then seamlessly resume your Fleet pipeline.

import polars as pl

# 1. Start by compiling your base ADSL dataset to a Polars DataFrame
# (Assuming you already have adsl base and adverse events dataframes)
base_adsl = ctx.build("ADSL") # Or adsl_pipeline.to_frame()

# 2. Compute complex custom logic using pure Polars (e.g. tracking a multi-step clinical event pattern)
# Here we find patients who had a Severe AE specifically after taking a certain concomitant medication.
complex_events = (
    base_adsl.select(["USUBJID", "TRTSDT"])
    .join(ae_df.filter(pl.col("AESEV") == "SEVERE"), on="USUBJID", how="inner")
    .join(cm_df.filter(pl.col("CMINDC") == "NAUSEA"), on="USUBJID", how="left")
    .group_by("USUBJID")
    .agg([
        pl.when(pl.col("AESTDTC").min() > pl.col("CMSTDTC").min())
          .then(pl.lit("Y"))
          .otherwise(pl.lit("N"))
          .alias("CUSTFL")
    ])
)

# 3. Merge the result natively using Polars
merged_adsl = base_adsl.join(complex_events, on="USUBJID", how="left")

# 4. Jump back into Fleet if you need to finalize any remaining standard derivations or metadata
final_adsl = (
    merged_adsl.adam.adsl
    .derivation("CUSTFL", expression=pl.col("CUSTFL").fill_null("N"))
    .to_frame()
)

This pattern ensures you are never bottlenecked by the package API: if you can write it in Polars, you can execute it in Fleet.

docs.title: Subclassing Namespaces
docs.text:
If your organisation uses standard proprietary derivations across multiple datasets, you can extend Fleet namespaces by subclassing them.

from fleet.adam.namespace import AdamNamespace
import polars as pl

class CompanyAdamNamespace(AdamNamespace):
    def proprietary_flag(self, target_col: str, condition: str) -> "CompanyAdamNamespace":
        """Re-usable custom flag for your company."""
        expr = pl.when(pl.col(condition) == "Y").then(pl.lit("Y")).otherwise(pl.lit(None))
        return self._chain(expr.alias(target_col))

# You can register this as a custom accessor using Polars
@pl.api.register_dataframe_namespace("company_adam")
class _CompanyAdamPolarsAccessor(CompanyAdamNamespace):
    def __init__(self, df: pl.DataFrame):
        super().__init__(df)

docs.title: Handing Non-CDISC Raw Sources
docs.text:
If you are pulling in non-standard vendor files, use Fleet verbs to rename and map columns directly inside the pipeline. The .source() verb (ADaM) and .assign_no_ct() verb (SDTM) both accept a from_col / source keyword to copy a raw column under a CDISC-compliant name — no intermediate Polars .rename() call needed:

import polars as pl
from fleet import load_study_context

raw_labs = pl.read_csv("vendor_labs.csv")

# Rename non-standard columns inline using Fleet verbs, then continue derivation
adlb = (
    raw_labs.adam
    .source("USUBJID", from_col="Subject_ID")
    .source("AVAL", from_col="Lab_Result")
    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL")
    .to_frame()
)

For SDTM pipelines the equivalent verb is .assign_no_ct():

dm = (
    raw_df.sdtm
    .assign_no_ct("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .assign_no_ct("SUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .to_frame()
)

Only fall back to raw Polars for pre-processing that genuinely cannot be expressed as a Fleet verb (e.g. pivoting wide vendor files, multi-file concatenation), and re-enter the Fleet pipeline immediately afterwards.

docs.title: Cross-Domain Derivations with .pin()
docs.text: Many CDISC derivations require data from sibling domains — SDTM study day needs DM's RFSTDTC, ADaM datasets need ADSL columns like TRTSDT and population flags. Fleet's Pipeline Passport (.pin()) lets verbs see reference data without polluting the frame.

docs.title: Pinning a reference domain
docs.text:
# Build DM first
dm = dm_raw.sdtm.hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN", value="DM") ...  .to_frame()

# Pin DM to the AE pipeline — verbs can now resolve RFSTDTC
ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm
    .hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign_no_ct("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
    .date("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .pin("DM", dm)                                      # ← attach reference
    .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")            # ← consumes the pin
    .baseline_flag("AEBLFL", date_col="AESTDTC")        # ← also consumes it
    .to_frame()
)

The pinned DataFrame is not merged into the frame — it stays beside it. Verbs borrow what they need, compute, and drop temp columns. The output frame stays clean.

docs.title: Multiple pins
docs.text:
You can pin as many domains as you need:

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm
    .pin("DM", dm_df)                                # join on USUBJID (default)
    .pin("TV", tv_df, join_on="VISITNUM")            # different join key
    .pin("EX", ex_df, join_on=["USUBJID", "EXTRT"]) # compound key
    .study_day("AESTDY", date_col="AESTDTC")        # uses DM pin
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Inspecting pins
docs.text:
ae_ns = ae_raw.sdtm.pin("DM", dm).pin("TV", tv, join_on="VISITNUM")
ae_ns.pins()
# {'DM': {'df': ..., 'join_on': ['USUBJID']},
#  'TV': {'df': ..., 'join_on': ['VISITNUM']}}

docs.title: ADaM: .join_adsl() and .study_day()
docs.text:
For ADaM datasets, pin ADSL and use .join_adsl() to carry forward columns, and .study_day() with the ADaM-standard default (TRTSDT):

adae = (
    ae_df.adam.occds("ADAE")
    .pin("ADSL", adsl)
    .source("USUBJID")
    .join_adsl("TRTSDT", "TRTEDT", "SAFFL")             # carry forward from ADSL
    .study_day("ASTDY", date_col="AESTDTC", ref_col="TRTSDT")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: FK validation
docs.text:
When a pin exists, Fleet can automatically check foreign-key integrity. By default it emits warnings for orphan values; use .fk_policy() to make it strict or silent:

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm
    .pin("DM", dm)
    .fk_policy("error")                                  # raise on FK violations
    .assign_no_ct("USUBJID", source="patient_number")   # FK auto-checked vs DM
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Lineage tracing
docs.text:
Every pin access is recorded. After building a pipeline, inspect pin lineage:

from fleet.core.lineage import pin_lineage_of

for dep in pin_lineage_of(ae_ns):
    print(f"{dep.target_col} ← {dep.source_domain}.{dep.source_cols} via {dep.verb}")
# AESTDY ← DM.['RFSTDTC'] via study_day

docs.title: Pipeline Debugging & Observability
docs.text: Fleet pipelines are lazy — all derivations accumulate until .to_frame() collects the result. This can make it hard to pinpoint which step introduced bad data or types. Two chainable verbs help:

docs.title: .inspect() — Hard Checkpoint
docs.text:
Materialises the pipeline at that point, prints schema, shape, and first rows, then returns a fresh namespace wrapping the collected frame. The pipeline resumes from this checkpoint.

adsl = (
    dm.adam.adsl
    .source("USUBJID")
    .first_date("TRTSDT", from_dataset=ex, date_col="EXSTDTC")
    .inspect(prefix="After TRTSDT")   # prints and checkpoints
    .duration("TRTDURD", start_date="TRTSDT", end_date="TRTEDT")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: .explain() — Query Plan
docs.text:
Prints the Polars logical plan without materialising. Useful for understanding how Polars optimises the accumulated derivation pipeline.

advs = (
    vs_raw.adam
    .source("USUBJID")
    .derivation("AVAL", expression="VSSTRESN")
    .explain()   # shows optimised plan
    .to_frame()
)

Both verbs are available on df.sdtm, df.adam, and all ADaM sub-namespaces.

docs.title: Custom Validation Rules
docs.text: When the standard CDISC CORE conformance rule set does not cover a study-specific requirement — a sponsor SOP constraint, an FDA Technical Conformance Guide (TCG) gap, or a protocol-specific range check — you can author custom rules and run them alongside the official rules.

docs.title: When to write custom rules
docs.text:
• Sponsor SOPs require checks not covered by CDISC CORE (e.g. mandatory SUPPQUAL variables).
  • FDA TCG requirements that have not yet been formalised as CORE rules.
  • Protocol-specific constraints such as custom reference ranges, visit windows, or dose limits.
  • Interim quality gates during study setup before official validation.

docs.title: 1. Configure the custom rules directory
docs.text:
In your study_config.yaml, set the custom_rules path:

validation:
  custom_rules: metadata/custom_rules  # directory for your .yaml rule files

fleet init cfg sets this up by default. The engine loads all .yaml files in this directory.

docs.title: 2. Scaffold a new rule
docs.text:
# Auto-increments ID: FLEET-AE-001, FLEET-AE-002, …
uv run fleet add-rule --domain AE --description "AESEV must be populated when AESER = Y"

# Custom prefix
uv run fleet add-rule --domain AE --prefix ROCHE --description "Severity required for serious AEs"

# Explicit ID (skips auto-increment)
uv run fleet add-rule --domain VS --id ROCHE-VS-010 --description "VSORRES range check"

# Output to a specific directory (overrides study_config)
uv run fleet add-rule --domain AE --description "Custom check" --output ./my_rules/

docs.title: 3. Edit the Check block
docs.text:
Open the generated YAML and fill in your validation logic in the Check: section:

Check:
  all:
    - name: AESER
      operator: equal_to
      value: "Y"
      value_is_literal: true
    - name: AESEV
      operator: empty

docs.title: 4. Run validation
docs.text:
# Inline in a pipeline
ae = (
    raw_df.sdtm.hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .validate("AE", custom_rules="metadata/custom_rules")
    .to_frame()
)

# Or via the ValidationService
from fleet.validation.service import ValidationService

svc = ValidationService()
result = svc.validate_sdtm(ae, domain="AE", custom_rules="metadata/custom_rules")
result.print_report()

docs.title: Rule anatomy
docs.text:
A custom rule follows the same YAML schema as CDISC CORE rules. Here is an annotated example:

Core:
  Id: FLEET-AE-001          # Unique ID (auto-generated by fleet add-rule)
  Status: Draft
  Version: "1"

Rule Type: Record Data       # Record-level check

Scope:
  Classes:
    Include: [EVENTS]
  Domains:
    Include: [AE]            # Restrict to the AE domain

Check:                       # The validation logic (what you write)
  all:
    - name: AESER
      operator: equal_to
      value: "Y"
      value_is_literal: true
    - name: AESEV
      operator: empty

Outcome:
  Message: >-
    AESEV is empty for a record where AESER = 'Y'. Serious adverse events
    must have severity documented.
  Output Variables: [USUBJID, AETERM, AESER, AESEV]

Description: >-
  AESEV must be populated when AESER = 'Y'.

Authorities:
  - Organization: Fleet
    Standards:
      - Name: SDTMIG
        Version: "3.4"
        References:
          - Origin: Sponsor SOP
            Rule Identifier:
              Id: FLEET-AE-001
              Version: "1"

Sensitivity: Record
Executability: Fully Executable

docs.title: The check DSL
docs.text:
CDISC CORE rules use a JSON/YAML check DSL built from composable operators:

Combinator Meaning all All conditions must be true (AND) any At least one condition is true (OR) not Negates the enclosed condition

Each leaf condition specifies a variable name, an operator, and optionally a value:

Check:
  all:
    - name: AESEV
      operator: is_contained_by
      value: ["MILD", "MODERATE", "SEVERE"]
    - name: AESER
      operator: equal_to
      value: "Y"
      value_is_literal: true

docs.title: Available operators
docs.text:
Operator Description equal_to Exact match not_equal_to Not equal empty Variable is null/blank non_empty Variable has a value less_than / greater_than Numeric/date comparison less_than_or_equal_to / greater_than_or_equal_to Inclusive comparison contains / does_not_contain Substring check is_contained_by Value is in a list starts_with / ends_with Prefix/suffix check matches_regex Regex pattern match date_less_than / date_greater_than Date comparison

For the full operator reference, see the CDISC CORE Rule Editor.

docs.title: Configuration and resolution order
docs.text:
Fleet resolves custom rules from multiple sources. The first match wins:

  1. Explicit custom_rules= parameter on .validate() or ValidationService methods.
  2. validation.custom_rules in study_config.yaml (team-wide default).
  3. None — no custom rules are loaded.

docs.title: Storing custom rules
docs.text:
Place custom rule files in the configured directory (default: metadata/custom_rules/):

my_study/
  study_config.yaml
  metadata/
    custom_rules/          ← Your sponsor-specific rules (all .yaml files loaded)
      FLEET-AE-001.yaml
      FLEET-AE-002.yaml
      ROCHE-VS-001.yaml
    sdtm/
      rules/               ← CDISC CORE rules (from fleet init rules)
    adam/
      rules/

Commit the directory to VCS so the complete rule inventory is versioned alongside the study.

docs.title: ID naming convention
docs.text:
Pattern Example Owner CORE-XXXXXX CORE-000001 CDISC (official — never reuse) <COMPANY>-<DOMAIN>-<NNN> ROCHE-AE-001 Your organisation FLEET-<DOMAIN>-<NNN> FLEET-DM-003 Default prefix

The --prefix flag on fleet add-rule controls the prefix. Auto-increment scans existing rules in the target directory to determine the next available sequence number.

docs.title: Uniqueness guarantee
docs.text: fleet add-rule checks all existing .yaml files in the target directory and refuses to create a rule if the Core.Id already exists. This prevents accidental overwrites.

docs.title: Validating rule schema locally
docs.text:
Before running rules through the engine, you can validate them against the vendored CDISC JSON Schema:

import json
import yaml
from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator
from pathlib import Path

schema_path = Path("src/fleet/validation/schemas/cdisc_rule_schema.json")
schema = json.loads(schema_path.read_text())

with open("metadata/custom_rules/FLEET-AE-001.yaml") as f:
    rule = yaml.safe_load(f)

validator = Draft202012Validator(schema)
errors = list(validator.iter_errors(rule))
# errors == [] means the rule is schema-valid

docs.title: Contributing upstream
docs.text: If your custom rule addresses a gap that would benefit the broader CDISC community, consider contributing it back via the CDISC Rule Editor or the CORE GitHub repository.

docs.title: How define.yaml Drives DataFrame Creation
docs.text:
define.yaml is the single source of truth for a Fleet study. One file simultaneously:

  1. Declares all output variables (fed to Define-XML 2.1 generation)
  2. Specifies how each variable is derived (executed as a pipeline)
  3. Declares codelists and controlled terminology references
  4. Defines structural metadata (keys, class, structure label)

docs.title: File Layout
docs.text:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../../src/fleet/define_xml/schemas/define_spec_schema.json
study:
  id:             CDISCPILOT01
  standard:       ADAMIG
  standard_version: "1.1"

codelists:
  - oid: C66731
    name: Sex
    type: text
    items:
      - coded_value: "M"
        decode: MALE
      - coded_value: "F"
        decode: FEMALE

datasets:
  - name: ADSL
    label: Subject-Level Analysis Dataset
    structure: One record per subject
    keys: [STUDYID, USUBJID]
    inputs:
      - name: DM
        type: dataset
    variables:
      - name: STUDYID
        ...

The schema is validated by the bundled JSON Schema (define_spec_schema.json), which means editors with YAML language server support provide auto-complete and inline error highlighting.

docs.title: Derivation Algorithms
docs.text:
Each variable's derivation.algorithm maps directly to an .adsl (or .adam) verb:

algorithm Namespace verb What it does assigned .assigned(target, value=...) Constant literal for all rows source .source(target, from_col=...) Copy column from predecessor derivation .derivation(target, expression=...) Arbitrary Polars expression first_date .first_date(target, from_dataset=..., date_col=..., where=...) Earliest event date per subject last_date .last_date(...) Latest event date per subject duration .duration(target, start_date=..., end_date=...) Integer day count flag .flag(target, criteria=...) "Y" / null flag count .count_events(target, from_dataset=..., where=...) Integer event count

docs.title: Study-specific callables (callable:)
docs.text:
When no built-in verb fits, point derivation: at a registered derivation name or a fully qualified Python dotted path. The runtime dispatch depends on the callable's kind:

  • kind="column" (zero-arg, returns pl.Expr) — stays fully lazy, no DataFrame materialisation.
  • kind="frame" or kind="param" (receives upstream DataFrame, returns pl.DataFrame) — the pipeline is materialised at that point, the function is called, and the result is wrapped back into the namespace.
- name: AGEGR1
  derivation:
    algorithm: callable
    callable: examples.cdiscpilot01.adam.derivations.AGEGR1

Or use the registered short name (if the derivations module was imported):

- name: AGEGR1
  derivation:
    callable: AGEGR1 # algorithm: callable injected automatically

docs.title: Derivations folder convention
docs.text:
Study derivations live under:

specs/<study_id>/adam/derivations/
    __init__.py        # auto-updated by `fleet derivation add`
    AGEGR1.py
    BMI.py

fleet init cfg creates the empty derivations/__init__.py automatically. fleet derivation add AGEGR1 --dataset ADSL scaffolds a new derivation file and appends the import to __init__.py.

Both algorithm: and callable: plug into Define-XML method enrichment: running DefineSpecGenerator(spec, enrich_methods=True) (or fleet define-xml --enrich-methods) emits a <MethodDef> whose <Description> is taken from the docstring of the callable. When the callable is a @derivation-decorated object, its dotted_path is used as the <FormalExpression> context, giving a verifiable link between the regulatory submission and the exact code that produced the data.

docs.title: Example — TRTSDT (date of first dose)
docs.text:
In define.yaml:

- name: TRTSDT
  label: Date of First Exposure to Treatment
  type: date
  origin: Derived
  derivation:
    algorithm: first_date
    from_dataset: EX
    date_col: EXSTDTC
    where: 'pl.col("EXDOSE") > 0'

Equivalent hand-written pipeline:

adsl = (
    dm_sdtm.adsl
    ...
    .first_date("TRTSDT", from_dataset=ex_sdtm,
                date_col="EXSTDTC",
                where='pl.col("EXDOSE") > 0')
    ...
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: End-to-End Flow
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[define.yaml] -->|parsed| B[DefineSpecGenerator]
    B -->|variable metadata| C[DefineXMLGenerator]
    B -->|derivation specs| D[StudyContext.build]
    D -->|applies verbs| E[Polars pipeline]
    E -->|calls .to_frame| F[ADSL DataFrame]
    C --> G[define_adam.xml]
    F --> H[adsl.parquet / adsl.csv]
    F --> I[DatasetChecker / ValidationService]

docs.title: Running the full pipeline programmatically
docs.text:
from fleet import load_study_context

ctx = load_study_context("examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/define.yaml")

# Build every dataset declared in the spec
adsl = ctx.build("ADSL")   # returns a polars.DataFrame
advs = ctx.build("ADVS")

docs.title: Generating Define-XML from the same spec
docs.text:
from fleet import DefineXMLGenerator

gen = DefineXMLGenerator("examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/define.yaml")
gen.write("outputs/cdiscpilot01/define_adam.xml")

docs.title: Codelist References
docs.text:
Variables can reference codelists declared in the codelists block:

- name: SEX
  label: Sex
  type: text
  codelist: C66731 # references the oid in codelists[]
  derivation:
    algorithm: source
    source: SEX

Fleet threads CT validation through the pipeline automatically — invalid values raise a CTError at runtime.

docs.title: Schema Validation — What, When, and How
docs.text: Fleet has two independent layers of schema validation for define.yaml. They run at different points and catch different classes of error.

docs.title: Layer 1 — Pydantic model validation (pipeline-build time)
docs.text:
When you call .from_spec() on an SDTM or ADaM namespace, Fleet parses each variable's derivation block through a Pydantic model (SDTMVariableSpec / ADAMVariableSpec). This runs immediately when .from_spec() is called, before any data is loaded.

What it catches:

  • Missing required fields for a given algorithm (e.g. assign_ct without ct_codelist)
  • Unknown algorithm names
  • Wrong field types (e.g. a list where a string is expected)
# define.yaml snippet with a bug — assign_ct is missing ct_codelist:
#   - name: SEX
#     derivation:
#       algorithm: assign_ct
#       source: sex               ← ct_codelist is required but absent

dm = raw_df.sdtm.from_spec("specs/define.yaml", dataset="DM")
# Raises pydantic.ValidationError immediately at this line, before .to_frame() is ever called.
# pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for SDTMVariableSpec
#   ct_codelist
#     Field required [type=missing, ...]

docs.title: Layer 2 — JSON Schema + business rule validation (DefineValidator)
docs.text:
DefineValidator runs a deeper structural check against the bundled JSON Schema (src/fleet/define_xml/schemas/define_xml_2_1_schema.json) and a set of CDISC business rules. This layer fires on demand, not automatically during pipeline execution.

Trigger it explicitly — before generating Define-XML or before submission:

from fleet.define_xml import DefineValidator
from pathlib import Path

validator = DefineValidator()
is_valid = validator.validate(Path("examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/define.yaml"))

for issue in validator.issues:
    print(f"[{issue.severity.upper()}] {issue.rule} @ {issue.location}: {issue.message}")

# Example output:
# [ERROR]   SCHEMA_001 @ datasets.0.variables.2: 'type' is a required property
# [ERROR]   BR03 @ datasets.0.variables.5.codelist: CodeListRef 'C99999' not found in codelists[]
# [WARNING] ALG02 @ datasets.0.variables.3: assign_ct should have ct_codelist declared

What it catches:

Rule Checks SCHEMA_001 All fields conform to the JSON Schema (types, required properties) BR01 Every dataset has at least one key variable BR02 All ItemRef references resolve to declared variables BR03 All codelist: references resolve to codelists declared in the spec BR04 All MethodDef references resolve ALG01 assign_no_ct has source_variable ALG02 assign_ct has both source_variable and ct_codelist ALG03 hardcode_* has constant_value ALG05 merge has merge_dataset and merge_key

validator.issues is a list of DefineIssue dataclasses with fields severity, location, message, and rule. validator.has_errors() returns True when any "error" severity issues exist. Warnings do not block Define-XML generation.

docs.title: When to run each layer
docs.text: Layer When it fires Blocks execution? Pydantic models Automatically on .from_spec() call Yes — raises ValidationError DefineValidator Manually, before Define-XML generation Only has_errors() returns True; you decide how to handle it CDISC Rules Engine Manually, after datasets are materialised No — report only

docs.title: JSON Schema & Editor Support
docs.text:
The YAML spec is validated against the bundled schema at:

src/fleet/define_xml/schemas/define_spec_schema.json

Add this comment to the top of every spec file to activate YAML language-server auto-complete in VS Code or any LSP-enabled editor:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../../src/fleet/define_xml/schemas/define_spec_schema.json

docs.title: CRF Page References
docs.text: Variables with origin: CRF can include page references to the annotated Case Report Form PDF. Fleet emits these as <def:DocumentRef> / <def:PDFPageRef> elements inside <def:Origin> in the Define-XML, and the standard define2-1.xsl stylesheet renders them as clickable links.

docs.title: Setup: declare the aCRF document
docs.text:
Add a documents block to the study: section:

study:
  id: CDISCPILOT01
  standard: SDTMIG
  standard_version: "3.4"
  documents:
    annotated_crf:
      href: blankcrf.pdf # path in the submission package
      title: Annotated Case Report Form # displayed in Define-XML

This emits the top-level <def:AnnotatedCRF> container and the <def:leaf> element that the XSLT needs to render document links.

docs.title: Layer 1 — Simple page strings (most common)
docs.text:
Add crf_pages to any CRF-origin variable:

variables:
  - name: SEX
    label: Sex
    type: text
    origin: CRF
    crf_pages: "8" # single page
    derivation:
      algorithm: assign_ct
      source: sex

  - name: RACE
    label: Race
    type: text
    origin: CRF
    crf_pages: "8 9" # space-separated multiple pages

The string value maps directly to the PageRefs attribute with Type="PhysicalRef".

docs.title: Layer 2 — Rich references (named destinations, page ranges)
docs.text:
For PDF bookmarks or page ranges, use the dict form:

- name: SEX
  origin: CRF
  crf_pages:
    pages: "DM_SEX" # PDF bookmark name
    type: NamedDestination # or PhysicalRef (default)

- name: RACE
  origin: CRF
  crf_pages:
    pages: "8 9"
    type: PhysicalRef
    first_page: "8" # optional range attributes
    last_page: "9"

docs.title: Layer 3 — External page map (EDC-driven workflows)
docs.text:
For studies where CRF annotations are extracted from an EDC system, point to an external YAML file:

study:
  documents:
    annotated_crf:
      href: blankcrf.pdf
      page_map: acrf_pages.yaml # relative to the define.yaml directory

The page map file uses DOMAIN.VARIABLE keys:

# acrf_pages.yaml — auto-generated from EDC export
DM.SEX: "7"
DM.BRTHDTC: "8"
AE.AETERM: "12 13"
VS.VSTESTCD: "20"

Inline crf_pages on individual variables always take precedence over the external page map.

docs.title: Supplemental documents
docs.text:
Additional supporting documents (reviewer's guide, protocol, etc.) can be declared alongside the annotated CRF:

study:
  documents:
    annotated_crf:
      href: blankcrf.pdf
    supplemental_docs:
      - id: LF.ReviewerGuide
        href: reviewers-guide.pdf
        title: Reviewer's Guide

These emit <def:SupplementalDoc> and corresponding <def:leaf> elements.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• The inputs block declares which upstream datasets the pipeline should join/merge.
  • Variables with no derivation block are expected to flow in via the source dataset — they appear in Define-XML as origin: CRF.
  • Run DefineValidator("...").validate(Path("specs/.../define.yaml")) to catch schema and business rule errors before generating Define-XML or running pipelines.

docs.title: Event-Priority Derivation with pick()
docs.text: Many ADaM variables require scanning multiple data sources in a defined priority order and selecting the first (or last) qualifying value. Admiral calls this pattern derive_vars_extreme_event / event(). Fleet provides pick() — a single verb that replaces multi-step joins, coalesces, and manual priority logic.

docs.title: The Problem
docs.text:
Consider LSTALVDT (Last Date Known Alive). The derivation spec typically reads:

Set LSTALVDT to the latest date from:

  1. Death date (DTHDT) — if the subject died
  2. Last AE end date (AEENDTC)
  3. Last AE start date (AESTDTC)
  4. Treatment end date (TRTEDT) — fallback

Each "event" has its own source dataset, filter condition, and column to extract. The first event that matches (in priority order) wins for each subject.

Without pick(), you'd need:

# Manual approach — 4 last_date lookups + coalesce
adsl = (
    adsl.adam.adsl.last_date("_dth", from_dataset=adsl_df, date_col="DTHDT")
    .last_date("_ae_end", from_dataset=ae, date_col="AEENDTC")
    .last_date("_ae_start", from_dataset=ae, date_col="AESTDTC")
    .derivation("LSTALVDT", expression='pl.coalesce("_dth", "_ae_end", "_ae_start", "TRTEDT")')
    .to_frame()
    .drop(["_dth", "_ae_end", "_ae_start"])
)

This is verbose, error-prone (column ordering = priority), and loses traceability.

docs.title: The Solution: pick()
docs.text:
adsl = adsl.adam.adsl.pick(
    "LSTALVDT",
    events=[
        {
            "when": pl.col("DTHDT").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "DTHDT"},
            "source": adsl_df,
            "label": "Death date",
        },
        {
            "when": pl.col("AEENDTC").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "AEENDTC"},
            "source": ae,
            "label": "AE end date",
        },
        {
            "when": pl.col("AESTDTC").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "AESTDTC"},
            "source": ae,
            "label": "AE start date",
        },
        {
            "when": pl.col("TRTEDT").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "TRTEDT"},
            "label": "Treatment end (self)",
        },
    ],
    by=["USUBJID"],
    order=["LSTALVDT"],
    mode="last",
).to_frame()

Priority is explicit in list order. Each event's "label" documents intent. No temporary columns needed.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Events list: ordered by priority] --> B{For each event}
    B --> C[Filter source by 'when' condition]
    C --> D[Apply 'set' mappings to targets]
    D --> E[Group by 'by' vars]
    E --> F[Select record per mode/order]
    F --> G[Tag with event priority number]
    G --> H[Stack all candidate records]
    H --> I[Sort by priority, then order]
    I --> J[Keep first per group = winner]
    J --> K[Left-join targets back to base frame]

Key properties:

  1. Priority = list position. Event at index 0 beats index 1, regardless of dates.
  2. Within-event selection uses mode ("first" or "last") + order (sort columns).
  3. Cross-event winner is the highest-priority event that has qualifying records.
  4. Subjects with no matching events get null for all targets.

docs.title: Event Dict Reference
docs.text:
Each event is a Python dict with these keys:

Key Required Type Description "when" Yes str \| pl.Expr Boolean filter — which records qualify "set" Yes dict[str, str \| pl.Expr \| Any] Maps each target to a source column name, expression, or literal "source" No pl.DataFrame External dataset to scan. Omit to use the current pipeline frame "mode" No str Override top-level mode for this event ("first" / "last") "order" No str \| list[str] Override top-level sort for this event "label" No str Documentation-only description (ignored at runtime)

docs.title: Multiple Targets
docs.text:
pick() can derive several columns simultaneously from the same event cascade:

adsl = adsl.adam.adsl.pick(
    ["LSTALVDT", "DTHFL"],
    events=[
        {
            "when": pl.col("DTHDT").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "DTHDT", "DTHFL": pl.lit("Y")},
            "source": adsl_df,
        },
        {
            "when": pl.col("AEENDTC").is_not_null(),
            "set": {"LSTALVDT": "AEENDTC", "DTHFL": pl.lit("N")},
            "source": ae,
        },
    ],
    by=["USUBJID"],
    order=["LSTALVDT"],
    mode="last",
).to_frame()

When an event only sets some targets, the others remain null for that event's candidates.

docs.title: String Conditions (YAML-Compatible)
docs.text:
For spec-driven pipelines, conditions can be strings that get evaluated safely:

events = [
    {"when": 'pl.col("DTHDT").is_not_null()', "set": {"LSTALVDT": "DTHDT"}},
]

This is equivalent to passing a pl.Expr directly and enables full round-tripping through define.yaml.

docs.title: Admiral Comparison
docs.text:
Admiral Fleet event(dataset, condition, set_values_to, order, mode) Event dict in events list derive_vars_extreme_event(events, source_datasets, by_vars, order, mode, check_type) .pick(targets, events=..., by=..., order=..., mode=...) Priority = position in event() list Priority = position in events list Requires pre-built event objects + explicit dataset references Inline dicts with optional "source" — current frame used by default

Fleet's pick() is semantically equivalent but:

  • Eliminates the need for a separate event() constructor
  • Supports per-event mode/order overrides
  • Accepts literals (pl.lit("Y")) directly in "set" alongside column references
  • Chains naturally into the ADaM pipeline without materialisation breaks

docs.title: When to Use pick() vs @derivation
docs.text:
Scenario Use Multi-source priority cascade (LSTALVDT, DTHCAUS, LDDTHELD) pick() Simple conditional (AGEGR1, EOSSTT) condderivation() Complex cross-record logic within one source (CBOR confirmation rules) @derivation(kind="frame") Aggregation that needs custom grouping (derived parameters) derive_param()

Rule of thumb: If your logic is "try source A, then B, then C" — use pick(). If it requires comparing multiple records within the same subject to determine a single result (e.g., sustained response confirmation), use a @derivation.

docs.title: Spec-Driven Usage
docs.text:
In a define.yaml, the pick algorithm maps directly:

variables:
  - name: LSTALVDT
    label: Last Date Known Alive
    algorithm: pick
    targets: [LSTALVDT]
    events:
      - when: 'pl.col("DTHDT").is_not_null()'
        set: {LSTALVDT: DTHDT}
        source: ADSL
      - when: 'pl.col("AEENDTC").is_not_null()'
        set: {LSTALVDT: AEENDTC}
        source: AE
    by: [USUBJID]
    order: [LSTALVDT]
    mode: last

Fleet's from_spec() dispatches to .pick() automatically when algorithm: pick is detected.

docs.title: Namespace Pipeline Architecture
docs.text: When using Fleet, you have two primary ways to create datasets: Code-driven (writing Python pipelines manually) or Spec-driven (authoring a define.yaml and having Fleet write the pipelines for you).

docs.title: The Recommended Approach: Spec-First with Custom Extensions
docs.text:
For the majority of modern statistical programming tasks, we highly recommend a hybrid "Spec-First" workflow.

In this approach, you let AI or your documentation team generate the define.yaml. Fleet consumes this YAML to automatically manage 90% of the derivations, dependencies, traceability, and Define-XML generation. Then, for the 10% of highly complex, proprietary derivations that do not fit neatly into a YAML file, you apply a thin layer of manual Polars python code on top of the built data step.

This hybrid approach ensures high reproducibility and documentation sync, while leaving an "escape hatch" open for when code must take over.

docs.title: 1. Code-Driven (Inline Python)
docs.text:
Best for: Quick exploration, ad-hoc analysis, smaller studies, or initial data discovery.

You construct your pipelines entirely in Python by chaining namespace verbs on Polars DataFrames. All logic is embedded directly in your scripts.

Example:

adsl = dm.adam.adsl.source("USUBJID").duration("ADY", start="TRTSDT", end="ADT").to_frame()

docs.title: 2. Spec-Driven (define.yaml)
docs.text:
Best for: Production clinical trials, regulatory submissions, repeatability across projects.

You define metadata, controlled terminology, and derivations in a central define.yaml file. Fleet reads the specification and automatically builds the datasets. In this model, your Python scripts simply load the study context and call .build().

Example of the Hybrid Escape Hatch:

# The standard derivations live in define.yaml.
from fleet import load_study_context
import polars as pl

ctx = load_study_context("specs/study01/adam/define.yaml")
base_adsl = ctx.build("ADSL")

# Add custom logic for the 10% of edge-case scenarios not covered by the spec:
final_adsl = base_adsl.adam.adsl.derivation(
    "CUSTOM_FLAG", expression=pl.when(pl.col("AGE") > 80).then(pl.lit("Y")).otherwise(pl.lit("N"))
).to_frame()

docs.title: How the pipeline works underneath
docs.text:
Every Fleet namespace (sdtm, adam, adsl, occds) follows the same pattern:

  1. Access the namespace on a Polars DataFrame: df.sdtm
  2. Chain verb calls — each returns a new namespace object accumulating pl.Expr objects
  3. Materialise with .to_frame() — executes a single df.with_columns(...) pass
result = (
    raw_df.sdtm.assign_no_ct("USUBJID", source="patient_id")  # 1. access  # 2. chain
    .hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign_ct("SEX", source="sex_raw", ct_codelist=SEX, ct_mapping={"M": "M", "F": "F"})
    .to_frame()  # 3. materialise
)

Nothing runs at step 2 — verbs only build an internal expression list.

To inspect intermediate state or the query plan during development, use the chainable debug verbs .inspect() (hard checkpoint with diagnostic output) and .explain() (print the Polars query plan). See Advanced Patterns for details.

docs.title: Lazy evaluation
docs.text:
df.sdtm
  │
  ├─ .assign_no_ct("USUBJID", ...)  →  [Expr("patient_id".alias("USUBJID"))]
  ├─ .assign_ct("SEX", ...)         →  [..., Expr(when/then.alias("SEX"))]
  └─ .to_frame()
       │
       └─ df.with_columns(*exprs)   ← single Polars pass

This means you pay no cost for columns you don't chain. Expression ordering mirrors declaration order.

docs.title: SDTM verbs at a glance
docs.text: Verb Purpose assign_no_ct(target, source) Copy raw column, no CT validation hardcode_no_ct(target, value) Constant literal for all rows assign_ct(target, source, ct_codelist, ct_mapping) Recode values through a CT codelist date(target, source) Normalise to ISO 8601 date or datetime derivation(target, expression) Arbitrary pl.Expr if_then_else(target, when, else_value) Multi-branch conditional to_frame() Materialise

docs.text: Verb Purpose source(target) Pass-through column derivation(target, expression) Arbitrary pl.Expr assigned(target, value) Constant literal date(target, source) Parse DTC → Date/Datetime with imputation duration(target, start, end) CDISC study day / elapsed time flag(target, criteria, groups) Per-group boolean flag baseline(target, aval, baseline_flag) Carry baseline AVAL within groups chg(target, aval, base) Change from baseline pchg(target, aval, base) Percent change from baseline bmi(target, weight, height) Body Mass Index nrind(target, value, low, high) Normal range indicator (LOW/NORMAL/HIGH) on_treatment(target, adt, trtsdt, trtedt) On-treatment flag shift(target, baseline_cat, post_cat) Categorical shift string bsa(target, weight, height, method) Body Surface Area (4 methods) map(target, systolic, diastolic) Mean Arterial Pressure qtc(target, qt, rr, method) Corrected QT interval (Fridericia/Bazett) derive_summary_records(by_vars, ...) Aggregate by group, append summary rows derive_locf_records(by_vars, ...) Forward-fill (LOCF) within patient groups derive_param(by_vars, ...) Derive a new parameter and append as rows to_frame() Materialise

docs.title: StudyContext — workspace initialisation
docs.text:
The recommended way to start a new study is the bootstrapping pipeline via the Fleet CLI:

fleet init cfg --study-id STUDY01 --company "Acme Pharma" \
  --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --adam-datasets ADSL,ADVS --root ./studies/STUDY01
fleet init define --config ./studies/STUDY01/study_config.yaml  # queries CDISC Library IG → define.yaml
fleet init ct     --config ./studies/STUDY01/study_config.yaml  # reads define.yaml → codelists.py

Note

When --root points to a non-current directory, pass --config <root>/study_config.yaml to init define and init ct, or cd into the root directory before running them.

See the CLI Reference for full details.

StudyContext.init() can also be used programmatically — it creates the folder tree and writes study_config.yaml. Define specs and codelists are produced by the subsequent pipeline steps (fleet init define, fleet init ct).

from fleet import StudyContext, SDTMConfig, ADAMConfig, load_study_context
from pathlib import Path

# ── Once, when starting a new study ──────────────────────────────────────
ctx = StudyContext.init(
    "./studies/STUDY01",
    study_id="STUDY01",
    company="Acme Pharma",
    sdtm=SDTMConfig(ig_version="3-4", domains=["DM", "AE", "VS", "EX"]),
    adam=ADAMConfig(ig_version="1-1", datasets=["ADSL", "ADVS"]),
)

# ── Every subsequent session ──────────────────────────────────────────────
ctx = load_study_context(Path("./studies/STUDY01/study_config.yaml"))
Outcome Behaviour Directories already exist Silently skipped (mkdir -p semantics) study_config.yaml exists Raises StudyConfigError — use load_study_context() instead

docs.title: Trial Design Domains
docs.text: Fleet provides first-class support for all seven CDISC Trial Design Model (TDD) domains through a fixed-sequence verb pipeline with rich Pydantic models and collection-level validators.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Domain Full Name Structure Type TE Trial Elements 1 rec/element Protocol-reference TA Trial Arms 1 rec/element/arm Protocol-reference TV Trial Visits 1 rec/visit/arm Protocol-reference TS Trial Summary 1 rec/parameter Protocol-reference TI Trial Inclusion/Exclusion 1 rec/criterion Protocol-reference SV Subject Visits 1 rec/subject/visit Subject-level SE Subject Elements 1 rec/subject/element Subject-level

docs.title: Domain Dependency Chain
docs.text:
TA + TE → TV → SV
TE + TA → SE

docs.title: Protocol-Reference Domains
docs.text:
Protocol-reference domains (TE, TA, TV, TS, TI) follow a fixed sequence:

fetch_structure() → study_header() → add_*() → to_frame()

Each step validates that the previous step was completed. Calling verbs out of order raises a ValueError with a descriptive message.

from fleet.sdtm.tdd import TrialElement, TrialElements, Epoch

# 1. Define your trial elements using rich Pydantic models
te_rows = TrialElements(
    elements=[
        TrialElement(
            etcd="SCRN",
            element="Screening",
            testrl="INFORMED CONSENT",
            teenrl="RANDOMIZATION - 1",
            tedur="P14D",
            epoch=Epoch.SCREENING,
        ),
        TrialElement(
            etcd="TRT",
            element="Treatment",
            testrl="RANDOMIZATION",
            teenrl="END OF TREATMENT",
            tedur="P84D",
            epoch=Epoch.TREATMENT,
        ),
        TrialElement(
            etcd="FU",
            element="Follow-up",
            testrl="END OF TREATMENT + 1",
            teenrl="END OF FOLLOW-UP",
            tedur="P28D",
            epoch=Epoch.FOLLOW_UP,
        ),
    ]
)

# 2. Build the pipeline
te = (
    pl.DataFrame()
    .sdtm.fetch_structure("TE", ig_version="3-4", save_to="metadata/sdtm/te_structure.yaml")
    .study_header(study_id="CDISCPILOT01", domain="TE")
    .add_elements(te_rows)
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Subject-Level Domains
docs.text:
Subject-level domains (SV, SE) use derivation verbs that freely mix with existing SDTM verbs:

sv = (
    raw_visits.sdtm.hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN", value="SV")
    .assign_no_ct("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .assign_dtc("SVSTDTC", source="visit_date")
    .visit_map(
        "VISITNUM",
        "VISIT",
        date_col="SVSTDTC",
        planned_visits=tv_rows,
        ref_date="RFSTDTC",
        tolerance={"before": 3, "after": 3},
    )
    .study_day("SVSTDY", date_col="SVSTDTC", ref_date_col="RFSTDTC")
    .epoch_assign("EPOCH", date_col="SVSTDTC", epoch_ranges=epoch_map)
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Collection Models
docs.text:
Every add_*() verb requires a collection model (not a bare list). Collections enforce integrity at construction time:

Collection Checks TrialElements Unique ETCD, epoch consistency TrialArms Sequential TAETORD per arm, FK to TE (opt.) TrialVisits Unique VISITNUM, VISITDY ordering TrialParameters Unique TSPARMCD TrialCriteria Unique IETESTCD

docs.title: Example: Collection Validation
docs.text:
# This raises ValueError — duplicate ETCD
TrialElements(
    elements=[
        TrialElement(etcd="SCRN", element="Screening", epoch=Epoch.SCREENING),
        TrialElement(etcd="SCRN", element="Screening 2", epoch=Epoch.SCREENING),
    ]
)
# ValueError: Duplicate ETCD: {'SCRN'}

docs.title: Cross-Domain FK Validation
docs.text:
Pass upstream collections to add_*() verbs for foreign-key validation. First, define the arm rows using the TrialArms / TrialArm models (each ETCD must match an element defined in te_rows above):

from fleet.sdtm.tdd import TrialArm, TrialArms

ta_rows = TrialArms(
    arms=[
        TrialArm(
            armcd="PBO",
            arm="Placebo",
            taetord=1,
            etcd="SCRN",
            element="Screening",
            epoch=Epoch.SCREENING,
        ),
        TrialArm(
            armcd="PBO",
            arm="Placebo",
            taetord=2,
            etcd="TRT",
            element="Treatment",
            epoch=Epoch.TREATMENT,
        ),
        TrialArm(
            armcd="PBO",
            arm="Placebo",
            taetord=3,
            etcd="FU",
            element="Follow-up",
            epoch=Epoch.FOLLOW_UP,
        ),
    ]
)

Then build TA with or without FK validation:

# Validates TA.ETCD ∈ TE.ETCD
ta = (
    pl.DataFrame()
    .sdtm.fetch_structure("TA")
    .study_header("CDISCPILOT01", "TA")
    .add_arms(ta_rows, te=te_rows)  # FK check
    .to_frame()
)

# Omit te= to skip FK check (iterative development)
ta_draft = (
    pl.DataFrame()
    .sdtm.fetch_structure("TA")
    .study_header("CDISCPILOT01", "TA")
    .add_arms(ta_rows)  # no FK check
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Schema Reconciliation
docs.text:
fetch_structure() queries the CDISC Library for the domain's IG metadata and compares it against Fleet's static Pydantic models. Discrepancies are reported as UserWarning:

  • Missing required variables: IG requires a field not in the model
  • Type mismatches: IG declares Num but model uses str
  • Codelist drift: IG links to a different codelist than the Epoch enum

docs.title: Epoch Enum
docs.text:
The Epoch enum is bound to NCI C99079 with all 14 standard values:

from fleet.sdtm.tdd import Epoch

Epoch.SCREENING  # "SCREENING"
Epoch.TREATMENT  # "TREATMENT"
Epoch.FOLLOW_UP  # "FOLLOW-UP"
Epoch.BASELINE  # "BASELINE"
# ... plus 10 more

docs.title: Mermaid Parser (Bonus)
docs.text:
Parse a Mermaid flowchart directly into TE and TA collections:

from fleet.sdtm.tdd import parse_trial_design

te, ta = parse_trial_design("""
    flowchart TD
    subgraph SCR[SCREENING]
        SCRN["Screening<br/>P14D"]
    end
    subgraph TRT[TREATMENT]
        TREAT["Treatment<br/>P84D"]
    end
    subgraph FU[FOLLOW-UP]
        FOLL["Follow-up<br/>P28D"]
    end
    SCRN --> TREAT
    TREAT --> FOLL
""")

docs.title: Code-Driven Pipeline (Inline)¶
docs.text:
Interactive Playground — Click the badge above to launch this notebook in Google Colab and experiment with Fleet live, no local setup needed.

This notebook demonstrates building clinical datasets entirely in Python code. It is best suited for quick ad-hoc analysis, smaller studies, or initial data discovery.

docs.title: 1. Derive SDTM¶
docs.text: We use the .sdtm namespace to standardize the raw inputs.

docs.title: 2. Derive ADaM¶
docs.text: We use the .adam namespace. Notice how easily we define a custom derivation to flag subjects who are older than 40.

docs.title: Spec-Driven Pipeline with Code Extensions
docs.text:
In [ ]: Copied! 
try:
    import fleet  # noqa: F401 — registers .sdtm / .adam namespaces
except ModuleNotFoundError:
    import importlib
    import subprocess
    import sys

    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "-q", "fleet-cdisc"])
    importlib.invalidate_caches()

import polars as pl

# Normally, we just build context:
# ctx = load_study_context('examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/define.yaml')

docs.title: Spec-Driven Pipeline with Code Extensions¶
docs.text:
Interactive Playground — Click the badge above to launch this notebook in Google Colab and experiment with Fleet live, no local setup needed.

This notebook demonstrates the standard workflow for Fleet in a production environment: Spec-First.

  1. You define as much as possible in define.yaml.
  2. Fleet automatically executes it.
  3. You write a thin layer of Python code for complex custom rules.

docs.title: Extending the Built Data¶
docs.text: Suppose define.yaml generated our base ADSL pipeline, but we have a completely proprietary calculation that the specification does not natively handle via its algorithms. We simply extend the resulting dataframe!

docs.title: End-to-End Walkthrough: Multi-Domain Pipeline
docs.text:
Interactive Playground — Click the badge above to launch a notebook in Google Colab and experiment with Fleet live, no local setup needed.

This guide walks you through building a complete, code-driven data pipeline. We will take synthetic raw data and map it into three SDTM domains (DM, VS, AE), and then derive two ADaM datasets (ADSL, ADVS).

You can find the full script in the examples/ directory under full_pipeline_example.py.

docs.title: 2. SDTM Derivation
docs.text: We map the raw datasets to SDTM variables using df.sdtm.

docs.title: DM (Demographics)
docs.text:
dm = (
    raw_dm.sdtm.hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .assign_no_ct("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .assign_no_ct("ARM", source="arm")
    .assign_ct("SEX", source="sex", ct_codelist=SEX, ct_mapping={"M": "M", "F": "F"})
    .assign_dtc("BRTHDTC", source="dob")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: VS (Vital Signs)
docs.text:
vs = (
    raw_vs.sdtm.hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN", value="VS")
    .assign_no_ct("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .assign_ct(
        "VSTESTCD",
        source="test_name",
        ct_codelist=VSTESTCD,
        ct_mapping={"Weight": "WEIGHT", "Heart Rate": "HR"},
    )
    .assign_no_ct("VSSTRESN", source="result")
    .assign_dtc("VSDTC", source="date")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: AE (Adverse Events)
docs.text:
ae = (
    raw_ae.sdtm.hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign_no_ct("USUBJID", source="subject_id")
    .assign_no_ct("AEDECOD", source="ae_term")
    .assign_dtc("AESTDTC", source="start_date")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: ADSL (Subject-Level Analysis)
docs.text:
ADSL aggregates information per subject. We source core demographics from dm, and then fetch the date of the first adverse event using the .first_date() verb from the ae dataset.

adsl = (
    dm.adam.adsl.source("USUBJID")
    .source("ARM")
    .source("SEX")
    .first_date(
        "TRTSDT", from_dataset=ae, date_col="AESTDTC"
    )  # For demonstration, using AE start date as proxy
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: ADVS (Vital Signs Analysis Dataset)
docs.text:
ADVS provides BDS-structured derivations like Day and Baseline. We join our derived vs dataset with adsl to obtain the reference date (TRTSDT), and apply BDS logic.

# First, pull in the required ADSL reference variables
vs_with_adsl = vs.join(adsl.select(["USUBJID", "TRTSDT"]), on="USUBJID", how="left")

advs = (
    vs_with_adsl.adam.source("USUBJID")
    .source("VSTESTCD")
    .source("VSSTRESN")
    # Identify Baseline logic (Dummy logic: first record is baseline)
    .derivation("ABLFL", expression=pl.lit("Y"))
    .baseline("BASE", aval="VSSTRESN", baseline_flag="ABLFL")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: In roughly 50 lines of code, we constructed an end-to-end multi-domain clinical pipeline that compiles into optimized execution plans and computes efficiently without intermediate pandas serialization!

docs.title: One file. One domain. Raw to Render.
docs.text:
The Raw-to-Render (R2R) strategy collapses the traditional multi-program pharma workflow into a single, self-contained script that takes raw source data all the way to a rendered clinical table:

ADSL (pre-built)  ─────────────────┐
                                    ▼
Raw AE CSV  →  SDTM AE  →  ADaM ADAE  →  Validate  →  TLG (HTML)

DM and ADSL are assumed to already exist — they are governed, shared artefacts produced by separate programs. The R2R script focuses on one domain end-to-end: raw AE data through SDTM, ADaM, validation, and table rendering.

Instead of maintaining separate programs for each layer — with hand-offs, naming conventions to remember, and scattered data lineage — an R2R script keeps the complete derivation chain for a single domain visible in one place.

docs.title: The traditional model
docs.text:
In conventional clinical programming, the AE deliverable involves at least four separate programs, often written by different people:

Program Input Output Owner ae.sas Raw AE extract SDTM AE SDTM prog. adae.sas SDTM AE + ADSL ADaM ADAE ADaM prog. adae_qc.sas ADAE Validation log QC prog. t_ae.sas ADAE + ADSL AE summary table TLG prog.

Each program runs independently. Context about why a particular derivation exists often lives only in the developer's head or in a Word document. When the table looks wrong, you debug backwards across four files, hoping the variable names haven't drifted.

docs.title: The R2R model
docs.text:
r2r_ae.py   ADSL (input) + Raw AE → SDTM AE → ADAE → validate → AE summary → HTML

One script. One review. When cell (3, 2) in the table looks wrong, scroll up — the derivation that produced it is in the same file.

DM and ADSL remain separate, governed programs — they are shared by many domains. The R2R script consumes ADSL as a pre-built input and owns everything else.

docs.title: Advantages
docs.text:
• Full lineage visibility — every transformation from raw value to table cell is traceable in a single scroll.
  • Faster debugging — no need to run four programs and cross-reference intermediate datasets; breakpoints anywhere in the chain.
  • Atomic reviews — a reviewer sees the complete picture; intent and implementation live together.
  • Agent-native — an AI coding agent can reason about the entire pipeline in one context window, generate it end-to-end, and fix issues without switching files.
  • Reproducible — one command (uv run python r2r_ae.py) regenerates everything from source.

docs.title: When to use R2R
docs.text:
R2R shines when:

  • You need to prototype fast — get a table on screen from raw data in minutes.
  • The domain is self-contained — AE, VS, LB, CM — where the analysis dataset depends only on its own SDTM domain plus ADSL.
  • You're working with an AI agent that benefits from seeing the full pipeline in one prompt.
  • You want a living specification — the code is the documentation of how raw data becomes a regulatory table.

docs.title: When NOT to use R2R
docs.text:
• Shared derivations — ADSL is consumed by many domains; it deserves its own program with governed outputs. The R2R script loads ADSL as an input — it does not derive it.
  • Large teams — when SDTM and ADaM are programmed by different people on different timelines, separation makes sense.
  • Validated production — regulatory submissions may require individual program-level sign-off; R2R is ideal for exploratory and rapid development before refactoring into governed programs.

docs.title: The Layers
docs.text: An R2R script is organised into clearly labelled layers. Each layer uses a different Fleet namespace:

docs.title: Layer 0 — Inputs
docs.text:
Load the pre-built ADSL and the raw AE extract:

import polars as pl
import fleet  # registers .sdtm / .adam / .tlg namespaces

# ADSL is produced by a separate governed program
adsl = pl.read_csv("outputs/cdiscpilot01/adsl_admiral.csv", try_parse_dates=True)
adsl = adsl.with_columns(pl.col("TRT01P").alias("TRTA"))

# Raw AE — the only raw data this script owns
ae_raw = pl.read_csv("datasets/cdiscpilot01/raw/ae_raw.csv")

docs.title: Layer 1 — SDTM (.sdtm namespace)
docs.text:
Standardise raw columns into CDISC-compliant SDTM variables:

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm.hardcode_no_ct("STUDYID", value="CDISCPILOT01")
    .hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign_no_ct("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
    .assign_no_ct("AETERM", source="ae_term")
    .assign_no_ct("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .assign_no_ct("AEENDTC", source="ae_end_date")
    .assign_no_ct("AESEV", source="ae_severity")
    .assign_no_ct("AESER", source="ae_serious")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Layer 2 — ADaM ADAE (.adam / .adam.occds namespaces)
docs.text:
Merge ADSL treatment dates into SDTM AE, then derive analysis dates, treatment-emergent flags, and worst-severity flags:

# Merge ADSL treatment dates & population flags into SDTM AE
_adsl_trt = adsl.select(["USUBJID", "TRTSDT", "TRTEDT", "TRT01P", "TRTA", "SAFFL"])
ae_with_trt = ae.join(_adsl_trt, on="USUBJID", how="left")

adae = (
    ae_with_trt.adam.source("STUDYID")
    .source("USUBJID")
    .source("AETERM")
    .source("TRTA")
    .source("SAFFL")
    .derive_dt("ASTDT", source="AESTDTC")
    .study_day("ADY", analysis_date="ASTDT", reference_date="TRTSDT")
    .to_frame()
    .adam.occds.treatment_emergent(
        "TRTEMFL",
        start_date="AESTDTC",
        trtsdt="TRTSDT",
        trtedt="TRTEDT",
    )
    .recode("AESEVN", source="AESEV", recode_map={"MILD": 1, "MODERATE": 2, "SEVERE": 3})
    .flag(
        "ANL01FL",
        criteria="max",
        value_col="AESEVN",
        groups=["USUBJID", "AETERM"],
    )
    .seq("ASEQ", groups=["USUBJID"])
    .to_frame()
)

docs.title: Layer 3 — Validate
docs.text:
Call .validate() directly in the pipeline chain — it prints the conformance report and returns the namespace unchanged so derivations can continue:

ae = (
    ae_raw.sdtm.hardcode_no_ct("STUDYID", value="CDISCPILOT01")
    .hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN", value="AE")
    .assign_no_ct("USUBJID", source="patient_number")
    .assign_no_ct("AETERM", source="ae_term")
    .assign_no_ct("AESTDTC", source="ae_start_date")
    .assign_no_ct("AEENDTC", source="ae_end_date")
    .assign_no_ct("AESEV", source="ae_severity")
    .assign_no_ct("AESER", source="ae_serious")
    .validate("AE")  # ← prints report, chain continues
    .to_frame()
)

adae = (
    ae_with_trt.adam.source("STUDYID")
    .source("USUBJID")
    .source("AETERM")
    .source("TRTA")
    .source("SAFFL")
    .derive_dt("ASTDT", source="AESTDTC")
    .study_day("ADY", analysis_date="ASTDT", reference_date="TRTSDT")
    .to_frame()
    .adam.occds.treatment_emergent(
        "TRTEMFL",
        start_date="AESTDTC",
        trtsdt="TRTSDT",
        trtedt="TRTEDT",
    )
    .recode("AESEVN", source="AESEV", recode_map={"MILD": 1, "MODERATE": 2, "SEVERE": 3})
    .flag(
        "ANL01FL",
        criteria="max",
        value_col="AESEVN",
        groups=["USUBJID", "AETERM"],
    )
    .seq("ASEQ", groups=["USUBJID"])
    .validate("ADAE")  # ← prints report, chain continues
    .to_frame()
)

The report printed to stdout makes conformance issues immediately visible:

======================================================================
CDISC Validation Report: AE
======================================================================
Dataset Type: SDTM 3.4
Status: FAIL
Total Issues: 2
----------------------------------------------------------------------

ERRORS (2):

1. [Error] SDTM.AE.R0001: AESEQ is required but missing
   Variable: AESEQ

2. [Error] SDTM.AE.R0014: AEBODSYS must be populated when AEDECOD is present
   Variable: AEBODSYS
   Rows: 43
   Producing verb: assign_no_ct (AETERM)
   Suggested fix: Map AEBODSYS from MedDRA lookup or hardcode domain SOC

======================================================================

======================================================================
CDISC Validation Report: ADAE
======================================================================
Dataset Type: ADaM 1.3
Status: PASS
Total Issues: 0
----------------------------------------------------------------------

======================================================================

The Producing verb field traces an error directly back to the Fleet verb that created the offending column — no manual variable hunting required.

docs.title: Layer 4 — Render (.tlg.ae namespace)
docs.text:
Compute the Analysis Results Dataset and render to HTML:

from fleet.tlg import (
    AESummarySpec,
    Row,
    Statistic,
    RenderMetadata,
    ard_to_table_model,
    render_html,
)

spec = AESummarySpec(
    rows=[
        Row(field="AEBODSYS", label="System Organ Class"),
        Row(field="AEDECOD", label="Preferred Term"),
    ],
    statistics=[Statistic.N_SUBJECTS, Statistic.N_PCT],
)

ard = adae.tlg.ae.t_summary(spec=spec, adsl=adsl)

meta = RenderMetadata(
    title="Table 14.3.1.1",
    subtitle="AE Summary by SOC and PT",
    footnotes=["Source: ADAE", "Population: Safety"],
)
html = render_html(ard_to_table_model(ard, meta))
Path("outputs/ae_r2r.html").write_text(html)

docs.title: R2R and Agentic Coding
docs.text:
The R2R strategy is purpose-built for AI agents. Here's why:

  1. Single-context reasoning — The entire derivation fits in one file (and one prompt). An agent doesn't need to discover dependencies across a file tree.

  2. End-to-end generation — Given a raw dataset schema and a target table shell, an agent can generate a complete R2R script in one pass — no multi-turn orchestration.

  3. Instant feedback — The script produces a visible output (HTML table). The agent (or user) can inspect the result and iterate without leaving the file.

  4. Self-documenting — The layered structure doubles as executable documentation. An agent reading the file can explain every derivation decision from raw to table.

  5. Deterministic re-execution — One uv run python r2r_ae.py reproduces the full artefact. No DAG scheduler, no Makefile, no external state.

docs.title: Agent prompt pattern
docs.text:
"Using Fleet's R2R pattern, write a single Python script that takes ae_raw.csv and a pre-built ADSL (adsl_admiral.csv) and produces an HTML AE summary table (Table 14.3.1.1). Include SDTM AE, ADAE with treatment-emergent flags, pre-validation, and a rendered HTML output."

The agent returns a complete, runnable script — no follow-up questions needed.

docs.title: Running the Example
docs.text:
The full working example is at examples/r2r_ae_example.py:

uv run python examples/r2r_ae_example.py

Output:

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
Fleet provides the fleet command-line tool for bootstrapping studies, generating define specs, managing CDISC Controlled Terminology, and producing Define-XML. Commands that query the CDISC Library require a valid CDISC_API_KEY — set it in a .env file at your project root or as an environment variable.

.env
CDISC_API_KEY=your-api-key-here

docs.title: Bootstrapping Pipeline
docs.text:
The recommended way to start a new study. Run these three commands in order:

fleet init cfg    --study-id STUDY01 --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --adam-datasets ADSL,ADVS
fleet init define                      # reads study_config.yaml, queries CDISC IG
fleet init ct                          # reads define.yaml, downloads codelists

Using --root?

If you pass --root to init cfg (e.g. --root ./my_study), the config is written to ./my_study/study_config.yaml instead of the current directory. You must then pass --config ./my_study/study_config.yaml to every subsequent init command — or cd into that directory before running them:

```bash
fleet init cfg --study-id STUDY01 --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --root ./my_study
fleet init define --config ./my_study/study_config.yaml
fleet init ct     --config ./my_study/study_config.yaml
```

docs.title: fleet init cfg
docs.text:
Create study_config.yaml and the study directory structure.

fleet init cfg --study-id CDISCPILOT01 --company "CDISC" \
  --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --adam-datasets ADSL,ADVS,ADAE --root ./my_study
Option Default Description --study-id (required) Study identifier --company (none) Originator / company name --domains (none) Comma-separated SDTM domains --adam-datasets (none) Comma-separated ADaM datasets --ig 3-4 SDTM IG version --adam-ig 1-1 ADaM IG version --package sdtmct-2023-12-15 CT package version --root / -r . Study root directory

Non-default --root requires --config in subsequent commands

When --root is set to anything other than ., the generated study_config.yaml lives inside that folder. The next commands (fleet init define, fleet init ct) default to looking for study_config.yaml in the current working directory. Pass --config <root>/study_config.yaml explicitly, or cd into the root first.

docs.title: fleet init define
docs.text:
Generate define.yaml files pre-populated with standard variables from the CDISC Library IG. Reads domains/datasets from study_config.yaml.

fleet init define                              # both SDTM + ADaM (default)
fleet init define --sdtm-only                  # SDTM only
fleet init define --adam-only                  # ADaM only
fleet init define --config path/to/config.yaml # custom config location
Option Default Description --config / -c study_config.yaml Path to config file --sdtm-only (off) Generate SDTM define only --adam-only (off) Generate ADaM define only --force (off) Overwrite existing define.yaml files

The generated YAML includes variable names, labels, types, mandatory flags, CDISC core designations (Req, Exp, Perm, Conditionally Required), codelist references, and origin hints — all sourced from the CDISC Library. The core field enables graduated check severity (see DatasetChecker below). Variables are created without derivation blocks (carry-through columns); add derivation blocks to drive the pipeline.

docs.title: fleet init ct
docs.text:
Generate codelists.py from the codelist references in the define.yaml files. Reads all define specs and downloads the referenced codelists from the CDISC Library.

fleet init ct                                # reads config + both defines
fleet init ct --config path/to/config.yaml   # custom config location
fleet init ct --no-docs                      # lightweight file
fleet init ct --force                        # overwrite existing codelists.py
Option Default Description --config / -c study_config.yaml Path to config file --no-docs (off) Omit definitions and preferred terms --force (off) Overwrite existing codelists.py

docs.title: Standalone Commands
docs.text: These commands work independently of the bootstrapping pipeline.

docs.title: fleet init-ct
docs.text:
Bootstrap a codelists.py from the CDISC Library SDTM Implementation Guide.

This is a one-time operation when setting up a new study. It queries the SDTM IG to discover every codelist referenced by variables in the requested domains, then downloads the term definitions and generates a typed Python module.

fleet init-ct --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --output specs/my_study/sdtm/codelists.py

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Default Description --domains (required) Comma-separated SDTM domain abbreviations (e.g. DM,AE,VS,EX,LB) --output / -o codelists.py Output file path --ig 3-4 SDTM IG version --package sdtmct-2023-12-15 CT package version to download terms from --no-docs (off) Omit definitions and preferred terms (smaller file)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Standard bootstrap for a typical study
fleet init-ct --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --output examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/codelists.py

# Pin to a specific CT version
fleet init-ct --domains DM,AE --ig 3-4 --package sdtmct-2025-09-26 --output codelists.py

# Generate a lightweight file without definitions
fleet init-ct --domains DM --no-docs --output codelists.py

docs.title: fleet add-ct
docs.text:
Add domains to an existing codelists.py without losing previously generated codelists.

This command reads the existing file, detects which concept IDs are already present, discovers the new codelists required by the requested domains, and regenerates the file with the merged set.

fleet add-ct --domains LB,CM --output specs/my_study/sdtm/codelists.py

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Same as init-ct. The --output path must point to an existing codelists.py (or a new file — in which case it behaves like init-ct).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Add lab and conmed domains to an existing file
fleet add-ct --domains LB,CM --output examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/codelists.py

# If all codelists are already present, the command reports "Nothing to add"
fleet add-ct --domains DM --output examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/codelists.py

docs.title: Typical output
