docs.title: fleet add-rule
docs.text:
Scaffold a new custom validation rule YAML skeleton.

Generates a schema-valid CDISC rule file with all required sections pre-filled. Only the Check: block needs to be edited with your validation logic.

# Minimal — auto-increments ID (FLEET-AE-001, FLEET-AE-002, …)
fleet add-rule --domain AE --description "AESEV must be populated when AESER = Y"

# Custom company prefix
fleet add-rule --domain AE --prefix ROCHE --description "Severity check"

# Explicit rule ID (skips auto-increment)
fleet add-rule --domain VS --id ROCHE-VS-010 --description "VSORRES range check"

# Write to a specific directory (overrides study_config)
fleet add-rule --domain DM --description "RFICDTC check" --output ./my_rules/

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Default Description --domain (required) SDTM/ADaM domain code (e.g. AE, DM, VS) --description (required) Human-readable rule description (used in Outcome) --prefix FLEET Rule ID prefix (e.g. your company name) --id (auto) Explicit rule ID; skips auto-increment --output / -o validation.custom_rules from study_config.yaml Output directory

The auto-increment scans all existing .yaml files in the target directory and picks the next available sequence number for the given prefix/domain combination. A uniqueness check prevents overwriting an existing rule.

docs.title: Generated file header
docs.text:
Each scaffolded file includes a header comment with:

  • A link to the CDISC Rules Engine wiki for operator reference
  • A quick reference of rule types (Record, Value-level, Cross-dataset)
  • The exact fleet check-rule command to validate the file
  • The .validate("DOMAIN", custom_rules="<dir>") pipeline usage

docs.title: fleet check-rule
docs.text:
Validate a custom rule YAML file before running it against datasets.

Performs three levels of checking:

  1. YAML syntax — can the file be parsed? Reports line/column on error.
  2. Structure — required top-level keys, Core.Id, Check combinator, non-empty Scope.Domains.
  3. JSON Schema — full validation against the vendored CDISC rule schema.
fleet check-rule metadata/custom_rules/FLEET-AE-001.yaml

docs.title: Example output (passing)
docs.text:
Checking rule: metadata/custom_rules/FLEET-AE-001.yaml
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Rule ID:   FLEET-AE-001
  Type:      Record Data
  Domains:   AE

  ✓ YAML syntax OK
  ✓ Structure OK
  ✓ Schema validation PASSED

docs.title: Example output (failing)
docs.text:
✗ Missing required top-level keys: Core, Rule Type, Scope
  ✗ Core.Id is missing or empty
  ✗ Schema: (root): 'Authorities' is a required property
  ✗ Schema: (root): 'Outcome' is a required property

  4 error(s) found.

Exits with code 1 if any errors are found — suitable for use as a CI gate.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
The recommended bootstrapping workflow for a new study:

graph TD
    A[New study] --> B["fleet init cfg --study-id ... --domains DM,AE,VS,EX"]
    B --> C["fleet init define"]
    C --> D["fleet init ct"]
    D --> E["Edit define.yaml — add derivation blocks"]
    E --> F["Write pipelines with from codelists import SEX, RACE"]
    F --> G{Need more domains?}
    G -->|Yes| H["fleet add-ct --domains LB,CM"]
    H --> F
    G -->|No| I["fleet define-xml --spec define.yaml --output define.xml"]

docs.title: Source of truth
docs.text: The source of truth for which variables and codelists to generate is the CDISC Library IG model. The init define command queries the IG endpoints and extracts variable metadata (name, label, type, core, codelist) from each domain. The init ct command then reads the generated define.yaml to download the exact codelists referenced.

docs.title: fleet add-rule
docs.text:
Scaffold a schema-valid custom validation rule YAML skeleton. Auto-increments the rule ID by scanning the target directory; the programmer only needs to fill in the Check: block.

# Minimal — writes FLEET-AE-001.yaml to the configured custom_rules directory
fleet add-rule --domain AE --description "AESEV must be populated when AESER = Y"

# Custom prefix
fleet add-rule --domain AE --prefix ROCHE --description "Severity check for serious AEs"

# Explicit rule ID (skips auto-increment)
fleet add-rule --domain AE --id ROCHE-AE-042 --description "Custom range check"

# Write to a specific directory
fleet add-rule --domain VS --description "VSORRES range check" --output ./my_rules/
Option Default Description --domain (required) SDTM/ADaM domain code (e.g. AE, DM, VS) --description (required) Human-readable rule description --prefix FLEET Rule ID prefix (e.g. ROCHE → ROCHE-AE-001) --id (auto-increment) Explicit rule ID override --output / -o validation.custom_rules from study_config.yaml Output directory

The generated YAML includes all required CDISC schema sections. The Check: block contains a placeholder with a # TODO comment and a link to the CDISC Rules Engine operator reference.

docs.title: fleet check-rule
docs.text:
Validate a custom rule YAML on the fly — before running the engine against real data.

fleet check-rule my_rules/FLEET-AE-001.yaml

Performs three validation levels:

  1. YAML syntax — reports exact line and column for parse errors
  2. Structure — checks required top-level keys, Core.Id, combinators in Check:, non-empty Scope.Domains
  3. JSON Schema — full validation against the vendored CDISC rule schema

Exits 0 on success, 1 on any error — scriptable in CI pipelines.

Checking rule: my_rules/FLEET-AE-001.yaml
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Rule ID:   FLEET-AE-001
  Type:      Record Data
  Domains:   AE

  ✓ YAML syntax OK
  ✓ Structure OK
  ✓ Schema validation PASSED
Option Description rule_file Path to the rule YAML to check

Generate a CDISC Define-XML 2.1 document from a define.yaml specification.

fleet define-xml --spec examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/define.yaml --output outputs/define_sdtm.xml

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Default Description --spec / -s (required) Path to the define.yaml specification file --output / -o (required) Output path for the Define-XML file --no-preview (off) Skip generating the HTML preview alongside the XML

By default, an HTML preview is generated alongside the XML (e.g. define_sdtm.xml → define_sdtm_preview.html) using the CDISC define2-1.xsl stylesheet. Place define2-1.xsl in the same directory as the output XML, or the preview step will be skipped with a warning.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Generate SDTM Define-XML with HTML preview
fleet define-xml --spec examples/cdiscpilot01/sdtm/define.yaml --output outputs/define_sdtm.xml

# Generate ADaM Define-XML without preview
fleet define-xml --spec examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/define.yaml --output outputs/define_adam.xml --no-preview

docs.title: 1. SDTM domain from raw data
docs.text:
import fleet
import polars as pl
from codelists import SEX  # generated by: fleet init ct

raw = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "patient_id": ["001", "002", "003"],
        "sex_raw": ["M", "F", "M"],
        "birth_date": ["1970-04-15", "1985-11-02", "1960-07-30"],
    }
)

dm = (
    raw.sdtm.hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .hardcode_no_ct("STUDYID", value="MYSTUDY01")
    .assign_no_ct("USUBJID", source="patient_id")
    .assign_ct("SEX", source="sex_raw", ct_codelist=SEX, ct_mapping={"M": "M", "F": "F"})
    .assign_dtc("BRTHDTC", source="birth_date")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.text:
vs_sdtm = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "USUBJID": ["001-01", "001-01", "001-01"],
        "VISITNUM": [1, 2, 3],
        "PARAMCD": ["SYSBP", "SYSBP", "SYSBP"],
        "AVAL": [120.0, 115.0, 118.0],
        "ADT": ["2024-01-10", "2024-02-10", "2024-03-10"],
        "TRTSDT": ["2024-01-10", "2024-01-10", "2024-01-10"],
    }
)

advs = (
    vs_sdtm.adam.source("USUBJID")
    .source("PARAMCD")
    .source("AVAL")
    .study_day("ADY", analysis_date="ADT", reference_date="TRTSDT")
    .flag("ABLFL", criteria='pl.col("VISITNUM") == 1', groups=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL")

)

docs.title: 4. define.yaml-driven pipeline
docs.text:
Fleet can read a define.yaml specification and execute the whole pipeline without hand-writing verbs:

from fleet import load_study_context

ctx = load_study_context("examples/cdiscpilot01/adam/define.yaml")
adsl = ctx.build("ADSL")  # reads inputs, applies derivations, validates output

See How define.yaml works for the full spec format.

gen.write("outputs/cdiscpilot01/define_adam.xml")

docs.title: Step 1: Bootstrap Controlled Terminology
docs.text:
Before writing SDTM pipelines, generate your study's controlled terminology constants from the CDISC Library. This requires a CDISC API key in a .env file at your project root:

.env
CDISC_API_KEY=your-key-here

Then bootstrap the codelists for your study's domains:

fleet init-ct --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --output codelists.py

This queries the SDTM Implementation Guide to discover every codelist referenced by variables in those domains, downloads the term definitions from the CDISC Library, and generates a typed Python module with IDE auto-completion.

docs.title: Step 2: Write your pipeline
docs.text:
import fleet
import polars as pl
from codelists import SEX  # generated in Step 1

raw = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "patient_id": ["001", "002", "003"],
        "sex_raw": ["M", "F", "M"],
        "birth_date": ["1970-04-15", "1985-11-02", "1960-07-30"],
    }
)

dm = (
    raw.sdtm.hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    .hardcode_no_ct("STUDYID", value="MYSTUDY01")
    .assign_no_ct("USUBJID", source="patient_id")
    .assign_ct("SEX", source="sex_raw", ct_codelist=SEX)
    .assign_dtc("BRTHDTC", source="birth_date")
    .to_frame()
)
print(dm)

assign_ct accepts the generated codelist class directly — no need to look up NCI concept IDs. When ct_mapping is omitted (as above), raw values are passed through and validated against the codelist. Add ct_mapping={"1": "M", "2": "F"} if your raw data needs recoding.

docs.title: Your first ADaM BDS dataset
docs.text:
vs_sdtm = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "USUBJID": ["001-01", "001-01", "001-01"],
        "VISITNUM": [1, 2, 3],
        "VSTESTCD": ["SYSBP", "SYSBP", "SYSBP"],
        "VSSTRESN": [120.0, 115.0, 118.0],
        "VSDTC": ["2024-01-10", "2024-02-10", "2024-03-10"],
        "TRTSDT": ["2024-01-10", "2024-01-10", "2024-01-10"],
    }
)

advs = (
    vs_sdtm.adam.source("USUBJID")
    .source("PARAMCD", from_col="VSTESTCD")
    .source("AVAL", from_col="VSSTRESN")
    .derive_dt("ADT", source="VSDTC")
    .study_day("ADY", analysis_date="ADT", reference_date="TRTSDT")
    .flag("ABLFL", criteria='pl.col("VISITNUM") == 1', groups=["USUBJID", "PARAMCD"])
    .baseline("BASE", aval="AVAL", baseline_flag="ABLFL")
    .chg("CHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .pchg("PCHG", aval="AVAL", base="BASE")
    .to_frame()
)

docs.text:
adsl = (
    dm_sdtm.adam.adsl.source("USUBJID")
    .source("AGE")
    .source("SEX")
    .first_date("TRTSDT", from_dataset=ex_sdtm, date_col="EXSTDTC", where='pl.col("EXDOSE") > 0')
    .last_date("TRTEDT", from_dataset=ex_sdtm, date_col="EXENDTC", where='pl.col("EXDOSE") > 0')
    .duration("TRTDURD", start_date="TRTSDT", end_date="TRTEDT")
    .flag("SAFFL", criteria='pl.col("TRTSDT").is_not_null()')
    .count_events("NUMAE", from_dataset=ae_sdtm)
    .to_frame()
)

Fleet also provides Admiral-parity verbs for advanced BDS derivations — bsa(), map(), qtc(), derive_summary_records(), derive_locf_records(), and derive_param() — as well as ADSL helpers age_years() and derive_period(). See the Cheat Sheet for the full list.

docs.title: Initialising a new study workspace
docs.text:
The bootstrapping pipeline is the recommended way to set up a new study. It creates the folder tree, queries the CDISC Library IG to generate define.yaml specs, and downloads the referenced codelists:

# Step 1 — create study_config.yaml + directory structure
fleet init cfg --study-id MYSTUDY01 --company "Acme Pharma" \
  --domains DM,AE,VS,EX --adam-datasets ADSL,ADVS --root ./studies/MYSTUDY01

# Step 2 — generate define.yaml from the CDISC Library IG
fleet init define

# Step 3 — generate codelists.py from define.yaml codelist references
fleet init ct

See the CLI Reference for full argument details and standalone commands like fleet init-ct and fleet add-ct.

The same first step can be done programmatically with StudyContext.init():

from fleet import StudyContext, SDTMConfig, ADAMConfig

ctx = StudyContext.init(
    "./studies/MYSTUDY01",
    study_id="MYSTUDY01",
    company="Acme Pharma",
    sdtm=SDTMConfig(ig_version="3-4", domains=["DM", "AE", "VS", "EX"]),
    adam=ADAMConfig(ig_version="1-1", datasets=["ADSL", "ADVS"]),
)

This creates:

studies/MYSTUDY01/
  study_config.yaml        ← load later with load_study_context()
  data/
    raw/
    sdtm/
    adam/
  metadata/
    sdtm/                  ← define.yaml created by `fleet init define`
    adam/                   ← define.yaml created by `fleet init define`
  outputs/

If study_config.yaml already exists, StudyContext.init() raises a StudyConfigError without touching anything — protecting in-progress work.

To reload an existing workspace in subsequent sessions:

from pathlib import Path
from fleet import load_study_context

ctx = load_study_context(Path("./studies/MYSTUDY01/study_config.yaml"))

docs.title: Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text: When building SDTM or ADaM pipelines in Fleet, you may encounter errors either from data mismatches or pipeline syntax. This guide will help you understand common errors and debug effectively.

docs.title: CTError: Invalid value for codelist...
docs.text:
What it means: A value in your source data does not match the expected Controlled Terminology mappings for a variable derived using .assign_ct().

How to fix it:

  1. Check the raw values using Polars: df.select("raw_column").unique().
  2. Compare those values to the mapping dictionary provided in .assign_ct(ct_mapping={...}).
  3. Add the missing key -> value pair, or fix upstream data collection errors.

docs.title: ColumnNotFoundError from Polars
docs.text:
What it means: You are attempting to derive a variable that depends on a column not yet present in the pipeline (e.g. asking for AVAL before it has been sourced or derived).

How to fix it: Order matters in a Fleet pipeline! Make sure that a dependency variable is derived before subsequent verbs that rely on it. For example, .source("AVAL") must appear before .baseline(aval="AVAL", ...)

docs.title: ValueError: Unknown algorithm in define.yaml
docs.text:
What it means: In a spec-driven pipeline, your define.yaml uses an algorithm name under a derivation block that doesn't match any recognised namespace verbs.

How to fix it: Check your spelling against the supported lists of verbs in the Namespace Pipeline or the API Reference. The JSON Schema (define_spec_schema.json) enforces a strict enum of valid algorithm names — if you include the # yaml-language-server: $schema=... directive at the top of your YAML file, your editor will flag invalid algorithms and empty derivation: {} blocks before you even run the pipeline.

docs.title: Debugging Lazy Evaluation
docs.text:
Because Fleet builds pipelines conceptually and executes them lazily via Polars, a python stack trace might sometimes point to .to_frame() rather than the specific verb that caused an issue.

To inspect what expressions have been queued up before running:

pipeline = dm.sdtm.hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN", "DM").assign_no_ct("USUBJID", "patient_id")

# Inspect the underlying Polars Expressions
print(pipeline._exprs)

You can also comment out .to_frame() and print intermediate outputs to verify your structure step-by-step.

# To debug an intermediate state, truncate the pipeline:
debug_df = (
    dm.sdtm.hardcode_no_ct("DOMAIN", value="DM")
    # .assign_ct("SEX", source="sex_raw", ...)  <-- Commented out to isolate the bug
    .to_frame()
)
print(debug_df.head())

docs.title: Validating define.yaml
docs.text:
If you are using the spec-driven approach, validate your define.yaml file against the Fleet schema before running pipelines. This ensures you don't waste time tracing runtime errors that are actually typos in the specification.

If you have configured the schema comment in your YAML file:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../../src/fleet/define_xml/schemas/define_spec_schema.json

Your editor (like VS Code) should highlight structural or naming errors automatically.
